### Steps
The advisor reviews the student's record. Advice is given on module selection or study skills. The advice is recorded in an Academic Advice Record. A follow-up meeting is scheduled if needed. If specialist support is required, a referral is made.

### Produces
Academic Advice Record. Support Referral.

### Outcome
Students receive personalised guidance to support academic progress.

### Fails when
The advisor lacks the Student Enrolment record and cannot provide accurate advice.

Name: Academic Policy & Regulation Mgt
Documentation:
### Identity
The work of drafting, approving, versioning and communicating the Academic Policies and Academic Regulations that govern admission, teaching, assessment and awards.

### Trigger
Arrival of a new Government Policy document or an internal proposal to amend existing rules.

### Consumes
Government Policy document supplies external compliance requirements. Academic Policy Proposal supplies the identified gap or improvement. Consultation Feedback supplies the views of academic boards and student representatives.

### Steps
First, a policy drafter compares existing Academic Policies against new requirements and drafts a revised Academic Policy Proposal. The proposal is circulated for Consultation Feedback from committees. Then consolidated feedback is incorporated and the draft is submitted to the Academic Board for Approval Decision. If the Approval Decision is refused, the process returns the proposal with required changes and the cycle repeats. Upon approval, the new Academic Policy or Academic Regulation is assigned a version number and publication date. The published version is distributed to all faculties. Each existing policy is reviewed on a scheduled cycle and flagged for revision if it no longer meets regulatory conditions.

### Produces
Academic Policy establishes the binding rule set. Academic Regulation establishes the operational rule set. Policy Publication Notice notifies affected areas of the change.

### Outcome
Academic Policies and Academic Regulations are current, version-controlled and aligned with external requirements.

### Fails when
A required change is blocked by conflicting consultation feedback and no Approval Decision is reached, leaving outdated rules in force.

Name: Academic Skills Development
Documentation:
### Identity
The work of delivering workshops and resources to improve academic skills.

### Trigger
A scheduled skills workshop or a student self-referral.

### Consumes
Skills Workshop Schedule supplies the dates. Student Enrolment supplies participants. Academic Skills Materials supplies the content. Needs Assessment supplies the identified gaps.

### Steps
The workshop is delivered. Attendance is recorded. The student's skill development is logged. Follow-up support is offered. An evaluation form is completed. The workshop material is updated based on feedback.

### Produces
Skills Attendance Record. Academic Skills Log. Workshop Evaluation Summary.

### Outcome
Students have improved academic skills as evidenced by attendance and participation.

### Fails when
No students enrol for the workshop and it is cancelled.

Name: Academic Year Scheduling
Documentation:
### Identity
The work of defining term dates, assessment windows and graduation ceremony dates for the academic year.

### Trigger
The start of the planning cycle for the next academic year, signalled by the end of the current one.

### Consumes
Academic Calendar from prior year supplies the baseline dates. Teaching Schedule constraints from faculties supply room and staff availability. Public Holiday Calendar supplies closed days. Programme Delivery Requirements supply the minimum teaching weeks per level.

### Steps
The scheduler drafts term dates and weeks of instruction. The draft is checked against the Public Holiday Calendar and major events. Faculties confirm availability of teaching weeks and examination periods. Conflicts are resolved through negotiation with faculty administrators. The final Academic Calendar is approved by the Academic Registrar. Any changes after publication go through a change request that documents the impact. The published Academic Calendar is distributed to all academic areas.

### Produces
Academic Calendar with term dates, assessment weeks and ceremony dates. Teaching Week Allocation with assigned teaching weeks per faculty. Change Request Log recording any post-publication amendments.

### Outcome
The institution has a single authoritative Academic Calendar for the year that all other scheduling consumes.

### Fails when
Faculty constraints conflict beyond resolution and the Academic Calendar cannot be approved, leaving no agreed teaching weeks.

Name: Accommodation Allocation
Documentation:
### Identity
Allocation work that assigns students to available rooms under accommodation policy. It matches preferences against room inventory, manages offers and declines, and maintains a waiting list.

### Trigger
The arrival of a confirmed Student Enrolment for a student who has submitted an Accommodation Application.

### Consumes
Accommodation Application supplies the student's room preferences, lifestyle requirements, and medical or accessibility needs. Room Inventory supplies available rooms, their attributes, and their live occupancy state. Accommodation Contract Template supplies the terms that must accompany any offer.

### Steps
The process validates the student's eligibility and accommodation guarantee status. It matches preferences against available rooms, giving priority to medical and accessibility needs. It selects the best-fit room or identifies a shortage. It issues an Accommodation Offer with the contract terms and a response deadline. If the student declines or the offer lapses, the room is released and the next waiting list candidate is considered. If no suitable room exists, the student is added to the Waiting List with a priority score. When an offer is accepted, the room is marked as allocated and the student's account is updated.

### Produces
Accommodation Offer sets the proposed room, fee, and contract terms for the student's acceptance. Room Assignment Record marks a specific room as allocated to a specific student. Waiting List records the unresolvable demand and its ordering.

### Outcome
Each eligible student is assigned a room or is placed on an ordered waiting list, and room inventory reflects live commitments.

### Fails when
Room Inventory holds no available rooms or the student's accessibility needs cannot be met by any current vacancy, causing the student to be left without an offer and the allocation to halt.

Name: Accommodation Departure & Turnaround Mgt
Documentation:
### Identity
Turnaround work that returns accommodation rooms to lettable condition after a departure. It coordinates inspection, cleaning, maintenance, and reallocation readiness.

### Trigger
The arrival of a Student Departure Notice that confirms a resident has vacated.

### Consumes
Student Departure Notice supplies the vacated room identity and the departure date. Room Condition Report supplies damage and inventory findings from the outgoing inspection. Cleaning Schedule supplies the sequence and standard required for each room type.

### Steps
The process records the vacant room and triggers an outgoing inspection. It compares the Room Condition Report against the prior check-in record to identify damage beyond fair wear. It assigns a cleaning work order and any repair tasks to the appropriate teams. It verifies that cleaning and repairs are complete against the required standard. It updates the room status to ready for allocation. If damage charges are due, it raises a Student Charge Note and applies the deposit terms. The room is then released to Room Inventory.

### Produces
Room Condition Report records the post-departure state and any damage liability. Facilities Work Order states the required cleaning and repair tasks for that room. Student Charge Note states the amount owed by the departing student for damages.

### Outcome
Each vacated room is restored, assessed, and made available for the next allocation or held for maintenance.

### Fails when
Inspection findings are disputed or cleaning work orders are not completed, causing the room to remain unavailable and the next allocation to fail.

Name: Accommodation Facilities Mgt
Documentation:
### Identity
Ongoing maintenance and upkeep of accommodation buildings, common areas, and room fittings. It manages reported faults and planned servicing.

### Trigger
The arrival of a Facilities Work Order or a student-reported fault notification for accommodation premises.

### Consumes
Facilities Work Order supplies the defect detail, location, and priority. Student Fault Notification supplies user-reported symptoms and access constraints. Maintenance Schedule supplies the planned servicing intervals for accommodation assets.

### Steps
The process triages the incoming work order or fault notification by urgency and health and safety impact. It assigns a maintenance operative and schedules access. The operative repairs or services the asset and records the action. A supervisor checks the work against the required standard. If the fault is not resolved, the work order is re-opened with a revised approach. Completion is confirmed and the student or reporting source is informed. Recurring faults are logged against the room or building for trend review.

### Produces
Completed Work Order records the repair action taken and the closure time. Asset Service Record updates the maintenance history for the affected asset. Student Fault Response informs the reporter of the resolution.

### Outcome
Accommodation assets and fittings are maintained to the required condition, and reported faults are closed or escalated.

### Fails when
Maintenance operative availability or spare parts are lacking, causing safety-critical faults to remain open and accommodation areas to become unusable.

Name: Accommodation Incident & Emergency Response
Documentation:
### Identity
Emergency response work that handles incidents in accommodation, including fire, flood, security, and welfare crises, and restores safe operation.

### Trigger
The arrival of an Incident Report from accommodation staff, a student, or an alarm system.

### Consumes
Incident Report supplies the nature, location, and people affected by the incident. Emergency Contact List supplies the responsible responders and external services. Accommodation Policy supplies the safety and conduct rules that govern the response.

### Steps
The process classifies the incident as safety, security, or welfare. It triggers the relevant emergency response, such as evacuation, first aid, or security attendance. It contains the immediate harm and preserves evidence. It notifies the identified emergency contacts and external services where required. It records actions taken and collects witness statements. It arranges for affected students to be relocated or supported. A post-incident review identifies corrective actions and assigns them to the responsible teams. The incident is closed only when corrective actions have an owner and a due date.

### Produces
Incident Report Record captures the full incident timeline, actions, and evidence. Corrective Action Request states the follow-up work required to prevent recurrence. Student Support Referral directs affected students to welfare services.

### Outcome
Accommodation incidents are responded to, contained, and converted into owned corrective actions, with affected residents supported.

### Fails when
Emergency contacts cannot be reached or the incident escalates beyond available on-site response, causing harm to residents and regulatory breach.

Name: Alumni Event & Campaign Mgt
Documentation:
### Identity
The work of planning and executing alumni events and fundraising campaigns.

### Trigger
Approval of an Alumni Event Plan for a specific event or campaign.

### Consumes
Alumni Contact Record supplies the invitation list. Event Venue Booking supplies the location and date. Campaign Budget supplies the financial limit. Event Registration List supplies confirmed attendees.

### Steps
The planner defines the event purpose and audience. Invitations are issued from the Alumni Contact Record. Registrations are collected and attendance is confirmed. The budget is checked against the Campaign Budget before expenditure. The event is delivered and attendance is recorded. For campaigns, pledges are tracked and collected. After the event, a post-event feedback survey is distributed. The survey responses are used to produce the Alumni Event Report.

### Produces
Alumni Event Report recording attendance and outcomes. Campaign Performance Summary recording funds raised. Post-Event Feedback Summary recording attendee satisfaction.

### Outcome
Alumni are engaged through delivered events and campaigns, with recorded participation and contributions.

### Fails when
Fewer than the planned minimum attendance is achieved and the Campaign Budget is not covered, stopping the planned engagement activity.

Name: Alumni Relationship Mgt
Documentation:
### Identity
The work of maintaining contact details and engagement history for alumni.

### Trigger
A change in alumni contact details or a new interaction is recorded.

### Consumes
Alumni Contact Record supplies the current details. Interaction Record supplies the history of engagement. Updated Contact Details supplies the new information. Communication Preference supplies the preferred contact method.

### Steps
The change is validated against the existing record. The Alumni Contact Record is updated with the new details. Engagement history is appended with the interaction. Preferences for communication are checked and applied. A data protection check confirms the update is lawful. The record is saved. A confirmation is sent to the alumni if the change was self-submitted.

### Produces
Updated Alumni Contact Record. Alumni Engagement Summary reflecting recent interactions. Data Protection Confirmation recording lawful processing.

### Outcome
Alumni records are current and complete, enabling targeted engagement.

### Fails when
Contact details are invalid or the record cannot be updated, leaving alumni unreachable.

Name: Application Lifecycle Mgt
Documentation:
### Identity
Management of the software application lifecycle, from need through development, deployment, and retirement.

### Trigger
The arrival of a business requirement for a new or changed application.

### Consumes
Business Requirement Document supplies the functional and non-functional needs. Current Application Portfolio supplies the existing applications and their status. Change Request supplies a request for modification to an existing application.

### Steps
The process analyses the requirement against current portfolio. It decides build, buy, or modify. It develops or configures the application. It tests against acceptance criteria. It deploys to production. It provides documentation and training. It maintains and updates the application. It retires applications at end of life. If a change fails in testing, it is returned for rework.

### Produces
Application Change Record states what was delivered and when. Test Report records the testing results and defects. Application Retirement Notice states the decommissioning plan.

### Outcome
The application portfolio meets business needs and is current, supported, and secure.

### Fails when
A critical application change fails in production, causing service outage and business disruption.

Name: Art/Museum Collection Mgt
Documentation:
### Identity
Management of the institution's art and museum collections, including acquisition, cataloguing, conservation, and display.

### Trigger
The arrival of a new acquisition offer or a conservation need.

### Consumes
Collection Acquisition Proposal supplies the item details and provenance. Collection Catalogue Record supplies the existing holdings. Conservation Assessment supplies the condition and treatment needs.

### Steps
The process evaluates the acquisition against collection policy. It obtains expert valuation and provenance checks. It acquires the item. It catalogues it. It manages conservation treatments. It plans and delivers displays or loans. It monitors environmental conditions for stored items. It reviews the collection periodically. If an item is deaccessioned, it follows disposal policy.

### Produces
Collection Item Catalogue Entry states the new item details. Conservation Treatment Record states the treatment applied. Display Plan states the items and schedule.

### Outcome
The institution's art and museum holdings are preserved, documented, and used for public benefit.

### Fails when
An item's provenance is not verified, causing acquisition of stolen or fake art and reputational damage.

Name: Assessment Administration
Documentation:
### Identity
The work of preparing and scheduling assessments for modules.

### Trigger
A term starts and module cohorts are established.

### Consumes
Module Registration supplies the students to be assessed. Academic Calendar supplies the assessment windows. Assessment Policy supplies the rules for format and invigilation. Room Inventory supplies the available rooms.

### Steps
The administrator determines the assessment format for each module based on Assessment Policy. Assessment Papers are produced or sourced. Assessment Schedules are defined, assigning dates and rooms. Invigilators are allocated. The schedule is published to students. Adjustments for students with approved exceptional circumstances are applied. The final papers are securely stored.

### Produces
Assessment Paper. Assessment Schedule. Invigilation Allocation.

### Outcome
All modules have scheduled, policy-compliant assessments ready for delivery.

### Fails when
Assessment Papers are not ready by the scheduling deadline, causing assessment windows to be missed.

Name: Assessment Delivery
Documentation:
### Identity
The work of running the actual assessment event, including examinations and coursework collection.

### Trigger
The Assessment Schedule date for a module arrives.

### Consumes
Assessment Paper supplies the questions. Assessment Schedule supplies the time and room. Module Registration supplies the candidate list. Invigilation Allocation supplies the invigilators.

### Steps
The room is prepared and candidates are checked against the Module Registration. Assessment Papers are distributed. The assessment is conducted under invigilation. At the end, papers are collected and counted. A Candidate Attendance Record is completed. For coursework, submission is received and logged. Completed Assessments are handed to marking.

### Produces
Completed Assessment. Candidate Attendance Record.

### Outcome
Assessments are delivered securely and all submissions are accounted for.

### Fails when
A student attends but is not on the Module Registration, causing a mismatch that must be resolved before marking.

Name: Assessment Marking and Feedback
Documentation:
### Identity
The work of marking completed assessments and providing feedback to students.

### Trigger
Completed Assessments are handed to markers.

### Consumes
Completed Assessment supplies the student's work. Marking Scheme supplies the criteria and marks. Academic Policy supplies moderation rules. Moderation Sample supplies the subset for checking.

### Steps
Each marker applies the Marking Scheme to produce a Student Assessment Mark and Feedback Record. Marks are recorded in a marking spreadsheet. A sample of marking is moderated by a second marker to check consistency. If moderation reveals variance, the marker is asked to remark. The final marks and Feedback Records are approved by the module leader. Marks are returned to students along with feedback.

### Produces
Student Assessment Mark. Feedback Record. Moderation Record.

### Outcome
Every assessment has a verified mark and actionable feedback.

### Fails when
Moderation reveals systematic marking errors and no agreed adjustment is reached, leaving marks contested.

Name: Asset Mgt
Documentation:
### Identity
Accounting and control of capital and non-capital assets, including their acquisition, depreciation, and disposal.

### Trigger
The arrival of an asset purchase invoice or a scheduled depreciation run.

### Consumes
Asset Purchase Invoice supplies the asset cost, description, and acquisition date. Asset Register supplies the existing asset records and depreciation status. Depreciation Policy supplies the useful lives and methods for each asset class.

### Steps
The process validates the asset purchase invoice against the asset register. It capitalises assets that meet the capitalisation threshold. It assigns a depreciation method and useful life. It runs periodic depreciation calculations. It reviews asset useful lives and impairment. It records asset disposals and transfers. It reconciles the asset register to the general ledger. If an asset is disposed of, the gain or loss is calculated and posted.

### Produces
Asset Register Update records new, changed, or disposed assets. Depreciation Journal supplies the calculated depreciation for the period. Asset Disposal Record states the disposal date and sale proceeds.

### Outcome
The institution's asset base is accurately recorded, valued, and depreciated in line with policy.

### Fails when
An asset is not recorded or is incorrectly depreciated, causing financial statements to be materially misstated.

Name: Benefactor Mgt
Documentation:
### Identity
The work of managing relationships with individuals who make major gifts.

### Trigger
A Benefactor Contact Record indicates a potential donation.

### Consumes
Benefactor Contact Record supplies the donor's history. Donation Pledge supplies the intended gift amount and purpose. Gift Agreement supplies the terms. Funding Priority List supplies the institutional needs.

### Steps
The benefactor's interests are matched to the Funding Priority List. The Donation Pledge is documented. The Gift Agreement is drafted and signed. A stewardship plan is created to maintain the relationship. The pledge is tracked until payment. A receipt is issued. The benefactor is invited to recognition events. The engagement is recorded.

### Produces
Signed Gift Agreement. Donation Receipt. Benefactor Engagement Record. Stewardship Plan.

### Outcome
Benefactor relationships are formalised and gifts are recorded against agreed purposes.

### Fails when
The benefactor withdraws the pledge before signing, leaving no gift recorded.

Name: Benefits Mgt
Documentation:
### Identity
This process tracks the realisation of benefits from approved change initiatives and enforces the discipline that expected benefits are measured after delivery. It is the part of the capability that connects investment decisions to measurable outcomes.

### Trigger
The approval of a Business Case with quantified expected benefits starts the process, at which point the change has committed investment but no benefit has yet been recorded.

### Consumes
Business Case supplies the expected benefits, their monetary value, and the planned dates by which each benefit should occur. Project Status Report supplies delivery progress and confirms whether planned outputs have been produced. Benefits Realisation Plan supplies the measurement method and owner for each benefit.

### Steps
First the process registers each expected benefit in a Benefits Register, assigning an owner and baseline measurement. Then it compares actual performance data against the baseline at each planned review point. When a benefit is behind plan, the process records a deviation and requests corrective action from the project sponsor. When a benefit is ahead of plan, it updates the forecast. It reviews benefits after project closure and for a further two years, then marks each benefit as realised, partially realised, or not realised.

### Produces
Benefits Register records the current status of each expected benefit after each review. Benefits Realisation Report states the actual value realised against planned value and explains variances.

### Outcome
Investment decisions are supported by measured evidence of benefits actually delivered, and unfulfilled benefits are visible for governance action.

### Fails when
The Benefits Register has no agreed measurement baseline or benefit owner, because benefits cannot be assessed and the organisation continues to fund change without evidence of return. Downstream, portfolio prioritisation and future business case approvals proceed without benefit reliability.

Name: Brand Mgt
Documentation:
### Identity
Management of the institutional brand, including identity standards, brand assets, and brand compliance.

### Trigger
The arrival of a brand usage request or a brand audit schedule.

### Consumes
Brand Usage Request supplies the intended use and context. Brand Guidelines supply the visual and verbal standards. Brand Asset Library supplies the approved logos and templates.

### Steps
The process reviews the request against guidelines. It issues the appropriate brand asset. It monitors external usage for compliance. It updates the guidelines as needed. It delivers brand training. It handles brand infringements. It audits brand applications periodically. If misuse is found, it issues a correction request.

### Produces
Brand Usage Approval states the permitted use. Brand Asset Issue records the asset provided. Brand Correction Notice states the required change for non-compliant usage.

### Outcome
The institution's brand is used consistently and correctly across all touchpoints.

### Fails when
Unauthorised or incorrect brand usage goes unchallenged, diluting the brand.

Name: Budget Mgt
Documentation:
### Identity
Annual and in-year budget construction, allocation, and monitoring. It sets financial limits and controls spend.

### Trigger
The arrival of a budget construction deadline or a budget revision request.

### Consumes
Budget Submission supplies each unit's planned income and expenditure. Prior Year Actuals supply the historical spend and income baseline. Institutional Financial Plan supplies the overall financial targets and constraints.

### Steps
The process consolidates budget submissions. It challenges and adjusts them against the financial plan. It allocates budgets to cost centres. It loads them into the finance system. It monitors actual spend against budget monthly. Variances are investigated and reforecast. Budget transfers and virements are processed within rules. If a unit exceeds budget, a corrective action is set. The final outturn is reported to governance.

### Produces
Approved Budget states the annual financial limit for each cost centre. Budget Variance Report records the difference between actual and budget. Budget Transfer records the movement of funds between cost centres.

### Outcome
The institution operates within an approved budget, and variances are managed through reallocation.

### Fails when
Budgets are not loaded or are overspent without correction, causing uncontrolled expenditure and financial loss.

Name: Business & Operational Reporting
Documentation:
### Identity
Production of business and operational reports from institutional data for management and statutory use.

### Trigger
The arrival of a reporting schedule date or an ad hoc report request.

### Consumes
Report Specification supplies the required data fields, filters, and format. Source Data Extract supplies the raw data from operational systems. Reporting Standard supplies the presentation rules and definitions.

### Steps
The process validates the report specification. It extracts and transforms the data. It builds the report. It checks for accuracy and completeness. It distributes to authorised recipients. It stores the report in the reporting library. It handles follow-up data questions. If data quality issues arise, they are logged for correction at source.

### Produces
Business Report states the required metrics and analysis. Operational Report states the operational performance data. Report Distribution Confirmation records who received the report.

### Outcome
The institution's management receives accurate and timely reports for decision-making.

### Fails when
Source data is missing or incorrect, causing the report to misstate performance and mislead management.

Name: Business Continuity Mgt
Documentation:
### Identity
This process establishes the institution's ability to continue critical activities during disruption and to recover within agreed timeframes. It is the part of the capability that maintains resilience against operational interruptions.

### Trigger
A material change in risk profile or a disruptive incident triggers the process, when the institution's existing continuity arrangements are known to be insufficient.

### Consumes
Business Impact Analysis supplies the analysis of critical activities, their dependencies, and maximum tolerable downtime. Risk Register supplies the threats and vulnerabilities that could cause disruption. Resource Inventory supplies the staff, facilities, systems, and suppliers available for recovery.

### Steps
First the process reviews the Business Impact Analysis for the critical activities in scope. It selects a continuity strategy for each, such as alternate site, manual workaround, or mutual aid. It then develops the Business Continuity Plan, assigning recovery teams, contact details, and step-by-step procedures. It schedules and conducts a test or exercise of the plan. It records test results and any failures. It updates the plan to address the failures and obtains sign-off from the accountable executive.

### Produces
Business Continuity Plan records the recovery procedures, roles, and invocation criteria for each critical activity. Test Report records the scenario tested, outcomes, and required plan amendments.

### Outcome
The institution has a tested Business Continuity Plan for each critical activity, with recovery time objectives that align to the Business Impact Analysis.

### Fails when
The Business Impact Analysis does not identify maximum tolerable downtime for a critical activity, because recovery priorities cannot be set and the plan cannot be validated against a time objective, leaving the recovery effort uncoordinated.

Name: Business Horizon Scanning
Documentation:
### Identity
This process surveys the external environment for political, economic, social, technological, legal, and environmental changes that could affect the institution's strategy. It is the part of the capability that provides early warning of strategic shifts.

### Trigger
A scheduled scanning cycle or the publication of a major Government Policy Document triggers the process, when the strategy team needs to refresh its assumptions.

### Consumes
Government Policy Document supplies formal regulatory and funding changes. Market Analysis supplies data on student demand, research income, and competitor behaviour. Stakeholder Input supplies observations from staff, students, and employers.

### Steps
First the process collects signals from the named sources. It filters signals for relevance to the institution's mission. It analyses the likely impact and timeframe of each relevant signal. It validates the analysis with subject matter experts. It then produces a Horizon Scan Report and updates the institution's Strategic Assumptions.

### Produces
Horizon Scan Report records the identified trends, their assessed impact, and the evidence base. Strategic Assumptions record the revised assumptions about the external environment used for planning.

### Outcome
The institution has a documented set of Strategic Assumptions based on current external evidence, and material changes are flagged before they appear in internal performance data.

### Fails when
The Market Analysis is not produced or lacks credible sources, because the scan misses shifts in student demand or funding, and the Strategic Plan is built on assumptions that no longer hold.

Name: Campaign Mgt
Documentation:
### Identity
Planning and execution of marketing campaigns, from research through delivery and evaluation.

### Trigger
The arrival of a campaign brief from the marketing plan.

### Consumes
Campaign Brief supplies the objectives, target audience, and message. Audience Data supplies the segmentation and contact rules. Marketing Channel Plan supplies the selected channels.

### Steps
The process develops the campaign strategy. It creates creative assets. It schedules and executes across channels. It monitors responses and engagement. It adjusts mid-campaign if needed. It reports on results. It manages the budget. If the campaign underperforms, it is paused or revised. It records lessons learned.

### Produces
Campaign Plan states the activities and schedule. Campaign Creative Assets supplies the adverts and content. Campaign Performance Report records the metrics and ROI.

### Outcome
The institution achieves its campaign objectives and learns for future campaigns.

### Fails when
The campaign target audience is incorrectly defined, causing wasted spend and no response.

Name: Campus Parking
Documentation:
### Identity
Operational control of car parks, permits, enforcement, and daily vehicle access on campus.

### Trigger
The arrival of a vehicle registration for a car park permit or a parking enforcement event.

### Consumes
Vehicle Registration supplies the vehicle and owner details. Car Park Permit Application supplies the applicant's eligibility and required access. Car Park Capacity Record supplies the number of spaces available per zone.

### Steps
The process verifies the applicant's eligibility for a permit. It checks available capacity in the requested zone. It issues a permit or places the applicant on a waiting list. It records the vehicle against the issued permit. Daily enforcement matches vehicles on site against permit records. A breach triggers a Parking Charge Notice. Appeals are reviewed against the parking terms and either upheld or dismissed. Permit renewals are issued before expiry where capacity allows.

### Produces
Car Park Permit authorises a specific vehicle to use a named zone. Parking Charge Notice states the penalty for an observed breach. Parking Appeal Decision records the outcome of a challenge.

### Outcome
Car park use is controlled through permits and enforcement, and capacity is managed within limits.

### Fails when
Car Park Capacity Record is inaccurate or permits are oversold, causing conflict and unmanaged demand on peak days.

Name: Campus Security
Documentation:
### Identity
Physical security operations across campus, including patrols, access control, incident response, and safeguarding.

### Trigger
The arrival of a Security Incident Report or a scheduled patrol roster activation.

### Consumes
Security Incident Report supplies the event type, location, and persons involved. Access Control Record supplies door and zone entry attempts. Security Patrol Schedule supplies the patrol routes and time intervals.

### Steps
The process assigns patrols according to the schedule and risk areas. It monitors access control records for anomalies. It responds to security incidents and records the response. It escalates serious incidents to emergency services and campus leadership. It secures affected areas and preserves evidence. It logs all actions and outcomes. It reviews incident patterns and adjusts patrol priorities. Completed patrols are signed off.

### Produces
Security Incident Log records each event and the response taken. Patrol Completion Record confirms each planned patrol was executed. Security Risk Assessment updates the risk priority for campus zones.

### Outcome
Campus physical security is maintained through patrolling, access monitoring, and incident handling.

### Fails when
Access control systems fail or patrols are not completed, causing an unmonitored period during which an incident may occur without response.

Name: Career & Employability Engagement Mgt
Documentation:
### Identity
The work of connecting students with career advice and employability opportunities.

### Trigger
A student books a career appointment or attends an employability event.

### Consumes
Student Enrolment supplies the student's programme. Career Opportunity Register supplies vacancies and placements. Employer Engagement Record supplies employer contacts. CV Draft supplies the student's current CV.

### Steps
The appointment is held and advice given. The student is matched to opportunities in the register. Applications to opportunities are tracked. The outcome is recorded. A mock interview is arranged. An employer introduction is made.

### Produces
Career Advisory Record. Employer Introduction. Application Tracking Record.

### Outcome
Students access career support and are introduced to employers.

### Fails when
The Career Opportunity Register is empty and no matches can be made.

Name: Change Portfolio Mgt
Documentation:
### Identity
This process prioritises and sequences change initiatives within the institution's change portfolio and makes explicit the trade-offs between competing investments. It is the part of the capability that ensures the total change load is deliverable.

### Trigger
A new Change Request or Business Case entering the portfolio for consideration starts the process, when the portfolio already has existing approved initiatives consuming resources.

### Consumes
Change Request supplies the scope and urgency of the proposed change. Business Case supplies the expected benefits, cost estimate, and strategic alignment. Resource Capacity Statement supplies the current availability of staff, budget, and key facilities. Strategic Objective supplies the criteria against which alignment is judged.

### Steps
First the process logs the incoming proposal and checks completeness of the Business Case. Then it scores the proposal against the institution's Strategic Objectives and risk appetite. It compares the proposal's resource demand with the Resource Capacity Statement to determine whether capacity exists. If capacity is insufficient, the process either rejects the proposal, defers it, or asks for a revised Business Case with reduced scope. If capacity exists, it ranks the proposal against the existing portfolio. It then issues a portfolio decision and updates the portfolio pipeline.

### Produces
Change Portfolio Decision records the outcome for each proposal: approve, defer, reject, or request revision, with reasons. Change Portfolio Report records the aggregate portfolio composition, resource utilisation, and strategic alignment after the decision.

### Outcome
The approved change portfolio has an explicit resource demand that does not exceed available capacity and a strategic alignment score for every initiative.

### Fails when
The Resource Capacity Statement is missing or outdated, because the process cannot judge whether new proposals can be delivered; as a result, the portfolio becomes overloaded and delivery risk transfers to individual projects without governance detection.

Name: Child Care Mgt
Documentation:
### Identity
Management of on-campus childcare provision, including places, staffing, and regulatory compliance.

### Trigger
The arrival of a childcare place application or a regulatory inspection date.

### Consumes
Childcare Application supplies the child's details and sessions required. Staffing Roster supplies the available qualified staff. Regulatory Standard supplies the legal requirements.

### Steps
The process assesses the application against available places. It allocates a place and starts records. It schedules staffing. It ensures compliance with child-to-staff ratios. It delivers daily care. It manages fees and invoicing. It meets inspection requirements. If a child has additional needs, it coordinates support. It reviews occupancy regularly.

### Produces
Childcare Place Offer states the allocated place and terms. Daily Attendance Record records children present. Regulatory Compliance Report states the outcome of inspections.

### Outcome
Children are cared for safely, and parents have reliable childcare.

### Fails when
Staff sickness causes ratios to fall below legal minimum, forcing temporary closure.

Name: Collaborative Opportunity Mgt
Documentation:
### Identity
Work here identifies and shapes collaborative research opportunities with external partners, moving from initial approach to a jointly agreed plan.

### Trigger
The arrival of a Collaboration Request from an external body or an internal researcher, when the proposed collaborative work is not yet defined.

### Consumes
Collaboration Request supplies the partner's interest, available resources, and intended research area. Research Opportunity supplies the underlying funding or research need that the collaboration would address. Research Capability Profile supplies the institution's contribution and expertise. Research Strategy supplies the institutional stance on partnerships and priority areas.

### Steps
The Collaboration Request is logged and matched against the Research Opportunity to confirm the need. The process then assesses the partner against the Research Capability Profile for complementary strengths. If the partner is not suitable, the request is declined and recorded. If suitable, the process drafts a Collaborative Opportunity Plan outlining the joint objectives, work split, and resource contributions. The plan is discussed with the partner and, if both sides agree, signed as a Collaborative Opportunity Agreement. The agreement is handed to relationship management for ongoing oversight.

### Produces
Collaborative Opportunity Plan: issued when the joint approach is defined, establishing the shared work and objectives. Collaborative Opportunity Agreement: issued when both parties sign, establishing the commitment to proceed jointly.

### Outcome
Viable collaborative opportunities are defined and agreed, ready for formal partnership establishment.

### Fails when
The partner suitability check is bypassed and a Collaborative Opportunity Agreement is signed with a partner lacking required expertise; the joint work fails.

Name: Commercial Activity Exit Mgt
Documentation:
### Identity
This process is controlled closure of a commercial arrangement once a counterparty or internal sponsor has signalled termination. It realises the delivery capability's obligation to end contracts without leaving unresolved liabilities or unreturned assets. It converts a termination notice into a settled, documented closure.

### Trigger
Arrival of an Exit Notice from a counterparty or internal budget holder, with the contract still active and obligations outstanding.

### Consumes
Contract Agreement supplies termination clauses, notice periods, asset return requirements and settlement basis. Exit Notice supplies the stated reason, effective date, and any request for early termination. Outstanding Invoice Register supplies the unpaid amounts and outstanding credits that must be settled.

### Steps
The process first verifies the Exit Notice against the termination clauses in the Contract Agreement to confirm validity and effective date. It then assembles a schedule of all outstanding obligations: invoices, credits, assets, data returns, and confidentiality deeds. Each obligation is assigned to an owner and a due date; any obligation contested by either party is logged as an unresolved item. The process calculates the exit settlement, applying early termination charges and set-offs from the Outstanding Invoice Register. It then obtains internal approval from Finance and the Commercial Delivery owner; if approval is refused, the process returns the settlement to negotiation and reissues the calculation. Once approved, it issues an Exit Settlement Statement to the counterparty and records the agreed final position. After confirmation of settlement and asset return, it closes the Contract Agreement and marks the contract as ended in the Contract Closure Record.

### Produces
Exit Settlement Statement records the final amounts payable or receivable and the effective closure date. Contract Closure Record establishes that all obligations are discharged and the contract is no longer active. Asset Return Schedule records the assets to be returned and their confirmed receipt.

### Outcome
The commercial relationship is closed with every liability settled, every asset returned, and the contract no longer available for new commitments.

### Fails when
Exit Notice is disputed or settlement is not approved before the notice period expires; the contract remains open, the counterparty pursues legal remedies, and Financial Statements cannot close the commitment.

Name: Commercial Activity Issue Mgt
Documentation:
### Identity
This process manages deviations that arise during delivery against a current commercial contract. It establishes ownership, root cause, corrective action and escalation for each reported issue, keeping the delivery obligation intact.

### Trigger
Arrival of an Issue Report from a delivery team, counterparty, or monitoring activity, stating that a contractual obligation is at risk or has been breached.

### Consumes
Issue Report provides the specific deviation, affected obligation, and impact on delivery. Contract Agreement supplies the performance standard and the remedy or escalation clause applicable. Risk Register supplies the existing risk posture and previous decisions that affect the response.

### Steps
On arrival, the process triages the Issue Report for severity, assigning a priority based on contract impact and delivery risk. It then confirms the obligation against the Contract Agreement and gathers evidence from the reporting party. A root cause is established and recorded; where the cause is disputed, the process convenes a review with the contract owner. The process drafts a Resolution Plan naming corrective action, owner, and due date. If the issue affects payment or acceptance, it also issues a Corrective Action Request to the counterparty or internal unit. Progress is tracked in the Issue Log until the corrective action is verified. Unresolved issues escalate to the Commercial Delivery owner at the escalation threshold defined in the Contract Agreement. On verification, the process closes the issue in the Issue Log and releases the holding entry.

### Produces
Resolution Plan specifies corrective action, owner and deadline. Issue Log records the lifecycle of each issue, including escalation and closure. Corrective Action Request formalises the required remedy to the responsible party.

### Outcome
Reported deviations are resolved or formally escalated, with no delivery obligation left unattended.

### Fails when
An Issue Report lacks sufficient detail to identify the breached obligation, or no owner accepts the corrective action; the issue remains open, delivery continues out of compliance, and the contract is breached.

Name: Commercial Activity Output Mgt
Documentation:
### Identity
This process controls the release and acceptance of contracted outputs. It ensures each output is inspected against the Contract Agreement before it is handed to the consuming unit or client.

### Trigger
Arrival of a Delivery Request requesting release of a specified output under the Contract Agreement.

### Consumes
Contract Agreement supplies the output specification, acceptance criteria and delivery schedule. Delivery Request supplies the consuming unit's request and intended use date. Quality Check Record supplies the result of inspection against the specification.

### Steps
The process checks the output against the acceptance criteria in the Contract Agreement. It then verifies that the Quality Check Record covers all required attributes and that no condition is outstanding. If any acceptance criterion fails, the process rejects the output and returns it to the originator with a Rejection Notice. If criteria are met, it obtains formal acceptance from the consuming unit or the designated acceptance authority. It then records the accepted output in the Output Register and issues a Delivery Acceptance to enable payment. When the output is rejected, the process tracks the rework until re-inspection is completed and then repeats acceptance. Each rejection and re-release is logged in the Output Register.

### Produces
Delivery Acceptance records that the output met the Contract Agreement and was accepted. Output Register records all outputs, acceptance status and rejections. Rejection Notice records a failed acceptance and the required rework.

### Outcome
Contracted outputs are either accepted and handed over, or formally rejected with rework required; no output is released without recorded acceptance.

### Fails when
The quality check record is missing or the consuming unit refuses acceptance and the disagreement cannot be resolved; the output is not released, payment is withheld, and the contract completion remains blocked.

Name: Commercial Activity Reporting
Documentation:
### Identity
This process assembles the periodic account of commercial activity for management and external reporting. It collects operational and financial records into a single Commercial Activity Report.

### Trigger
Arrival of the final month-end performance data for the reporting period.

### Consumes
Contract Performance Data supplies actual output, service levels and delivery status by contract. Financial Transaction Records supply the value of invoices, payments and commitments settled in the period. Issue Log supplies the open issues and their resolution status.

### Steps
The process first reconciles Contract Performance Data against the accepted delivery records for the period. It then extracts from Financial Transaction Records all commercial spend and income, applying the institution's chart of accounts. Any transaction that cannot be matched to a Contract Agreement is flagged as unreconciled and returned to the originating unit for correction. Once all records are matched, it consolidates the data into a draft Commercial Activity Report. The draft is reviewed by the Commercial Monitoring owner and Finance; if they reject the draft, the process revises the underlying data and reissues. After approval, it publishes the Commercial Activity Report and archives the source records. The process also logs the report issue date for audit.

### Produces
Commercial Activity Report records the consolidated performance and financial position for the period. Reconciliation Exception Log records all unmatched transactions and their resolution.

### Outcome
Management has an accurate, reconciled view of commercial performance and financial position for the period.

### Fails when
Contract Performance Data or Financial Transaction Records contain unmatched entries that cannot be corrected before the reporting deadline; no report is issued, leaving performance unreported and financial statements incomplete.

Name: Commercial Contingency Planning
Documentation:
### Identity
This process maintains pre-agreed fallback arrangements for the failure of critical commercial partners or services. It converts risk exposure into tested contingency arrangements.

### Trigger
Arrival of a Risk Register update that changes the rating of a material commercial failure scenario.

### Consumes
Risk Register supplies the current risk ratings and existing mitigation actions. Contract Agreement supplies the critical obligations and the terms that apply on early termination or failure. Supplier Performance Data supplies the actual reliability and recovery capability of each critical supplier.

### Steps
The process identifies the commercial failure scenarios that exceed the institution's risk appetite, using the Risk Register. For each scenario, it reviews the Contract Agreement to determine the contractual fallback rights and the maximum acceptable downtime. It then evaluates each affected partner's recovery capability using Supplier Performance Data. Where no adequate fallback exists, it designs a Contingency Plan specifying alternate suppliers, internal workarounds, and communication triggers. The plan is costed and submitted to the Commercial Monitoring owner for approval. If rejected, it is revised and resubmitted. Once approved, it is stored in the Risk Register and assigned an owner. The process also schedules a test or review date for each plan.

### Produces
Contingency Plan records the trigger, fallback actions, owners and test schedule for each material failure scenario. Risk Register Update records the revised mitigation status for the risk.

### Outcome
Every material commercial failure scenario has a pre-agreed, owned fallback arrangement that can be invoked without negotiation.

### Fails when
No adequate fallback can be identified or the plan is not approved; the institution remains exposed to a single point of failure and improvises during an actual disruption.

Name: Commercial Contract Performance Mgt
Documentation:
### Identity
This process assesses actual performance against each active Contract Agreement and forces corrective action for any shortfall. It is the continuous monitoring heartbeat of commercial delivery.

### Trigger
Arrival of scheduled Contract Performance Data for the reporting interval.

### Consumes
Contract Agreement supplies the performance standards, key performance indicators and remedy clauses. Contract Performance Data supplies the measured actuals for each indicator. Issue Report supplies the already-reported deviations that the process re-reviews.

### Steps
The process first compares each indicator in the Contract Performance Data against the standard in the Contract Agreement. It calculates variance and trend, flagging any indicator outside tolerance. For each flagged indicator, it checks the Issue Log for an existing open resolution; if none exists, it issues a Corrective Action Request to the responsible party. It then holds a performance review with the contract owner and the counterparty where variance is material. The review decides whether to adjust the performance target, impose a remedy, or escalate. Decisions are recorded and the process updates the Contract Performance Data with the agreed interpretation. At the close of the review, it produces a Contract Performance Report for the contract. If any issue remains unresolved, it marks the report as qualified and names the open item.

### Produces
Contract Performance Report records the assessed performance, variance, and any qualifications for each contract. Corrective Action Request formalises the required remedy for each performance breach. Performance Review Minutes record the decisions and agreed actions from the review.

### Outcome
Every active contract has a current assessed performance position, and any deviation is under corrective action or formally qualified.

### Fails when
Contract Performance Data is incomplete or the review cannot agree on variance interpretation; no report is issued, and underperformance continues unmanaged and unreported.

Name: Commercial Market Analysis
Documentation:
### Identity
This process analyses the supply market for a specific requirement, producing evidence for sourcing decisions. It turns an internal Sourcing Request into a structured market understanding.

### Trigger
Arrival of a Sourcing Request from an internal unit, specifying a need for external supply and the expected category.

### Consumes
Sourcing Request supplies the requirement, volume, and category of spend. Market Data supplies supplier landscape, pricing benchmarks, and availability. Government Policy supplies procurement regulations and any mandatory sourcing constraints.

### Steps
The process first validates the Sourcing Request for completeness and category classification. It then collects Market Data from published sources, supplier briefings and internal spend records. The data is filtered for relevance to the requirement and assigned a confidence rating. The process analyses supplier concentration, pricing range, and barriers to entry. It also checks Government Policy for mandatory exclusions or preferred routes. Where the market is thin or monopolistic, it flags a sourcing risk. The analysis is compiled into a Market Analysis Report with a recommended sourcing approach. The report is reviewed by the Commercial Sourcing owner; if found insufficient, the process repeats data collection. Once approved, it produces a Supplier Shortlist of viable candidates.

### Produces
Market Analysis Report records the market structure, pricing evidence, risk and recommended approach. Supplier Shortlist records the suppliers that meet the threshold for further assessment.

### Outcome
The supply market for the requirement is understood, and a viable supplier set is available for opportunity assessment.

### Fails when
Market Data is unavailable or the requirement cannot be classified to a market; no analysis is produced, and sourcing cannot proceed.

Name: Commercial Opportunity Assessment
Documentation:
### Identity
This process evaluates each Commercial Opportunity for strategic fit, financial viability and risk before any commitment. It converts opportunities into a prioritised decision.

### Trigger
Arrival of a Commercial Opportunity from the identification step, with its provisional scope and source.

### Consumes
Commercial Opportunity supplies the proposed scope, expected benefits and origin. Market Analysis Report supplies the market evidence on feasibility, pricing and competition. Risk Register supplies the institution's current risk appetite and existing risk responses.

### Steps
The process first reviews the Commercial Opportunity for alignment with institutional strategy and the commercial portfolio. It then builds a financial model estimating income, cost and return over the contract term, using data from the Market Analysis Report. It identifies legal, operational and reputational risks and maps them to the Risk Register. Where a risk exceeds appetite, the process proposes mitigation and recalculates viability. The assessment is compiled into an Opportunity Assessment Report with a recommendation of proceed, defer, or reject. The report is submitted to the Commercial Sourcing owner for a Go/No-Go decision. If a decision is deferred, the process requests additional data and updates the report. Once decided, it issues an Opportunity Decision recording the outcome and any conditions for proceeding.

### Produces
Opportunity Assessment Report records the financial analysis, risk assessment and recommendation. Opportunity Decision records the Go/No-Go outcome and any conditions.

### Outcome
Each Commercial Opportunity is assessed and prioritised; only viable, strategically aligned opportunities proceed to sourcing or engagement.

### Fails when
The financial model cannot be built or the owner withholds a decision beyond the assessed window; the opportunity remains in limbo and cannot be acted upon.

Name: Commercial Opportunity Identification
Documentation:
### Identity
This process recognises and logs potential commercial opportunities from internal needs and market signals. It is the front door for new commercial activity.

### Trigger
Arrival of a Service Request expressing an internal need or a market signal that supports an external commercial arrangement.

### Consumes
Service Request supplies the need, expected volume and the benefit sought. Market Analysis Report supplies the currently known market conditions that affect feasibility.

### Steps
The process first screens the Service Request against the institution's commercial strategy and existing Contract Agreements to avoid duplication. It then extracts the core need and converts it into a draft Commercial Opportunity with a provisional scope and outcome. The draft is validated against the Market Analysis Report to confirm there is a supply market for the need. If no market exists, the process rejects the opportunity and returns the Service Request to the originator with a Rejection Notice. For valid opportunities, it logs the Commercial Opportunity in the Opportunity Register and assigns a preliminary owner. The process also records the source of the opportunity for audit.

### Produces
Commercial Opportunity records the defined need, provisional scope and next step for assessment. Opportunity Register records all identified opportunities and their status. Rejection Notice records a need that cannot be converted and the reason.

### Outcome
Each viable internal need is converted into a logged Commercial Opportunity awaiting assessment; non-viable needs are returned with reason.

### Fails when
A Service Request cannot be expressed as a commercial opportunity or no market exists; nothing is logged, and the need remains unaddressed.

Name: Commercial Partner Engagement
Documentation:
### Identity
This process selects and agreements external partners for a commercial activity. It moves from initial opportunity to a signed Engagement Agreement, ensuring only qualified partners proceed.

### Trigger
Arrival of a Partner Opportunity identifying a need for an external party to participate in a commercial activity.

### Consumes
Partner Opportunity supplies the scope of collaboration and the capability sought. Partner Profile supplies the prospective partner's track record, financial standing and service capabilities. Due Diligence Questionnaire supplies the prospective partner's responses on compliance, data protection, and financial stability.

### Steps
The process first qualifies the Partner Opportunity against the Commercial Activity scope and confirms the required partner profile. It then issues a Due Diligence Questionnaire to shortlisted partners and receives their responses. The process evaluates the responses against mandatory criteria, including financial standing and regulatory compliance; any partner that fails a mandatory criterion is removed from consideration. For remaining partners, it conducts a comparative assessment and selects a preferred partner. Negotiation then produces draft engagement terms, which are reviewed by Legal and Finance. If a review rejects the terms, the process returns to negotiation. When terms are approved, it issues an Engagement Agreement and a Partner Selection Decision, recording the selected partner and the agreed scope.

### Produces
Engagement Agreement records the signed terms for collaboration. Partner Selection Decision records the chosen partner and the reasons for selection. Partner Due Diligence Report records the due diligence findings and confirmation of mandatory criteria.

### Outcome
A qualified partner is selected and engaged under agreed terms for a defined commercial activity.

### Fails when
No shortlisted partner passes due diligence or the internal review rejects the engagement terms and no alternative is proposed; the commercial activity cannot proceed to integration and remains without a partner.

Name: Commercial Partner Integration & Transition
Documentation:
### Identity
This process brings a newly engaged partner into operational delivery and, where required, transfers activity from an incumbent. It produces the plans and evidence that make the partner accountable.

### Trigger
Arrival of a signed Engagement Agreement and a completed Partner Due Diligence Report, marking the point at which the partner is ready to begin operational integration.

### Consumes
Engagement Agreement supplies the scope, obligations and service levels the partner must meet. Partner Profile supplies the partner's operational capabilities and contact structures. Incumbent Handover Record supplies the confirmed state of current activity, open items and asset transfers.

### Steps
The process first reviews the Engagement Agreement and Partner Profile to build an Integration Plan specifying milestones, owners and readiness checks. It then assesses the partner's operational readiness against the plan; if any readiness check fails, the process holds the start of service and requires the partner to remediate. Once readiness is confirmed, it develops a Transition Plan for moving each activity, asset and data set from the incumbent or internal unit to the partner. It executes the transition in the agreed sequence, verifying each handover against a checklist. Any unresolved item is logged and assigned to the partner or the incumbent. After all items are confirmed, it issues a Handover Certificate recording that the partner has accepted operational responsibility. The process also issues a Transition Plan as a live document for post-transition review.

### Produces
Integration Plan records the staged integration activities and readiness checks. Transition Plan records the agreed sequence and owner for each transferred activity. Handover Certificate records that the partner has accepted operational responsibility and all open items are resolved.

### Outcome
The partner is operating within the commercial activity with no gap in service and with a documented transfer of accountability.

### Fails when
A readiness check fails repeatedly or an open transition item has no owner by the service start date; the partner cannot begin, the incumbent has already exited, and the commercial activity suffers a service gap.

Name: Commercial Tenancy
Documentation:
### Identity
Management of commercial leases and licences for third-party occupation of institutional space. It handles rent, compliance, and tenant relations.

### Trigger
The arrival of a Commercial Tenancy Application or a rent review date.

### Consumes
Commercial Tenancy Application supplies the prospective tenant's business and proposed use. Lease Agreement Template supplies the standard terms and obligations. Tenant Payment Record supplies the rent and service charge status.

### Steps
The process assesses the proposed use against planning and institutional policy. It negotiates and finalises the Lease Agreement. It collects rent and service charges and reconciles them. It monitors tenant compliance with lease terms. It handles tenant requests and maintenance obligations. If a tenant breaches terms, a Breach Notice is issued with a remedy period. At lease expiry, renewal or termination is processed. The space condition is inspected on handover.

### Produces
Commercial Lease Agreement states the tenant's occupancy rights and obligations. Rent Demand states the amount and due date for each period. Tenant Breach Notice states the specific non-compliance and remedy required.

### Outcome
Institutional space is legally occupied by approved tenants, and rent and compliance are actively managed.

### Fails when
A tenant stops paying rent or breaches occupancy terms, causing lost income and unmanaged space.

Name: Commercialise Research Outcomes
Documentation:
### Identity
Work here converts research outputs with commercial potential into revenue-generating agreements, licences, or new ventures.

### Trigger
The arrival of an Intellectual Property Disclosure from a researcher, when a Research Output has been flagged as having commercial application.

### Consumes
Intellectual Property Disclosure supplies the invention description, inventors, and the funder or contractual background. Research Output supplies the underlying research result and its publication status. Commercialisation Plan supplies the chosen route to market, target sector, and revenue model. Market Assessment supplies the demand evidence and competitor analysis. Research Contract supplies any prior rights or obligations that affect ownership.

### Steps
The Intellectual Property Disclosure is logged and checked for completeness and inventorship. The process then commissions a Market Assessment to establish demand and patentability. If the assessment shows no commercial value, the disclosure is closed and recorded as non-commercial. If value exists, the process drafts a Commercialisation Plan selecting licensing, assignment, or spinout as the route. The plan is approved by the research commercialisation committee. For licensing, the process negotiates and issues a License Agreement that specifies royalty terms and field of use. For spinout, the process establishes a Spinout Company, allocates equity, and licenses the underlying Research Output to the new company. Royalty Record is created to track future payments due to the institution.

### Produces
License Agreement: issued when a third party receives rights to use the intellectual property, establishing revenue terms. Spinout Company: established when the route requires a new legal entity, transferring ownership of the commercial activity. Royalty Record: issued when a licence is signed, establishing the schedule of payments owed to the institution.

### Outcome
Research outputs with commercial value are under a revenue-generating agreement or a formally established venture.

### Fails when
The Market Assessment underestimates patent risk and a License Agreement is signed without freedom-to-operate clearance; the institution faces an infringement claim.

Name: Complaint & Compliment Mgt
Documentation:
### Identity
Handling of complaints and compliments from students, staff, and the public.

### Trigger
The arrival of a formal complaint or compliment.

### Consumes
Complaint Form supplies the issue and resolution sought. Compliment Note supplies the praise. Complaint Policy supplies the timeframes and stages.

### Steps
The process logs the complaint or compliment. It acknowledges receipt. It investigates the complaint. It gathers evidence from relevant parties. It issues a response. If unresolved, it escalates to the next stage. It records learning and actions. It reports on complaint trends. Compliments are shared with the responsible teams.

### Produces
Complaint Response Letter states the outcome and any remedy. Complaint Investigation Record states the findings. Compliment Acknowledgement Letter thanks the sender.

### Outcome
Complaints are resolved fairly and within time limits, and learning is captured.

### Fails when
A complaint is not acknowledged within the policy timeframe, causing escalation and reputational damage.

Name: Compliance Monitoring & Reporting
Documentation:
### Identity
This process monitors the institution's compliance with external regulatory obligations and reports evidence to the relevant regulator by each due date. It is the part of the capability that demonstrates lawful operation.

### Trigger
A new Government Policy Document or a scheduled regulatory reporting date triggers the process, when the institution must show evidence of compliance.

### Consumes
Compliance Obligation supplies the specific legal requirement, owner, and due date. Evidence Record supplies the documents and data proving compliance. Statutory Filing Template supplies the format and data fields required by the regulator. Policy Statement supplies the institution's approved position on the obligation.

### Steps
First the process maps each Compliance Obligation to the applicable Evidence Record and owner. It then schedules each required return in advance of its due date. It gathers the needed evidence and assesses whether it meets the obligation. If evidence is missing or inadequate, it raises a corrective action and notifies the owner. It drafts the Statutory Filing using the template and the evidence. It obtains formal approval from the accountable executive. It files the completed return with the regulator and records the filing date.

### Produces
Compliance Status Report records the status of each Compliance Obligation: compliant, non-compliant, or partially compliant. Statutory Filing records the completed return submitted to the regulator and its submission date.

### Outcome
Every Compliance Obligation has a current evidence status and every due Statutory Filing has been submitted; non-compliance is visible to the governing body.

### Fails when
The Evidence Record for a Compliance Obligation cannot be located, because the associated Statutory Filing cannot be completed and the institution misses a regulatory deadline, exposing it to sanction.

Name: Contract Mgt
Documentation:
### Identity
Management of contracts from drafting through negotiation, execution, and post-signature compliance.

### Trigger
The arrival of a contract drafting request or a contract review need.

### Consumes
Contract Request supplies the business need and key terms. Contract Template supplies the standard clauses. Risk Assessment supplies the identified legal and business risks.

### Steps
The process drafts the contract using the template. It negotiates terms with the counterparty. It reviews legal and commercial risks. It obtains internal approvals. It executes the contract. It stores the signed agreement. It monitors key dates and obligations. It handles amendments and variations. If a breach occurs, it initiates the dispute process.

### Produces
Contract Agreement states the final signed terms. Contract Register Entry records the metadata and key dates. Contract Variation states the agreed change.

### Outcome
The institution's contracts are valid, accessible, and managed for compliance.

### Fails when
A contract is executed without approval or key deadlines are missed, causing legal exposure.

Name: Copyright Mgt
Documentation:
### Identity
Management of copyright for institutional works, including licensing, permissions, and enforcement.

### Trigger
The arrival of a copyright permission request or a copyright infringement notice.

### Consumes
Copyright Permission Request supplies the work and proposed use. Copyright Policy supplies the institution's rules on use. Copyright Register supplies the owned copyrights and licences.

### Steps
The process evaluates the request against policy and rights. It obtains or grants permissions. It records licences. It monitors for infringement. It issues takedown requests for unauthorised use. It advises staff and students on copyright. It renews licences. If an infringement is disputed, it refers to legal. It reports annually.

### Produces
Copyright Permission Grant states the allowed use and conditions. Licence Agreement records the terms for third-party content. Infringement Notice states the violation and required action.

### Outcome
The institution complies with copyright law and protects its own works.

### Fails when
A permission requirement is overlooked, causing an infringement claim and financial penalty.

Name: Corporate Performance Mgt
Documentation:
### Identity
This process monitors the institution's Key Performance Indicators against annual targets, analyses variances, and initiates corrective action where performance is off track. It is the part of the capability that holds the institution to its strategic commitments.

### Trigger
The end of a reporting period or the availability of a new Performance Data set triggers the process, when targets for that period are due to be assessed.

### Consumes
Key Performance Indicators supply the defined measures and their targets for the academic year. Performance Data supply the actual values for student enrolments, research outputs, commercial contracts, and service requests. Corrective Action Request from previous periods supplies unresolved performance gaps.

### Steps
First the process collects the actual Performance Data for each KPI and calculates the variance against target. It then identifies the KPIs with significant adverse variance. For each, it analyses the root cause using the underlying activity data. It drafts a Performance Review Report for the responsible executive. It decides whether a Corrective Action Request is required and assigns an owner. It monitors the implementation of existing corrective actions and updates their status. It presents the performance dashboard to the governing body.

### Produces
Performance Dashboard records the current values, targets, and variances for each KPI. Performance Review Report records the analysis of significant variances and the actions agreed. Corrective Action Request records the owner, action, and due date for each unresolved variance.

### Outcome
The institution's performance against its KPI targets is visible each reporting period, and each significant variance has an assigned corrective action.

### Fails when
Performance Data for a KPI are not available, because the variance cannot be calculated and the KPI is reported as null, leaving a gap in the governing body's view of institutional performance.

Name: Curriculum & Resource Development
Documentation:
### Identity
The work of developing learning materials and resources for approved curricula.

### Trigger
A Curriculum Approval indicating a need for new teaching resources.

### Consumes
Curriculum Approval supplies the approved learning outcomes. Teaching Content Pack from prior modules supplies reusable materials. Resource Budget supplies funding constraints. Accessibility Standard supplies the compliance requirements.

### Steps
The developer identifies required resources against the learning outcomes. Materials are produced or sourced. The draft Teaching Content Pack is reviewed against institutional standards and the Accessibility Standard. Copyright and licensing checks are completed. A peer review is conducted. The final pack is stored in the repository with version control. A Resource Usage Log is updated.

### Produces
Teaching Content Pack for the module. Resource Usage Log recording what was produced. Peer Review Record confirming quality.

### Outcome
Approved curricula have complete learning resources available for delivery.

### Fails when
Resource Budget is insufficient and the pack cannot be completed, leaving modules without materials.

Name: Curriculum Change Mgt
Documentation:
### Identity
The work of evaluating, approving and implementing changes to existing curricula.

### Trigger
A Curriculum Change Request submitted by a faculty or external body.

### Consumes
Curriculum Change Request supplies the proposed modification. Current Curriculum Blueprint supplies the baseline. Academic Policy supplies the rules governing change. Professional Body Requirement supplies external constraints.

### Steps
The request is logged and assessed for impact on learning outcomes, resources and accreditation. The assessor checks the change against Academic Policy and Professional Body Requirement and identifies affected modules. If the change is minor, it is approved by the faculty board; if major, it goes to the Curriculum Approval Committee. The committee decision is recorded. On approval, the Curriculum Blueprint is updated and affected modules are flagged. Stakeholders are notified. If the request is rejected, the proposer receives a Rejection Notice with reasons.

### Produces
Updated Curriculum Blueprint. Curriculum Change Decision. Stakeholder Notification.

### Outcome
Curriculum changes are controlled, recorded and aligned with approved learning outcomes.

### Fails when
A major change fails committee approval and no revised request is submitted, leaving the curriculum misaligned with requirements.

Name: Curriculum Design
Documentation:
### Identity
The work of creating a new programme or module specification, including learning outcomes, content structure and assessment strategy.

### Trigger
A Curriculum Proposal is submitted by a faculty.

### Consumes
Curriculum Proposal supplies the academic intent and target market. Market Demand Analysis supplies evidence of student demand. Academic Policy supplies the regulatory framework. Resource Capacity Statement supplies available staff and rooms.

### Steps
