The process evaluates the proposal against strategy and policy. It conducts due diligence on the partner. It negotiates the collaboration agreement. It obtains internal approval. It establishes monitoring and annual review. It manages joint activities and resolves disputes. If the collaboration is non-viable, it is declined or wound down. It maintains a register of all inter-institutional relationships.

### Produces
Inter-Institutional Agreement states the agreed scope and obligations. Due Diligence Report records the partner assessment. Collaboration Review summarizes performance and future options.

### Outcome
The institution maintains productive and compliant relationships with other tertiary institutions.

### Fails when
A partner institution fails to meet its obligations, causing joint programmes to suffer and the relationship to deteriorate.

Name: PGR Student Skills Development
Documentation:
### Identity
Work here assesses and develops the skills of postgraduate research students to meet doctoral training requirements.

### Trigger
The arrival of a new PGR Student Record at the start of doctoral study, when the student has no Training Plan.

### Consumes
PGR Student Record supplies the student's background, discipline, and programme requirements. Training Needs Assessment supplies the identified skill gaps from induction and supervisor input. Training Completion Record supplies any prior completed training that counts towards the requirement.

### Steps
The Training Needs Assessment is reviewed against the PGR Student Record to confirm the required skills. A Training Plan is drafted listing mandatory and elective training courses. The plan is agreed with the student and supervisor. As training is completed, the Training Completion Record is updated and checked against the plan.

### Produces
Training Plan: issued when the required skills and courses are agreed, establishing the student's development route. Training Completion Record: updated after each course, establishing progress towards the plan.

### Outcome
Every PGR student has a current Training Plan and an accurate record of completed training.

### Fails when
The Training Needs Assessment is not completed and the student is assigned generic training; a required skill is missed and the student fails progression.

Name: PGR Supervisor Development
Documentation:
### Identity
Work here ensures postgraduate research supervisors have the required competencies and ongoing development to supervise effectively.

### Trigger
The assignment of a new PGR supervisor, when the supervisor's Competency Record does not show current approval.

### Consumes
Supervisor Competency Record supplies the supervisor's training history and approval status. PGR Student Record supplies the number and discipline of students assigned. Training Completion Record supplies evidence of completed development activities.

### Steps
The Supervisor Competency Record is checked for required supervisory training. If the supervisor is not approved, they are required to complete the mandatory induction before assignment is confirmed. A Supervisor Development Plan is issued, listing any further training needed based on current student load. As development is completed, the Training Completion Record and Supervisor Competency Record are updated.

### Produces
Supervisor Development Plan: issued when gaps are identified, establishing the required development actions. Supervisor Competency Record: updated with the new approval status, establishing the supervisor's current competence.

### Outcome
All PGR supervisors are approved and have a current development plan.

### Fails when
The assignment is confirmed before induction training is completed and the supervisor fails a student progression review; the student complains and the assignment is revoked.

Name: Personal Learning Mgt
Documentation:
### Identity
The work of helping students plan their personal development goals.

### Trigger
A student requests personal learning guidance.

### Consumes
Student Enrolment supplies the programme context. Personal Development Plan supplies existing goals. Progress Check supplies the current status.

### Steps
The student's current progress is reviewed. New goals are set. A Personal Development Plan is updated. The plan is scheduled for follow-up. A progress check is completed at the next meeting.

### Produces
Personal Development Plan. Progress Update.

### Outcome
Students have current personal learning goals.

### Fails when
The student does not attend follow-up and the plan goes stale.

Name: Personal Tutor Provision
Documentation:
### Identity
The work of assigning and delivering personal tutoring to students.

### Trigger
A new student cohort is created and personal tutor assignments are due.

### Consumes
Student Enrolment supplies the student list. Staff Availability Record supplies tutors. Personal Tutor Allocation Rule supplies the allocation basis. Tutorial Schedule supplies the meeting times.

### Steps
Students are matched to tutors based on programme and availability. The allocation is recorded. The tutor meets the student at least once per term. Issues raised are logged. Escalations to specialist support are recorded. An annual review of the allocation is performed.

### Produces
Personal Tutor Allocation. Tutorial Meeting Record. Support Referral.

### Outcome
Every student has an assigned personal tutor and regular contact.

### Fails when
Insufficient staff are available and some students are left without a tutor.

Name: Policy & Regulation Mgt
Documentation:
### Identity
This process develops, reviews, and approves the institution's Policy Statements in response to changing external regulation and internal governance decisions. It is the part of the capability that maintains a current suite of compliant policies.

### Trigger
The publication of a new or amended Government Policy Document, or a Governance Decision requiring policy change, starts the process when existing policy is known to be insufficient.

### Consumes
Government Policy Document supplies the new legal or regulatory requirement. Existing Policy Statement supplies the current policy to be amended or replaced. Stakeholder Consultation Feedback supplies the views of affected staff and students. Equality Impact Assessment Record supplies the analysis of equalities implications.

### Steps
First the process analyses the new requirement and identifies which Existing Policy Statement is affected. It drafts a revised policy. It conducts a consultation with affected stakeholders and records their feedback. It completes an equality impact assessment. It incorporates the required changes and prepares the final Policy Statement. It submits the policy to the governing body for approval. After approval, it publishes the policy and records the effective date.

### Produces
Policy Statement records the approved policy text, its effective date, and the governing body approval reference. Equality Impact Assessment Record records the equalities analysis and any mitigations included in the final policy.

### Outcome
The institution has a current, approved Policy Statement for each changed regulatory requirement, with evidence of consultation and equality impact assessment.

### Fails when
The Equality Impact Assessment Record is not completed before approval, because the Policy Statement cannot lawfully proceed to governing body approval and the regulatory deadline is missed.

Name: Presence Based Teaching
Documentation:
### Identity
The work of delivering face-to-face teaching sessions.

### Trigger
The published Timetable indicates a presence based session.

### Consumes
Teaching Content Pack supplies the materials. Room Booking Confirmation supplies the room. Module Registration supplies the expected attendees. Equipment Check supplies the required technology.

### Steps
The room is prepared. The session is delivered. Attendance is recorded. Any issues are logged. An incident report is created if significant disruption occurs.

### Produces
Teaching Session Record. Attendance Register. Incident Report.

### Outcome
Students receive scheduled face-to-face teaching.

### Fails when
The room is double-booked and no alternative is available, cancelling the session.

Name: Printing Mgt
Documentation:
### Identity
Management of institutional printing, including print requests, production, and document finishing.

### Trigger
The arrival of a print request.

### Consumes
Print Request supplies the document and specifications. Print Machine Availability supplies the capacity and capability. Stock Record supplies paper and consumables.

### Steps
The process validates the request against policy. It schedules printing. It produces the document. It finishes and binds. It quality checks. It delivers or notifies the requester. It records usage and charges. If a print error occurs, it is reproduced. It maintains machines.

### Produces
Printed Document states the physical output. Print Job Record states the quantity and cost. Usage Report records the consumption.

### Outcome
Requesters receive high-quality printed materials on time.

### Fails when
A printer breaks down, causing a backlog and missed deadlines for critical documents.

Name: Private Sector Housing Mgt
Documentation:
### Identity
Management of relationships with private landlords and the placement of students into external rented housing. It maintains property listings, inspects standards, and supports student tenants.

### Trigger
The arrival of a private landlord property registration or a student request for private housing assistance.

### Consumes
Private Landlord Registration supplies the property details, safety certificates, and letting terms. Student Housing Request supplies the student's needs, budget, and preferred area. Property Inspection Report supplies the condition and compliance status of a listed property.

### Steps
The process validates landlord registration and safety certificate currency. It matches student requests against registered properties that meet standards. It arranges viewings and provides tenancy guidance. It monitors tenancy agreements and supports dispute resolution. It schedules property inspections and follows up on non-compliance. If a property fails inspection, it is suspended from the listings until remedial works are confirmed. It maintains a record of available and unavailable properties. Tenancy deposits are tracked for return or dispute.

### Produces
Private Property Listing states a compliant property as available or suspended. Tenancy Guidance Pack supplies the student with contract and deposit advice. Inspection Follow-Up Request states the remedial work required for a listed property.

### Outcome
Students are placed only in compliant private housing, and landlord listings reflect verified standards.

### Fails when
Landlord safety certificates expire or properties fail inspection, causing available housing stock to shrink and student demand to go unmet.

Name: Procurement & Purchasing Mgt
Documentation:
### Identity
Procurement of goods, services, and works from requisition through sourcing to contract award.

### Trigger
The arrival of a Procurement Request from an authorised budget holder.

### Consumes
Procurement Request supplies the specification, quantity, and budget code. Approved Budget supplies the available funds for the purchase. Supplier Catalogue supplies pre-approved items and prices.

### Steps
The process validates the procurement request against budget and procurement policy. It determines the appropriate route: catalogue, quotation, or tender. It runs the sourcing process, issuing requests for quotation or tender. It evaluates bids against criteria. It obtains internal approval and awards the contract or purchase order. It records the commitment. It manages any legal review of the contract. If the request exceeds budget or policy, it is rejected or escalated. Award decisions are documented.

### Produces
Purchase Order states the supplier, price, and quantity of the order. Contract Agreement states the legal terms for a procured service or works. Bid Evaluation Record records the scoring and award justification.

### Outcome
The institution procures goods and services at best value and within budget and policy.

### Fails when
Budget is insufficient or tenders receive no compliant bids, causing the requisitioning unit to operate without required goods or services.

Name: Professional Accreditation
Documentation:
### Identity
The work of preparing and submitting accreditation applications for professional programmes.

### Trigger
An Accreditation Submission Deadline set by the professional body.

### Consumes
Accreditation Application supplies the programme evidence. Curriculum Blueprint supplies the programme specification. Graduate Outcomes Data supplies employment statistics. Standards Evidence Matrix supplies the mapping of criteria to evidence.

### Steps
The accreditation coordinator collects evidence against each accreditation criterion. The Accreditation Application is compiled. An internal reviewer checks completeness. The application is submitted to the professional body. A site visit or panel review occurs. The Accreditation Decision is received and recorded. If conditions are attached, the faculty responds with an action plan. The action plan is implemented and evidence of completion is submitted.

### Produces
Accreditation Application. Accreditation Decision. Accreditation Action Plan. Standards Evidence Matrix.

### Outcome
Professional programmes hold recognised accreditation status.

### Fails when
The Accreditation Decision is denied and no appeal or resubmission is made, losing professional recognition.

Name: Professional Learning (Staff)
Documentation:
### Identity
The work of arranging and recording staff professional development activities.

### Trigger
A Staff Development Need identified by an annual appraisal.

### Consumes
Staff Development Plan supplies the identified training needs. Training Course Catalogue supplies available courses. Training Budget supplies funding. Line Manager Approval supplies the authorisation.

### Steps
The staff member selects a course from the catalogue. Approval is sought from the line manager. The booking is made. Attendance is recorded. A Staff Development Record is updated. An evaluation form is completed. The new competence is added to the staff profile.

### Produces
Staff Development Record. Training Certificate. Training Evaluation Form.

### Outcome
Staff have current professional development records and completed training.

### Fails when
The Training Budget is exhausted and no approval is given, leaving development need unmet.

Name: Programme and Project Mgt
Documentation:
### Identity
This process manages approved programmes and projects from initiation through to closure, controlling scope, schedule, cost, quality, and risk. It is the part of the capability that delivers the outputs of change initiatives.

### Trigger
An approved Business Case or Project Mandate authorises a new project or programme, when resources are available and the project manager is appointed.

### Consumes
Business Case supplies the objectives, expected benefits, budget, and success criteria. Project Plan supplies the activities, milestones, dependencies, and resource assignments. Resource Allocation supplies the assigned staff and budget against each activity. Risk Register supplies the known risks and their ownership. Issue Log supplies the current issues requiring resolution. Deliverable Acceptance Record supplies evidence of acceptance for completed outputs.

### Steps
First the process reviews the Business Case and establishes the project governance structure and baseline Project Plan. Then it tracks actual progress against the plan, collecting status data from work packages. It manages risks and issues, deciding whether to mitigate, transfer, accept, or escalate each. It controls changes to scope, schedule, or cost through a change control decision. When a deliverable is completed, it obtains formal acceptance from the sponsor. It monitors stage boundaries and decides whether the project should continue to the next stage. At closure, it reviews benefits handover and confirms all deliverables are accepted.

### Produces
Project Status Report records actual progress, forecasts, and exceptions after each reporting period. Change Request records a proposed change to baselines and its disposition. Project Closure Report records the final performance against baselines and the lessons learned.

### Outcome
Every approved project has a controlled baseline, a documented decision at each stage boundary, and a formal closure record; benefits commitments pass to the accountable owner for post-project tracking.

### Fails when
The Business Case baseline is not approved or the Project Plan lacks dependencies, because project performance cannot be measured and changes cannot be distinguished from initial scope, leading to uncontrolled delivery.

Name: Programme Enrolment
Documentation:
### Identity
The work of formally enrolling an accepted applicant onto a programme.

### Trigger
An Offer Acceptance is received from the applicant.

### Consumes
Offer Acceptance supplies the accepted offer and conditions. Student Application supplies the applicant's data. Academic Policy supplies enrolment requirements. Identity Document supplies the verification.

### Steps
The acceptance is matched to the original offer. Any conditions are checked; if unmet, the applicant is notified. The applicant's identity is confirmed using Identity Document. Fees are confirmed. The Student Enrolment record is created. The Student Record is created or updated. An Enrolment Confirmation is issued. The new student is eligible for module selection.

### Produces
Student Enrolment. Enrolment Confirmation. Updated Student Record.

### Outcome
Accepted applicants become enrolled students with an active record.

### Fails when
Conditions remain unmet and the applicant does not provide evidence, leaving the offer unfulfilled.

Name: Programme Transfer Mgt
Documentation:
### Identity
The work of evaluating and executing a student's transfer between programmes.

### Trigger
A Programme Transfer Request submitted by a student.

### Consumes
Student Enrolment supplies the current programme. Programme Transfer Request supplies the target programme and rationale. Academic Policy supplies transfer rules including credit recognition. Target Programme Capacity supplies the available places.

### Steps
The request is assessed for eligibility against the target programme's entry requirements. The student's current Student Results Record is reviewed for transferable credit. The target programme capacity is checked. If credit recognition is needed, a credit mapping is prepared. The receiving faculty approves or rejects the request. On approval, the Student Enrolment is updated to the new programme. The Student Record is updated with the transfer. The student is issued a Programme Transfer Approval. If rejected, the student is informed with reasons.

### Produces
Programme Transfer Approval. Updated Student Enrolment. Credit Recognition Record.

### Outcome
Students are correctly enrolled in a programme that matches their academic path.

### Fails when
The target programme has no capacity or the credit recognition cannot be agreed, leaving the student unable to transfer.

Name: Property Maintenance
Documentation:
### Identity
Reactive and planned maintenance of buildings, plant, and infrastructure. It receives work requests and planned schedules, and executes them.

### Trigger
The arrival of a Facilities Work Order from a building user or a planned maintenance schedule date.

### Consumes
Facilities Work Order supplies the defect or task description, location, and priority. Maintenance Schedule supplies the planned service intervals for building assets. Building Condition Survey supplies the life-cycle defect list.

### Steps
The process prioritises work orders against safety and operational impact. It schedules work and allocates resources. It performs the maintenance or repair. It checks completion against the required standard. Safety-critical work is completed first. If a repair cannot be completed, it is escalated to a higher work category. Completed work is recorded against the asset. Recurring issues are fed back into the maintenance schedule.

### Produces
Completed Work Order records the repair action and closure time. Asset Service Record updates the maintenance history. Follow-Up Work Order states any remaining or new work identified.

### Outcome
Building assets are maintained to an acceptable condition, and reported defects are resolved or escalated.

### Fails when
Critical spares are unavailable or skilled labour is absent, causing safety-critical repairs to remain open and building areas to close.

Name: Prospective Student Engagement
Documentation:
### Identity
The work of engaging prospective students before application.

### Trigger
A Prospective Student Enquiry is received via website, email or phone.

### Consumes
Prospective Student Enquiry supplies the question and contact details. Prospectus supplies programme information. Open Day Schedule supplies events. Response Template supplies standard answers.

### Steps
The enquiry is logged and routed to the appropriate recruiter. A response is prepared using Prospectus information and the Response Template. The prospective student is invited to an Open Day. Follow-up is scheduled. The interaction is recorded. A lead score is assigned based on engagement.

### Produces
Enquiry Response. Prospective Student Interaction Record. Lead Score.

### Outcome
Prospective students receive timely and accurate information and are invited to engage further.

### Fails when
Enquiries are not answered within the service standard, losing the prospective student.

Name: Public Relationship Mgt
Documentation:
### Identity
Management of the institution's relationship with the general public, including community engagement and public events.

### Trigger
The arrival of a public enquiry or a scheduled community engagement event.

### Consumes
Public Enquiry supplies the public's question or concern. Community Engagement Plan supplies the planned activities and messages. Event Proposal supplies the proposed public event.

### Steps
The process logs and routes public enquiries to the appropriate unit. It plans and delivers community events. It monitors public perception. It responds to complaints or concerns. It reports on engagement outcomes. If a public event is planned, it obtains necessary permissions and manages logistics. It records all interactions for future reference.

### Produces
Public Enquiry Response states the answer given. Community Event Report records the outcomes and feedback. Public Perception Summary records the measured sentiment.

### Outcome
The institution is accessible to the public and manages its community reputation.

### Fails when
A public concern is ignored or a community event causes disruption, leading to community opposition and reputational loss.

Name: Quality Mgt
Documentation:
### Identity
This process defines quality standards for the institution's operational processes and verifies that those standards are met through audits and reviews. It is the part of the capability that ensures consistent service delivery.

### Trigger
The approval of the annual quality plan or the receipt of a quality complaint or incident starts the process, when quality performance needs to be assessed.

### Consumes
Quality Standard supplies the acceptance criteria and benchmarks for a given activity. Audit Findings supplies evidence of nonconformance from previous assurance work. Service Delivery Record supplies actual performance data for the period under review.

### Steps
First the process selects the operational area to be reviewed from the annual plan. It compares the Service Delivery Record against the Quality Standard. When it finds nonconformance, it records the finding and its severity. It then identifies root causes and requested corrective actions. It agrees a Quality Improvement Plan with the process owner. It schedules a follow-up review to verify that actions have closed the gaps. If a finding is high severity, it escalates to the responsible director and sets an immediate corrective action deadline.

### Produces
Quality Review Report records the assessed area, criteria used, and findings. Quality Improvement Plan records each nonconformance, its root cause, the agreed action, owner, and due date.

### Outcome
Operational processes have verified conformance to defined quality standards, and identified nonconformances have an owner and a committed correction date.

### Fails when
The Quality Standard is not defined for the area under review, because conformance cannot be judged and the review produces no actionable findings, leaving poor service ungoverned.

Name: Records Mgt
Documentation:
### Identity
Records management, including classification, retention, disposal, and archival of institutional records.

### Trigger
The arrival of a new record or a retention disposal review.

### Consumes
New Record Item supplies the record and its metadata. Retention Schedule supplies the required retention periods and disposal actions. Records Classification Scheme supplies the categories and access rules.

### Steps
The process classifies the record. It applies metadata and security. It stores in the records repository. It manages retention and holds. It executes disposal or transfer to archive. It provides access to authorised users. It responds to Freedom of Information requests. It audits disposal. If a record is subject to litigation hold, disposal is suspended.

### Produces
Records Disposal Certificate records the authorised destruction. Records Transfer Confirmation records the move to archive. Records Access Log records who accessed what.

### Outcome
The institution's records are complete, retrievable, and disposed of lawfully.

### Fails when
Records are destroyed before their retention period, causing legal non-compliance and loss of evidence.

Name: Religious Support
Documentation:
### Identity
Provision of religious and pastoral support, including chaplaincy services and prayer spaces.

### Trigger
The arrival of a request for religious support or a scheduled service.

### Consumes
Support Request supplies the individual's need. Religious Calendar supplies the upcoming events and festivals. Room Booking Confirmation supplies the prayer space.

### Steps
The process receives the request. It assigns a chaplain. It provides counselling or ritual support. It organises services. It manages prayer spaces. It promotes interfaith dialogue. It responds to emergencies. If a request needs external clergy, it arranges contact. It records the interaction.

### Produces
Support Session Record states the support provided. Service Schedule states the upcoming services. Room Booking Confirmation for prayer spaces.

### Outcome
The campus community has access to religious support and appropriate spaces.

### Fails when
No suitable prayer space is available, causing unmet religious needs.

Name: Remuneration & Entitlements Mgt
Documentation:
### Identity
Management of staff remuneration, payroll, and entitlements, including salaries, allowances, and pension contributions.

### Trigger
The arrival of a payroll cycle date or a change to an employee's contractual terms.

### Consumes
Payroll Input File supplies the employee time, changes, and deductions for the period. Employee Contract supplies the base salary and terms. Entitlement Policy supplies the rules for pension, leave, and allowances.

### Steps
The process collects and validates payroll inputs. It calculates gross pay, deductions, and net pay. It processes the payroll run. It distributes payslips. It pays employees and statutory bodies. It reconciles the payroll to the general ledger. It handles payroll queries and corrections. If a payroll error occurs, an off-cycle correction is run. Year-end reporting is completed.

### Produces
Payslip states the employee's pay and deductions for the period. Payroll Report states the total payroll cost and deductions. Payroll Correction Entry records any adjustment to a previous pay period.

### Outcome
Employees are paid correctly and on time, and all statutory obligations are met.

### Fails when
Payroll input is late or incorrect, causing delayed or incorrect pay and employee dissatisfaction.

Name: Research Compliance Mgt
Documentation:
### Identity
Work here translates external research policy into binding internal controls and verifies that active research activity complies with data protection, open access, and funder conditions. It is the control function that keeps the Research domain inside legal and funder mandates.

### Trigger
The arrival of a new Government Policy document or a changed Research Funding Application template, when existing Compliance Requirements do not yet reflect the change.

### Consumes
Government Policy supplies the new statutory or funding condition that must be turned into an internal control. Research Activity Record supplies the current set of live research projects, data handling practices, and publication intentions against which the new condition is checked. Data Management Plan supplies the agreed data handling controls for each active project; when a plan conflicts with the new condition, the process flags it. Compliance Requirement supplies the existing register of internal controls that the new condition may supersede or extend.

### Steps
First, the new Government Policy is read and each clause mapped to the institution's existing research activity. Where a clause affects data handling, the matching Data Management Plan is selected for review. A gap check then compares the clause against the current Compliance Requirement register. Where no gap exists, a note of continued compliance is recorded. Where a gap exists, the process drafts a new Compliance Requirement stating the exact action required and the deadline for implementation. The draft is presented to the accountable academic and, if approved, added to the register. If the required action changes a Data Management Plan, the plan is updated and re-approved before the compliance date. The process then issues a Compliance Assessment Report listing the gap, the corrective action, and the date of verification. When the change affects open access publication, the process sets an Open Access Compliance Record flag for all affected Research Outputs.

### Produces
Compliance Requirement: issued when the new government condition has been translated into a specific internal control and assigned an owner. Compliance Assessment Report: issued after each gap check, recording the assessed activity, the gap found, and the decision taken. Corrective Action Plan: issued when a gap requires changes to research practice; it lists actions, owners, and completion dates.

### Outcome
All active research activity is demonstrably aligned with the current set of funding, data protection, and open access obligations.

### Fails when
A new Government Policy arrives and the process does not complete gap scoring before the next Research Output is deposited; as a result, non-compliant outputs are released and the institution breaches funder conditions.

Name: Research Dataset Mgt
Documentation:
### Identity
Work here catalogues, stores, and controls access to research data so that datasets remain findable, citable, and compliant with data management obligations.

### Trigger
The arrival of a new Research Data deposit from a research activity, when the producing project has an active Data Management Plan.

### Consumes
Research Data supplies the raw data files and accompanying description of how they were produced. Data Management Plan supplies the storage location, retention period, and access restrictions agreed for that dataset. Metadata Record supplies the descriptive fields to be confirmed and extended during deposit.

### Steps
On arrival, the Research Data is checked for completeness against the Data Management Plan. The process then extracts or confirms the Metadata Record, including creator, funder, date, and file format. The dataset is deposited into the research data repository and assigned a persistent identifier. Access controls are applied according to the Data Management Plan, and an Access Control Record is issued. If the dataset contains personal data, a data protection check is run and the access level is set to restricted. The process records the deposit in the repository and issues a Dataset Repository Entry.

### Produces
Dataset Repository Entry: issued when the dataset is stored and described, establishing its discovery point. Access Control Record: issued when access restrictions are set, establishing who may retrieve the data. Metadata Record: issued when the descriptive fields are confirmed, establishing the dataset's citable description.

### Outcome
Research data is stored under active access control and is discoverable and citable via the repository.

### Fails when
The completeness check is skipped and an incomplete Research Data deposit is given a persistent identifier; downstream reuse fails because files are missing.

Name: Research Funding Identification
Documentation:
### Identity
Work here scans the external funding landscape and identifies which funding calls match the institution's research strengths.

### Trigger
The arrival of a new Research Funding Opportunity from a funder, when no existing Research Opportunity has been recorded for that call.

### Consumes
Research Funding Opportunity supplies the call details, eligibility, deadline, and funding amount. Research Strategy supplies the institutional priorities and target research areas. Research Capability Profile supplies the current expertise and track record of academic staff.

### Steps
The new Research Funding Opportunity is parsed into its eligibility, scope, and deadline. The process then maps the scope against the Research Strategy to confirm alignment. For aligned calls, the Research Capability Profile is searched for researchers whose expertise matches the call. A shortlist of potential applicants is produced and a Researcher Alert is sent to each named academic.

### Produces
Researcher Alert: issued to each matched academic, establishing awareness of the opportunity and the application deadline. Research Opportunity: issued when an aligned call is recorded, establishing the institution's interest in the call.

### Outcome
The institution has a current list of funding calls that align with its research strategy and are assigned to named potential applicants.

### Fails when
The mapping step uses an outdated Research Strategy and a misaligned call is circulated; staff apply to funding outside institutional priority and the application fails.

Name: Research Funds Mgt
Documentation:
### Identity
Work here controls the financial management of awarded research funds, ensuring spend aligns with the award terms and that funder financial reports are produced on schedule.

### Trigger
The arrival of a Research Award Notice, when the institution has accepted the award and established a Research Budget for the project.

### Consumes
Research Award Notice supplies the approved budget, spending rules, and reporting dates. Research Budget supplies the internal plan for spend across cost categories and periods. Research Expenditure Record supplies the actual committed and paid spend from financial systems. Research Funder Report supplies the template and prior submissions for financial progress. Research Contract supplies the legal obligation to report and any cost eligibility restrictions.

### Steps
The Research Award Notice is logged and its financial terms are extracted into the Research Budget. The process then sets up spend categories, cost centres, and approval limits. Each month, Research Expenditure Records are reconciled against the Research Budget and a Budget Variance Report is produced. If the variance exceeds the permitted tolerance, the process triggers a Budget Review; the review decides whether to reallocate funds or request a funder variation. The variation request is sent and, if approved, the Research Budget is updated. At each funder reporting date, the process assembles the Research Funder Report including expenditure to date, commitments, and forecast. The report is checked against the Research Award Notice terms and, if compliant, submitted. If non-compliant, the report is returned for correction before submission.

### Produces
Budget Variance Report: issued each reconciliation, establishing the difference between planned and actual spend. Research Funder Report: issued at each reporting date, establishing the financial position against the award. Research Budget: updated after any variation, establishing the current approved spending plan.

### Outcome
Research funds are spent within the award terms and every funder financial report is accurate and submitted on time.

### Fails when
The monthly reconciliation misses an overspend and the next Research Funder Report is submitted without correction; the funder reclaims funds and future awards are withheld.

Name: Research Infrastructure Mgt
Documentation:
### Identity
This process maintains the physical and digital research estate so that booked facilities and equipment are available when research activity needs them. It allocates existing assets and repairs those that fail.

### Trigger
The arrival of a Research Infrastructure Request from an academic unit, when the requested asset is not currently assigned to another project.

### Consumes
Research Infrastructure Request supplies the required asset, preferred dates, and the research purpose. Research Infrastructure Asset supplies the current inventory location, condition status, and existing booking commitments. Research Equipment Record supplies the maintenance history and operating status for each requested item. Facility Booking supplies the current allocation diary showing which assets are already reserved.

### Steps
The request is checked against the Research Infrastructure Asset register to confirm the asset exists and is functional. If the asset is unavailable due to prior booking, the request is returned with alternative dates. If functional, the process creates a Facility Booking for the requested period and updates the Research Infrastructure Asset to show reserved status. At the end of the booking, the process records usage and any fault in the Research Equipment Record. A fault triggers a maintenance order and changes the asset status to unavailable until repair is completed.

### Produces
Facility Booking: issued when an asset is reserved for a specific period, establishing the requester's right to use it. Research Equipment Record: updated after each booking with usage and fault observations, leaving the record reflecting current condition. Maintenance Order: issued when a fault is recorded, establishing that repair work is authorised.

### Outcome
Research infrastructure is either in use, reserved, or under repair, and no request proceeds without a valid Facility Booking.

### Fails when
The Research Infrastructure Asset register is not updated at booking time and two projects receive the same Facility Booking; downstream research activity stalls because the asset is double-booked.

Name: Research Opportunity Analysis
Documentation:
### Identity
Work here evaluates the feasibility and strategic fit of research opportunities before resources are committed.

### Trigger
The arrival of a Research Opportunity from the scanning or collaboration activity, when the opportunity has not yet been assessed.

### Consumes
Research Opportunity supplies the call or proposal details, deadline, and expected outcomes. Research Capability Profile supplies the available expertise, facilities, and track record. Research Strategy supplies the institutional priorities that the opportunity must serve.

### Steps
The Research Opportunity is scored against the Research Strategy for alignment. The process then checks the Research Capability Profile to confirm sufficient expertise and capacity. If capacity is missing, the process records a capacity gap and either rejects the opportunity or proposes a collaboration. A feasibility assessment is produced, covering budget, timeline, and risk. The process issues an Opportunity Assessment Report with a Go/No-Go Decision.

### Produces
Opportunity Assessment Report: issued when the evaluation is complete, establishing the evidence and recommendation. Go/No-Go Decision: issued as the final call, establishing whether the institution will pursue the opportunity.

### Outcome
No research opportunity proceeds without a documented feasibility assessment and explicit decision.

### Fails when
The capacity check is skipped and an opportunity is marked Go despite insufficient staff; the subsequent application fails or the project stalls.

Name: Research Output Mgt
Documentation:
### Identity
Work here validates, deposits, and assigns metadata to research outputs so each output is recorded as an institutionally owned research asset.

### Trigger
The arrival of a Research Final Report from a research activity, when the underlying research has concluded.

### Consumes
Research Final Report supplies the completed findings and the evidence that the research activity ended. Research Output supplies the draft version of the output to be validated and deposited. Data Management Plan supplies the required storage and open access conditions for the output. Open Access Compliance Record supplies the funder-required embargo or licence terms.

### Steps
The Research Final Report is checked for completeness against the output description. The draft Research Output is then validated against quality, format, and metadata requirements. If validation fails, the output is returned to the originator with a Correction Notice. If validation passes, the output is deposited in the institutional repository. The process then applies the open access conditions from the Data Management Plan and creates or updates the Open Access Compliance Record to show compliance. A persistent identifier is assigned and the output's Metadata Record is updated. The process issues the validated Research Output.

### Produces
Research Output: issued when the output has passed validation and been deposited, establishing it as a citable research asset. Open Access Compliance Record: issued or updated when the deposit meets the funder's open access mandate, establishing the evidence of compliance. Metadata Record: issued when descriptive fields are confirmed, establishing discoverability.

### Outcome
Every completed research activity has a validated, deposited output with a compliance record.

### Fails when
The validation step approves an output that is missing the required data access statement; the Open Access Compliance Record is then incorrect and the institution is non-compliant.

Name: Research Output Reporting
Documentation:
### Identity
Work here assembles the institution's research output and publication records into external reports required by funders and regulators.

### Trigger
The arrival of a reporting deadline, when the institution has accumulated Research Outputs and Research Publications for the reporting period.

### Consumes
Research Output supplies the validated and deposited outputs to be reported. Research Publication supplies the published records and their open access status. Research Funder Report supplies the template and required fields for the specific funder. Open Access Compliance Record supplies the compliance evidence for each publication.

### Steps
The process collects all Research Outputs and Research Publications created during the reporting period. Each item is checked against the Research Funder Report template to ensure all required fields are present. Missing fields trigger a request to the owning researcher for completion. The populated Research Funder Report is submitted to the funder before the deadline.

### Produces
Research Funder Report: issued as the completed submission, establishing the institution's formal reporting of research outputs.

### Outcome
The institution has fulfilled its research output reporting obligations for the period.

### Fails when
The report is submitted with missing Open Access Compliance Records and the funder rejects the return; the institution is recorded as non-compliant.

Name: Research Prioritisation
Documentation:
### Identity
Work here ranks competing research proposals and allocates scarce institutional resources to those with highest strategic and return potential.

### Trigger
The arrival of a set of Research Proposals at a prioritisation round, when available Research Budget is less than total requested.

### Consumes
Research Proposal supplies the objectives, expected outputs, and requested resources. Research Strategy supplies the institutional priority areas and success measures. Research Budget supplies the total available allocation for the round. Research Performance Report supplies past success rates and return from prior proposals.

### Steps
Each Research Proposal is scored against the Research Strategy using predetermined criteria. The process then weights the score by past performance from the Research Performance Report to adjust for delivery risk. A ranked list is produced and the available Research Budget is allocated down the list until exhausted. Proposals that fail to receive allocation are recorded as unfunded. The process issues a Prioritisation Decision for each proposal and updates the Research Portfolio Plan.

### Produces
Prioritisation Decision: issued for each proposal, establishing its rank and whether it receives resources. Research Portfolio Plan: updated with the chosen and rejected proposals, establishing the institutional research portfolio for the period.

### Outcome
Research resources are allocated to the highest-priority proposals and the portfolio reflects strategic choices.

### Fails when
The scoring weights are out of date and a low-priority proposal receives funding; a high-priority proposal is left unfunded and institutional targets are missed.

Name: Research Production
Documentation:
### Identity
Work here executes the funded research activity from award acceptance to completion, producing the research results and the final report required by the funder.

### Trigger
The arrival of a Research Award Notice from a funder, when the institution has an approved Research Proposal and an active Research Budget for the project.

### Consumes
Research Award Notice supplies the funder's formal commitment, funding amount, and reporting conditions. Research Proposal supplies the original objectives, methodology, and timeline against which delivery is measured. Research Budget supplies the financial allocation and spending plan. Data Management Plan supplies the required data collection and storage protocols. Research Contract supplies the legal terms including intellectual property and reporting obligations.

### Steps
The Research Award Notice is logged and matched to the Research Proposal. The process then allocates the Research Budget to cost centres and appoints a project lead. The project lead initiates the research activity, following the methodology in the Research Proposal. At each scheduled milestone, a Research Progress Report is produced and checked against the timeline. Deviations from the timeline or budget trigger a Project Review; if the review decides to continue, the timeline is revised and approved. Data collected during the activity is stored under the Data Management Plan and issued as Research Data. When the work is complete, the process assembles the Research Final Report and verifies that all funder conditions have been met. If the final report is incomplete, it is returned for revision before submission.

### Produces
Research Data: issued as the collected datasets are deposited under the Data Management Plan, establishing the raw evidence of the research. Research Final Report: issued when all milestones are complete and the funder conditions are met, establishing the formal deliverable. Research Progress Report: issued at each milestone, establishing the current status and variance from plan.

### Outcome
The funded research project is executed, its data is stored, and the final report is ready for output validation and funder submission.

### Fails when
The final report is submitted without completing a milestone deviation review; the funder rejects the final claim and the Research Award Notice is not closed.

Name: Research Programme Development
Documentation:
### Identity
Work here shapes broad research ideas into structured programme plans and, where appropriate, into submitted research proposals.

### Trigger
The arrival of a Research Programme Idea from a senior academic, when the idea aligns with a priority area in the Research Strategy.

### Consumes
Research Programme Idea supplies the initial concept, target research question, and potential funders. Research Strategy supplies the institutional priorities and resource boundaries. Research Capability Profile supplies the available staff, facilities, and track record. Research Performance Report supplies past programme outcomes and success rates. Research Budget supplies the indicative funding envelope for programme development.

### Steps
The Research Programme Idea is logged and scored against the Research Strategy. If it fails alignment, the idea is rejected and recorded. If aligned, the process assembles a programme team from the Research Capability Profile. The team defines the programme's objectives, work packages, milestones, and required resources. A Research Programme Plan is drafted and reviewed by the relevant research committee. The plan is approved or returned for revision. Once approved, the process identifies suitable funding calls and drafts a Research Proposal based on the plan. The proposal is approved and submitted. If the proposal is rejected, the process records the rejection and decides whether to revise and resubmit or close the idea.

### Produces
Research Programme Plan: issued when the idea is structured and approved, establishing the agreed scope, resources, and timeline. Research Proposal: issued when a funding call is targeted, establishing the formal application for external funding.

### Outcome
Priority research ideas are translated into approved programme plans and, where funded, into submitted proposals.

### Fails when
The Research Programme Plan is approved without checking the Research Capability Profile and a key staff member is already committed elsewhere; the programme stalls and the proposal is withdrawn.

Name: Research Programme Performance Mgt
Documentation:
### Identity
Work here reviews the performance of research programmes against institutional targets and intervenes when programmes drift from planned outcomes.

### Trigger
The arrival of a Research Performance Report at the end of a reporting period, when the report shows actual results against target.

### Consumes
Research Performance Report supplies the completed outputs, income, and milestones for each programme. Research Strategy supplies the target outcomes and priorities for the period. Research Budget supplies the financial plan against which spend is evaluated.

### Steps
The Research Performance Report is parsed to extract output, income, and milestone data for each programme. The process then compares each metric against the Research Strategy targets. Programmes that meet or exceed target are recorded as on track. Programmes that miss target trigger a variance analysis to identify the cause. The process issues a Performance Review naming the underperforming programme and the required corrective action. If the cause is financial, the Research Budget is examined and a reallocation is proposed.

### Produces
Performance Review: issued for each programme, establishing its current performance status and any variance. Corrective Action Plan: issued when a programme is off target, establishing the actions and owners required to recover performance.

### Outcome
Research programme performance is measured and every off-target programme has an agreed recovery plan.

### Fails when
The Research Performance Report is received but no variance analysis is run; a failing programme continues without correction and institutional research income falls below target.

Name: Research Publication Mgt
Documentation:
### Identity
Work here moves validated research outputs through the publication submission and open access process so that every publication is compliant and recorded.

### Trigger
The arrival of a validated Research Output from the output management process, when the output has an assigned persistent identifier and an Open Access Compliance Record.

### Consumes
Research Output supplies the final version of the research finding to be published. Open Access Compliance Record supplies the funder-required open access route, embargo, and licence. Data Management Plan supplies the publisher's requirements for data availability statements. Copyright Transfer Agreement supplies the author's rights retained or transferred to the publisher.

### Steps
The Research Output is matched to its Open Access Compliance Record to determine the required publication route. The process then selects a target journal or publisher and prepares the submission package including the manuscript and data availability statement. The package is submitted and the publisher's decision is awaited; if rejected, the process revises and resubmits to another outlet. When accepted, the Copyright Transfer Agreement is reviewed to ensure open access compliance. If the agreement conflicts with the Open Access Compliance Record, the process negotiates a compliant licence or selects another publisher. On final acceptance, the output is published and the process issues a Research Publication. The Open Access Compliance Record is updated to show published status and the persistent identifier.

### Produces
Research Publication: issued when the output is accepted and published, establishing the citable public record. Open Access Compliance Record: updated to show published status and licence, establishing final compliance evidence. Publication Record: issued to log the publisher, date, and open access route, establishing an audit trail.

### Outcome
Every research output that reaches publication is published under a compliant open access licence and its publication is recorded.

### Fails when
The Copyright Transfer Agreement is signed without checking against the Open Access Compliance Record and the publication is not open access; the institution breaches the funder mandate and the publication is excluded from the next assessment.

Name: Research Quality Mgt
Documentation:
### Identity
Work here assures that research activity meets ethical, integrity, and quality standards before and during execution.

### Trigger
The arrival of a Research Ethics Application from a researcher, when the proposed research involves human participants, personal data, or sensitive material.

### Consumes
Research Ethics Application supplies the study design, participant information, consent processes, and risk assessments. Research Protocol supplies the planned methodology and data handling steps. Data Management Plan supplies the privacy and storage controls for any personal data. Audit Findings supplies prior nonconformities from earlier reviews of similar research.

### Steps
The Research Ethics Application is checked for completeness and for inclusion of all required approvals. The process then reviews the Research Protocol against the institution's ethical framework, focusing on consent, risk, and vulnerable participants. If the application has gaps, it is returned with a Request for Revision. If complete, the review panel decides whether to approve, require modifications, or reject. Approval issues an Ethics Approval with conditions that are recorded against the research project. During the research, a Quality Review Report is produced at each milestone, drawing on Audit Findings to verify that conditions are being met. Any nonconformity triggers a Corrective Action Request.

### Produces
Ethics Approval: issued when the research design meets ethical standards, establishing the permission to proceed. Quality Review Report: issued at each milestone, establishing the current state of quality and ethics compliance. Corrective Action Request: issued when a nonconformity is found, establishing the required fix and deadline.

### Outcome
All active research involving sensitive subjects has an Ethics Approval and is periodically reviewed for quality.

### Fails when
The Ethics Approval is issued without checking the consent process and a participant complaint arises; the research is suspended and the institution is investigated.

Name: Researcher Performance Mgt
Documentation:
### Identity
Work here assesses individual researcher performance and agrees development actions to improve research capability.

### Trigger
The start of the annual appraisal cycle, when each researcher has a Researcher Performance Record for the previous period.

### Consumes
Researcher Performance Record supplies the research outputs, funding success, and impact activity for the period. Training Completion Record supplies the completed development activities since the last appraisal. Research Output supplies the evidence of published work and its quality.

### Steps
The Researcher Performance Record and Research Output are reviewed together to measure against the institution's research standards. The Training Completion Record is checked to confirm required development was completed. A Performance Appraisal meeting is held where the reviewer and researcher agree on strengths and areas for improvement. The process then issues a Development Plan with agreed training or workload changes for the next period.

### Produces
Performance Appraisal: issued after the meeting, establishing the recorded assessment and agreed objectives. Development Plan: issued with the appraisal, establishing the specific actions and funding allocated to development.

### Outcome
Each researcher has a current appraisal and an agreed plan for improving performance.

### Fails when
The Training Completion Record is not checked and a required training course is missed; the researcher's development plan does not address the gap and performance stalls.

Name: Researcher Training & Development
Documentation:
### Identity
Work here identifies and addresses the development needs of research staff to maintain research capability.

### Trigger
The arrival of a Researcher Training Needs Assessment at the start of an appraisal cycle, when the researcher does not have a current Training Plan.

### Consumes
Researcher Training Needs Assessment supplies the identified skill gaps against the research strategy. Training Completion Record supplies prior completed training and current competencies.

### Steps
The training needs assessment is analysed to prioritise required skills. A Training Plan is drafted and agreed with the researcher and line manager. The plan is scheduled against available training dates. As training is completed, the Training Completion Record is updated.

### Produces
Training Plan: issued when the needs are prioritised and agreed, establishing the development route. Training Completion Record: updated after each course, establishing progress.

### Outcome
Every research staff member has a current Training Plan and an accurate completion record.

### Fails when
The Training Needs Assessment is not updated and an obsolete Training Plan is issued; the researcher misses required training and fails a performance review.

Name: Risk Mgt
Documentation:
### Identity
This process identifies, assesses, and treats the institution's strategic, operational, and compliance risks, and reports the aggregate risk position to the governing body. It is the part of the capability that keeps risk within the approved appetite.

### Trigger
The discovery of a new risk, an incident, or a scheduled risk review triggers the process, when the current Risk Register no longer reflects the actual exposure.

### Consumes
Risk Register supplies the current set of risks, their owners, and existing treatments. Incident Report supplies details of events that have caused loss or harm. Strategic Objective supplies the objectives against which risk impact is judged. Risk Appetite Statement supplies the amount and type of risk the institution is willing to accept.

### Steps
First the process identifies the new or changed risk and assigns an owner. It analyses the likelihood and impact using defined criteria. It compares the assessed risk against the Risk Appetite Statement. If the risk is outside appetite, it develops treatment options and selects one. It assigns treatment actions with owners and due dates. It updates the Risk Register with the new risk status. It reports the risk profile to the risk committee at the next scheduled meeting.

### Produces
Risk Assessment records the likelihood, impact, and risk rating for each risk considered. Risk Treatment Plan records the selected treatment actions, owners, and deadlines. Updated Risk Register records the changed risk posture after treatment.

### Outcome
All identified risks have an assessed rating, a treatment decision, and an owner; the aggregate residual risk is within the approved appetite.

### Fails when
The Risk Appetite Statement is absent or ambiguous, because risks cannot be judged as acceptable or unacceptable and the process issues no treatment decisions, leaving exposure unmanaged.

Name: Scholarship & Bursary Mgt
Documentation:
### Identity
The work of awarding and paying scholarships and bursaries to students.

### Trigger
A Scholarship Application or Bursary Eligibility List is received.

### Consumes
Scholarship Application supplies the student's need and merit evidence. Bursary Eligibility List supplies students meeting need criteria. Scholarship Budget supplies available funds. Award Criteria supplies the ranking rules.

### Steps
Applications are checked for eligibility against Award Criteria. Eligible candidates are ranked by merit or need. A Scholarship Award is approved for selected students. The award is recorded on the Student Fee Account. Payments are made or fee reductions applied. A Scholarship Payment Record is created. Students not selected are notified.

### Produces
Scholarship Award. Scholarship Payment Record. Student Fee Account update.

### Outcome
Scholarships and bursaries are allocated within budget to eligible students.

### Fails when
Scholarship Budget is insufficient for the number of eligible applicants, leaving some without support.

Name: Space Utilisation
Documentation:
### Identity
Measurement and management of how space is used across the estate, including allocation, utilisation surveys, and reallocation.

### Trigger
The arrival of a space utilisation survey schedule or a space request from a department.

### Consumes
Space Request supplies the department's requirement and intended use. Space Inventory supplies the current room list, capacities, and owners. Space Utilisation Survey supplies measured occupancy and usage data.

### Steps
The process records space requests and validates them against policy. It reviews current utilisation data to identify underused space. It proposes reallocation or new allocation. It updates the space inventory with ownership changes. It publishes allocations and monitors occupancy. If demand exceeds supply, a waiting list or prioritisation rule is applied. Survey results are reviewed annually to adjust the space strategy.

### Produces
Space Allocation Decision states which room is assigned to which unit. Space Utilisation Report records measured occupancy against capacity. Space Inventory Update records any change to room ownership or usage type.

### Outcome
The institution uses its space efficiently, with demand matched to available capacity and underused space reallocated.

### Fails when
Space Inventory is outdated or departments do not report changes, causing double bookings and wasted spaces.

Name: Sport & Recreation Mgt
Documentation:
### Identity
Management of sport and recreation facilities and programmes, including bookings, memberships, and events.

### Trigger
The arrival of a facility booking or a programme registration.

### Consumes
Facility Booking Request supplies the facility and time. Membership Application supplies the applicant's details. Programme Schedule supplies the organised activities.

### Steps
The process checks availability. It confirms bookings. It issues memberships. It runs programmes. It maintains facilities. It manages safety and supervision. It collects fees. It reports on usage. If a facility is double-booked, it resolves the conflict.

### Produces
Facility Booking Confirmation states the reserved slot. Membership Card states the member's access. Programme Attendance Record records participants.

### Outcome
The community has access to sport and recreation, contributing to well-being.

### Fails when
A facility is not maintained, causing injury or closure.

Name: Staff Absence Mgt
Documentation:
### Identity
Management of employee absence, including sick leave, annual leave, and other leave types.

### Trigger
The arrival of an absence notification from an employee or manager.

### Consumes
Absence Notification supplies the dates, type, and reason. Employee Record supplies the employee's leave entitlement and sickness history. Leave Policy supplies the rules for each absence type.

### Steps
The process records the absence. It checks against the employee's remaining entitlement. It approves or queries the absence. It monitors sickness triggers and patterns. It initiates return-to-work interviews for long-term sickness. It refers to occupational health where required. It updates the employee's absence record. It reports absence data to management.

### Produces
Absence Record states the approved absence and dates. Return to Work Interview Record states the outcome of the interview. Absence Trigger Alert notifies the manager when an employee reaches a policy threshold.

### Outcome
Absence is recorded and managed within policy, and excessive absence is addressed.

### Fails when
Absence records are not maintained, causing entitlement errors and unmanaged absence patterns.

Name: Staff Engagement
Documentation:
### Identity
Staff engagement activities, including surveys, town halls, and feedback mechanisms. It measures and improves employee engagement.

### Trigger
The arrival of a staff survey results or a scheduled engagement event.

### Consumes
Staff Survey Results supply the engagement scores and comments. Engagement Action Plan supplies the agreed initiatives. Employee Feedback Record supplies ad hoc suggestions.

### Steps
The process analyses survey results. It identifies engagement drivers and low-scoring areas. It develops an action plan with owners. It monitors the implementation of actions. It communicates progress to staff. It runs follow-up pulse surveys. It updates the engagement dashboard. If an action fails, it is re-scoped.

### Produces
Staff Engagement Report states the survey results and trends. Engagement Action Plan states the agreed improvement actions. Engagement Communication informs staff of progress.

### Outcome
The institution understands and improves staff engagement, leading to higher retention and morale.

### Fails when
Engagement survey results are ignored, causing disengagement and turnover.

Name: Staff Record & Details Mgt
Documentation:
### Identity
Maintenance of employee personal and job records, including changes to roles, contacts, and documentation.

### Trigger
The arrival of a change to an employee's details or a new employee joining.

### Consumes
Employee Record update request supplies the new or changed details. Employment Contract supplies the initial terms. Personal Document supplies identity and right-to-work evidence.

### Steps
The process validates the change request against the employee's file. It updates the HR system. It files the supporting evidence. It notifies payroll and other dependent areas. It confirms the change to the employee. It checks for data protection compliance. It archives old records according to retention rules. If the change affects pay or benefits, it triggers the remuneration process.

### Produces
Employee Record Update states the new data and effective date. HR System Change Confirmation records the successful update. Data Protection Compliance Record states the basis for processing.

### Outcome
Employee records are accurate, current, and compliant, enabling reliable HR decisions.

### Fails when
A change is not recorded or is recorded incorrectly, causing payroll errors and legal risk.

Name: Staff Recruitment
Documentation:
### Identity
End-to-end recruitment, from vacancy creation through selection to offer and onboarding.

### Trigger
The arrival of a Vacancy Request from a hiring manager.

### Consumes
Vacancy Request supplies the role, salary, and justification. Job Description supplies the duties and person specification. Employment Application supplies candidate information.

### Steps
The process validates the vacancy against budget and workforce plan. It advertises the role. It shortlists applications against the person specification. It arranges interviews and assessments. It selects the preferred candidate. It conducts right-to-work and reference checks. It issues an offer letter and contract. It manages the onboarding process. If the preferred candidate declines, the next candidate is approached. All rejected candidates are informed.

### Produces
Job Advertisement states the vacancy details. Interview Assessment Record scores each candidate. Employment Contract states the agreed terms with the selected candidate.

### Outcome
The institution hires qualified staff into approved roles, meeting authorisation and compliance requirements.

### Fails when
A vacancy cannot be filled because no suitable candidates apply, causing the role to remain vacant and work to be redistributed.

Name: Strategic Plan Development
Documentation:
### Identity
This process develops the institution's five-year Strategic Plan by translating the strategic vision into measurable objectives and resource commitments. It is the part of the capability that converts direction into an approved plan.

### Trigger
A mandate from the governing body to develop or renew the Strategic Plan triggers the process, when the current plan has expired or the vision has changed.

### Consumes
Strategic Vision supplies the long-term aspirations and priorities. Horizon Scan Report supplies the external environment assumptions. Stakeholder Consultation Document supplies feedback from staff, students, and external partners. Financial Forecast supplies the projected income and expenditure over the plan period.

### Steps
First the process establishes the planning framework and timetable. It drafts strategic objectives and priorities based on the Strategic Vision and Horizon Scan Report. It consults stakeholders and records their responses. It reconciles the draft with the Financial Forecast to ensure affordability. It refines the objectives and sets measurable targets. It prepares the Strategic Plan along with the Strategic Objectives and Key Performance Indicators. It submits the plan to the governing body for approval. It addresses any conditions or amendments requested by the governing body before final approval.

### Produces
Strategic Plan records the approved five-year objectives, priorities, and targets. Strategic Objectives records the cascade of objectives to portfolios. Financial Plan records the resource envelope aligned to the Strategic Plan.

### Outcome
The institution has an approved Strategic Plan with measurable objectives and a matching financial plan, endorsed by the governing body.

### Fails when
The Financial Forecast does not reconcile with the draft objectives, because the plan cannot be approved and the institution continues without a current five-year plan, leaving budget and performance management unanchored.

Name: Strategic Plan Mgt
Documentation:
### Identity
This process keeps the approved Strategic Plan current by reviewing progress and incorporating material changes to objectives, targets, or priorities. It is the part of the capability that ensures the plan remains a live management instrument.

### Trigger
An annual review date, a material change in the external environment, or a performance shortfall triggers the process, when the existing plan needs adjustment.

### Consumes
Strategic Plan supplies the current objectives, targets, and priorities. Performance Report supplies actual progress against those targets. Risk Register supplies the risks that may affect future achievement. Horizon Scan Report supplies any new external assumptions.

### Steps
First the process reviews the actual performance against each Strategic Objective. It identifies objectives where targets are no longer achievable or no longer appropriate. It evaluates proposed changes against the Risk Register and Horizon Scan Report. It prepares a draft update to the Strategic Plan. It consults the governing body or its committee on the changes. It approves the update and issues the revised Strategic Plan.

### Produces
Strategic Plan Update records the specific changes approved and the rationale for each. Strategic Plan Review Decision records the governing body's confirmation or rejection of each change.

### Outcome
The Strategic Plan remains aligned with current performance, risk, and external assumptions, and each change is formally approved.

### Fails when
The Performance Report is missing or materially inaccurate, because the review cannot determine where the plan is off track and changes are either not made or made without evidence, leading to continued use of an outdated plan.

Name: Strategic Reporting
Documentation:
### Identity
This process prepares the institution's strategic and annual reports for the governing body, regulators, and the public, synthesising performance and governance outcomes. It is the part of the capability that discharges accountability.

### Trigger
The end of the academic year or a regulator's reporting deadline triggers the process, when the institution must report its performance and governance.

### Consumes
Performance Dashboard supplies the annual KPI outcomes. Governance Decisions supplies the material decisions taken by the governing body. Statutory Filings supplies the returns already submitted to regulators. Financial Statements supplies the audited financial position.

### Steps
First the process collects the required content from the named sources. It drafts the narrative sections of the Strategic Report. It cross-checks the performance claims against the Performance Dashboard and Financial Statements. It obtains approval from the accountable executive and the governing body. It then publishes the report according to the reporting deadline.

### Produces
Strategic Report records the institution's performance, strategy, and principal risks for the academic year. Annual Report records the combined financial and non-financial statements for the year.

### Outcome
The governing body and external stakeholders receive a single, approved report that presents the institution's performance and governance accurately.

### Fails when
The Financial Statements are not yet audited, because the Annual Report cannot be approved and the institution misses its statutory publication deadline, risking regulatory sanction.

Name: Strategic Vision Development
Documentation:
### Identity
This process creates the institution's long-term Strategic Vision through engagement with the governing body, staff, and external stakeholders. It is the part of the capability that sets the direction for all subsequent planning.

### Trigger
A request from the governing body or a significant change in the external environment triggers the process, when the existing vision is no longer seen as fit for purpose.

### Consumes
Horizon Scan Report supplies the external trends and uncertainties. Stakeholder Input supplies the values, concerns, and aspirations of staff, students, and partners. Current Strategic Plan supplies the current priorities and constraints.

### Steps
First the process convenes workshops with the governing body and senior leaders. It synthesises the Horizon Scan Report and Stakeholder Input into a set of draft vision statements. It tests the drafts against the Current Strategic Plan to identify contradictions. It selects a preferred vision statement. It validates the vision with the governing body and records the decision.

### Produces
Strategic Vision records the final agreed vision statement and its rationale. Strategic Scenarios records the alternative futures considered and why they were not selected.

### Outcome
The institution has a single agreed Strategic Vision that frames the next Strategic Plan and is owned by the governing body.

### Fails when
The governing body cannot agree on a vision statement, because no Strategic Vision is issued and the subsequent planning cycle has no directional anchor.

Name: Student Application Mgt
Documentation:
### Identity
The work of receiving and processing Student Applications through validation and assessment.

### Trigger
A Student Application is submitted.

### Consumes
Student Application supplies the applicant's details, qualifications and programme choice. Entry Requirements Register supplies the criteria for the programme. Fee Status Questionnaire supplies data for fee classification. Supporting Document supplies transcripts and references.

### Steps
The application is checked for completeness; missing documents are requested. The applicant's qualifications are verified against the Supporting Document. Fee status is assessed from the Fee Status Questionnaire. The application is matched to the programme's Entry Requirements Register. If the applicant meets minimum criteria, an Assessed Application is created with a recommendation. If not, a Rejection Notice is issued. The Assessed Application is forwarded for offer decision. Duplicate applications are identified and merged.

### Produces
Assessed Application. Application Acknowledgement. Rejection Notice.

### Outcome
Every submitted Student Application has a validated and assessed outcome.

### Fails when
Required evidence is missing and the applicant does not respond, leaving the application incomplete.

Name: Student Engagement & Retention
Documentation:
### Identity
The work of monitoring student engagement and intervening to retain at-risk students.

### Trigger
An Engagement Alert is raised by attendance or performance data.

### Consumes
Student Engagement Data supplies absence and participation records. Student Results Record supplies academic performance. Student Record supplies contact details. Retention Policy supplies the intervention thresholds.

### Steps
