The data is analysed to identify at-risk students. Each student's situation is reviewed. An intervention is designed (e.g., tutoring, wellbeing referral, study skills). The intervention is delivered. Follow-up is scheduled. The outcome is recorded. A Retention Report summarises the cohort.

### Produces
Engagement Intervention Record. Retention Report.

### Outcome
At-risk students receive timely intervention to support continuation.

### Fails when
Engagement Alerts are not acted on and students withdraw without intervention.

Name: Student Exceptional Factors Misconduct / Appeal Mgt
Documentation:
### Identity
The work of managing student appeals, misconduct cases and exceptional circumstances affecting assessment.

### Trigger
A Student Appeal or Student Misconduct Case is submitted.

### Consumes
Student Appeal Case supplies the grounds and evidence. Student Misconduct Case supplies the alleged breach and evidence. Student Results Record supplies the assessment context. Academic Policy supplies the rules for handling.

### Steps
The case is logged and assigned to a case officer. The evidence is reviewed. For misconduct, a hearing panel is convened; for appeals, the grounds are checked against permissible criteria. The panel or officer issues a Case Decision. If the decision upholds the appeal, the Student Results Record is amended. If misconduct is confirmed, a penalty is applied according to Academic Policy. The student is notified. An appeal against the Case Decision is lodged and triggers a review by a higher panel. The final outcome is recorded.

### Produces
Case Decision. Student Appeal Outcome. Student Misconduct Outcome. Updated Student Results Record where applicable.

### Outcome
Student cases are resolved fairly and records reflect final decisions.

### Fails when
Evidence is incomplete and the panel cannot reach a decision, leaving the case unresolved.

Name: Student Financial Administration
Documentation:
### Identity
The work of managing student fee accounts, payments, debt and refunds.

### Trigger
A Student Fee Payment or Student Fee Invoice is received or due.

### Consumes
Student Enrolment supplies the fee liability. Student Fee Account supplies the current balance. Student Fee Payment supplies the amount paid and method. Payment Schedule supplies the due dates.

### Steps
The payment is matched to the Student Fee Account. If the payment meets the liability, the account is marked as settled. If it is partial, the outstanding balance is recorded. Invoices are issued for unpaid balances. Payment plans are set up where eligible. Refunds for overpayments are processed and recorded. Debt collection procedures are initiated for accounts in arrears beyond a threshold. The Student Fee Account is updated with each transaction.

### Produces
Updated Student Fee Account. Student Fee Invoice. Payment Receipt. Refund Record.

### Outcome
Student fee accounts are accurate and current.

### Fails when
Payments cannot be matched to an account and the debt remains unresolved, causing fee collection to stop.

Name: Student Financial Advice
Documentation:
### Identity
The work of advising students on managing finances and funding.

### Trigger
A student books a financial advice appointment.

### Consumes
Student Enrolment supplies the fee status. Student Fee Account supplies the current balance. Funding Body Guidance supplies eligibility rules. Budget Template supplies the planning format.

### Steps
The advisor reviews the student's financial situation. Options are explained. A budget is created using the Budget Template. A referral for a payment plan is made. The advice is recorded. Debt advice is provided if needed.

### Produces
Financial Advice Record. Payment Plan Referral.

### Outcome
Students receive advice to manage their finances.

### Fails when
The advisor cannot access the Student Fee Account and cannot advise accurately.

Name: Student Health & Wellbeing
Documentation:
### Identity
The work of providing health and wellbeing support to students.

### Trigger
A student self-refers or is referred for wellbeing support.

### Consumes
Student Health & Wellbeing Referral supplies the presenting issue. Student Record supplies the student's history. Risk Assessment supplies the risk level. Wellbeing Support Plan supplies the existing plan.

### Steps
The referral is triaged. If urgent, immediate support is arranged. A support plan is developed with the student. Ongoing sessions are delivered. The plan is reviewed. Safeguarding concerns are escalated. The Student Record is updated with the support activity.

### Produces
Wellbeing Support Plan. Risk Assessment Update. Updated Student Record.

### Outcome
Students receive appropriate wellbeing support and risk is managed.

### Fails when
A high-risk referral lacks capacity and the student is not seen, leaving risk unmanaged.

Name: Student Induction Mgt
Documentation:
### Identity
The work of delivering induction activities for new students.

### Trigger
A batch of Student Enrolments is created for a new intake.

### Consumes
Student Enrolment supplies the new student list. Induction Schedule supplies the planned activities. Welcome Pack supplies orientation materials. IT Account Setup supplies the credentials.

### Steps
New students are invited to induction events. Attendance is recorded. Activities include library, IT and safety briefing. The Welcome Pack is distributed. Completion is recorded in the Student Record. A campus tour is conducted. A follow-up survey is issued.

### Produces
Induction Attendance Record. Updated Student Record. Induction Feedback Survey.

### Outcome
New students are oriented to institutional services and expectations.

### Fails when
The Induction Schedule is not published in time and students do not attend, leaving orientation incomplete.

Name: Student Mobility
Documentation:
### Identity
The work of approving and recording student participation in exchange or study abroad placements.

### Trigger
A Student Mobility Application submitted by a student.

### Consumes
Student Enrolment supplies the home programme. Student Mobility Application supplies the proposed host institution and period. Host Institution Agreement supplies the terms of the exchange. Study Plan supplies the intended modules abroad.

### Steps
The application is checked for academic suitability and host availability. The student's Study Plan is agreed to ensure credit transfer. The Host Institution Agreement is signed by both parties. Funding and visa requirements are confirmed. The placement is recorded in the Student Record. While abroad, the student's progress is monitored. On return, transcripts are received and credit is applied.

### Produces
Student Mobility Agreement. Updated Student Record. Credit Transfer Record.

### Outcome
Student mobility is formally approved and academically recognised.

### Fails when
The Host Institution Agreement cannot be finalised or the Study Plan is rejected, blocking the placement.

Name: Student Placement Mgt
Documentation:
### Identity
The work of arranging and monitoring student work placements.

### Trigger
A Student Placement Application is submitted.

### Consumes
Student Enrolment supplies the student's programme. Placement Opportunity supplies available placements. Placement Agreement supplies the terms with the employer. Health & Safety Checklist supplies the required checks.

### Steps
The student's eligibility is checked. The student applies to Placement Opportunities. An interview or selection process occurs. On selection, a Placement Agreement is signed. A placement supervisor is assigned. Health & Safety checks are completed. During the placement, progress is monitored via Placement Reports. On completion, the placement is recorded on the Student Record and credit is applied.

### Produces
Placement Agreement. Placement Progress Report. Updated Student Record. Credit Transfer Record.

### Outcome
Students complete approved placements that contribute to their programme.

### Fails when
No Placement Opportunity is available and the student cannot secure a placement, blocking progression.

Name: Student Record & Details Mgt
Documentation:
### Identity
The work of maintaining the authoritative Student Record, including personal details and academic history.

### Trigger
A Student Details Change Request or an academic decision that alters the record.

### Consumes
Student Details Change Request supplies the new personal information. Academic Decision supplies the results, status or award changes. Student Record supplies the existing record. Supporting Evidence supplies verification documents.

### Steps
The change request is verified against the Supporting Evidence. The new details are checked for consistency. The Student Record is updated. The change is logged in an audit trail. Confirmation is sent to the student. The record is made available to authorised consumers. A periodic reconciliation checks the record for missing or inconsistent fields.

### Produces
Updated Student Record. Student Details Change Confirmation. Audit Trail Entry.

### Outcome
The Student Record is accurate, complete and auditable.

### Fails when
Supporting documents are missing and the change cannot be verified, leaving the record stale.

Name: Student Recruitment Agent Mgt
Documentation:
### Identity
The work of appointing, monitoring and terminating student recruitment agents.

### Trigger
A prospective agent applies for appointment.

### Consumes
Agent Application supplies the agent's credentials. Student Recruitment Agent Contract supplies the agreed terms. Agent Performance Report supplies the evaluation data. Due Diligence Checklist supplies the verification steps.

### Steps
The Agent Application is assessed against institutional criteria. Due diligence is conducted using the Due Diligence Checklist. If approved, a Student Recruitment Agent Contract is issued and signed. The agent is briefed and given recruitment materials. Performance is monitored periodically against the contract. Underperforming agents are warned or terminated. A termination notice is issued if required.

### Produces
Student Recruitment Agent Contract. Agent Appointment Decision. Agent Performance Report.

### Outcome
The institution has a compliant, performing agent network.

### Fails when
Agent due diligence fails or performance falls below contract terms and no replacement is found, reducing international recruitment capacity.

Name: Student Results Mgt
Documentation:
### Identity
The work of aggregating marks, applying progression rules and producing formal results.

### Trigger
All Student Assessment Marks for a module are finalised.

### Consumes
Student Assessment Mark supplies the raw scores. Module Registration supplies the student set. Academic Policy supplies progression and award rules. Results Board Agenda supplies the items for review.

### Steps
Marks are combined per module to produce a Module Result. The module result is checked against progression rules. Students with borderline or exceptional cases are flagged for the Results Board. The Results Board reviews and confirms final Student Results Records. The results are published to students. Students who fail are identified for resit or reassessment. The Student Results Record is stored as the official outcome.

### Produces
Student Results Record. Results Board Decision. Progression Outcome.

### Outcome
Students receive formally approved results and progression status.

### Fails when
Marks are incomplete or contested and the Results Board cannot confirm a result, delaying progression decisions.

Name: Supplier Mgt
Documentation:
### Identity
Ongoing management of supplier relationships, performance, and contracts post-award.

### Trigger
The arrival of a new supplier contract or a supplier performance issue.

### Consumes
Supplier Contract supplies the agreed terms, service levels, and obligations. Supplier Performance Data supplies delivery, quality, and compliance information. Supplier Invoice supplies the billing against the contract.

### Steps
The process registers the supplier and contract terms. It monitors delivery and service performance against agreed levels. It holds regular supplier review meetings. It manages supplier corrective actions for non-performance. It authorises payments based on performance. It handles supplier disputes and escalations. It updates supplier risk ratings. If a supplier fails repeatedly, termination is considered. At contract end, handover and debrief are completed.

### Produces
Supplier Performance Report records the supplier's service delivery against targets. Corrective Action Request states the improvement required from the supplier. Supplier Risk Rating updates the supplier's risk profile.

### Outcome
The institution manages supplier performance actively, resolving issues and ensuring contracted value.

### Fails when
A key supplier underperforms and corrective actions are not enforced, causing service disruption across dependent operations.

Name: Talent Mgt
Documentation:
### Identity
Management of high-potential employees, succession planning, and talent pools.

### Trigger
The arrival of a talent identification review or a succession planning cycle.

### Consumes
Employee Performance Record supplies the performance and potential ratings. Succession Plan supplies the current successors for key roles. Talent Pool Definition supplies the criteria for inclusion.

### Steps
The process identifies high-potential employees using performance and potential data. It reviews current succession plans against future needs. It develops individual development plans for talented staff. It monitors progress and rotates assignments. It updates the talent pool. It reports on readiness for key roles. If a key role has no successor, it triggers targeted development or external search.

### Produces
Talent Pool Update records the current members and their readiness. Individual Development Plan states the agreed development actions. Succession Plan Update records changes to named successors.

### Outcome
The institution has a pipeline of internal talent ready to fill key roles.

### Fails when
Succession planning is not maintained, leaving critical roles unfilled after departures.

Name: Taxation Mgt
Documentation:
### Identity
Institutional tax compliance, including VAT, payroll taxes, and corporate tax obligations.

### Trigger
The arrival of a tax filing deadline or a change in tax legislation.

### Consumes
Transaction Records supply the taxable inputs and outputs for the period. Tax Legislation supplies the rules and rates to apply. Tax Filing Schedule supplies the deadlines for each tax return.

### Steps
The process extracts transaction data and determines taxable amounts. It calculates tax liabilities and input credits. It prepares and reviews tax returns. It obtains sign-off. It submits returns to the relevant tax authority. It makes payments by the due date. It maintains records for audit. If a discrepancy is found, it is investigated and a correction is filed. Changes in legislation are assessed for impact on current processes.

### Produces
Tax Return states the taxable amount and liability for each tax type. Tax Payment Confirmation records the payment made. Tax Correction Filing records any amendment to a previous return.

### Outcome
The institution pays the correct amount of tax on time and maintains compliant records.

### Fails when
Transaction data is incomplete or tax rules are misapplied, causing an underpayment penalty and interest charges.

Name: Teaching & Learning Content Mgt
Documentation:
### Identity
The work of storing, versioning and distributing teaching content.

### Trigger
A Teaching Content Pack is submitted for publication.

### Consumes
Teaching Content Pack supplies the files. Module Registration supplies the target audience. Copyright Record supplies licensing status. Metadata Template supplies the tagging structure.

### Steps
The content is checked for completeness. Version number is assigned. The pack is stored in the repository. Access is granted to enrolled students. Updates are logged. Copyright clearance is verified. Metadata is applied.

### Produces
Stored Teaching Content Pack. Access List. Copyright Clearance Confirmation.

### Outcome
Teaching content is available to students in the correct version.

### Fails when
Copyright clearance is missing and the content cannot be published.

Name: Timetabling Mgt
Documentation:
### Identity
The work of allocating rooms, times and staff to Teaching Sessions and examinations.

### Trigger
Arrival of the Module Registration set for the term.

### Consumes
Module Registration supplies the student cohorts and module demands. Room Inventory supplies available spaces and capacities. Staff Availability Record supplies instructor constraints. Academic Calendar supplies the term and examination windows.

### Steps
The timetabler collects Module Registration data and groups modules by size and delivery mode. Room requests are matched against Room Inventory. Clashes are resolved by reassigning times or rooms. The draft Timetable is published for review. Incomplete or conflicting assignments return for correction. After a review window, the final Timetable is issued. Changes requested after publication are assessed for impact and approved only on documented grounds. A Timetable Change Notice is issued for each approved adjustment.

### Produces
Timetable with final session schedule. Room Booking Confirmation for each allocated space. Timetable Change Notice for any post-publication adjustment.

### Outcome
Teaching Sessions and examinations have conflict-free room and staff assignments.

### Fails when
Room capacity cannot satisfy module demand and no alternative times are accepted, leaving sessions unscheduled.

Name: Training & Development
Documentation:
### Identity
Delivery and administration of training and development, including mandatory, professional, and personal development.

### Trigger
The arrival of a training need identified in a development plan or a scheduled course date.

### Consumes
Development Plan supplies the agreed training needs. Training Course Catalogue supplies the available courses. Employee Record supplies the employee's eligibility and role.

### Steps
The process matches training needs to available courses. It enrols employees and confirms attendance. It delivers or procures the training. It records attendance and completion. It evaluates learning outcomes. It updates the employee's development record. If mandatory training is missed, a follow-up is scheduled. Training spend is tracked.

### Produces
Training Attendance Record states who attended and completed. Training Evaluation Report records the effectiveness and feedback. Development Record Update records the employee's new skill.

### Outcome
The workforce has the skills required by the institution, and compliance training is completed.

### Fails when
Mandatory training is not tracked, causing regulatory non-compliance or skill gaps.

Name: Treasury Mgt
Documentation:
### Identity
Management of cash, investments, borrowings, and working capital. It ensures liquidity and optimises returns.

### Trigger
The arrival of a cash flow forecast update or a significant cash movement.

### Consumes
Cash Flow Forecast supplies expected inflows and outflows for the period. Bank Account Balance supplies the current cash position. Investment Mandate supplies the permitted investment types and limits.

### Steps
The process reviews the cash position and forecast. It identifies surplus or deficit periods. It invests surplus cash within the mandate. It arranges short-term borrowing or drawdowns for deficits. It manages banking relationships and accounts. It monitors counterparty risk. It re-forecasts regularly. If a covenant is at risk, it alerts governance. It records all treasury transactions.

### Produces
Investment Trade Confirmation records an investment made or redeemed. Loan Drawdown Advice states the amount and terms of a borrowing. Cash Position Report states the current and forecast cash balances.

### Outcome
The institution has sufficient liquidity at all times and earns optimal returns within risk limits.

### Fails when
Cash flow forecasting misses a significant payment, causing a liquidity shortfall and inability to meet payroll or supplier obligations.

Name: Vehicle Mgt
Documentation:
### Identity
Management of the institution's owned and leased vehicle fleet, including allocation, maintenance, and driver records.

### Trigger
The arrival of a vehicle booking request or a scheduled fleet maintenance date.

### Consumes
Vehicle Booking Request supplies the required vehicle type, date, and driver. Fleet Maintenance Schedule supplies the service intervals for each vehicle. Driver Record supplies the driver's licence and eligibility status.

### Steps
The process checks driver eligibility and licence validity. It reserves an available vehicle that meets the requirement. It issues a Vehicle Key Handover with condition check. It monitors vehicle return and records mileage and damage. It schedules and records maintenance. If a vehicle is returned damaged, a Damage Report is created and costs are assigned. Vehicle availability is updated daily. Expired licences or insurance trigger a block on future bookings.

### Produces
Vehicle Booking Confirmation states the vehicle, driver, and time period. Vehicle Condition Report records the pre- and post-use state. Fleet Maintenance Record updates the service history.

### Outcome
Vehicles are available, maintained, and used only by eligible drivers.

### Fails when
A vehicle breaks down or an ineligible driver gains access, causing disruption or legal liability.

Name: Venue Mgt
Documentation:
### Identity
Management of campus venues for internal and external hire, including bookings, setup, and compliance.

### Trigger
The arrival of a venue hire request.

### Consumes
Venue Hire Request supplies the event details and requirements. Venue Availability Record supplies the free slots. Venue Setup Specification supplies the furniture and technical needs.

### Steps
The process checks venue availability. It confirms the hire and terms. It arranges setup and technical support. It ensures health and safety. It runs the event. It restores the venue after use. It invoices the hirer. It collects feedback. If damage occurs, it claims against the deposit.

### Produces
Venue Booking Confirmation states the hire details. Venue Setup Order states the required configuration. Venue Invoice states the hire charge.

### Outcome
Venues are used efficiently and generate income while remaining in good condition.

### Fails when
A venue is double-booked or damaged, causing customer disputes and lost income.

Name: Workforce Planning
Documentation:
### Identity
Strategic workforce planning, including demand forecasting, capability analysis, and headcount planning.

### Trigger
The arrival of the annual planning cycle or a change in institutional strategy.

### Consumes
Institutional Strategy supplies the future direction and priorities. Current Workforce Profile supplies the existing headcount, skills, and demographics. Turnover Data supplies the rate and reasons for leavers.

### Steps
The process forecasts future workforce demand by role and skill. It assesses current supply and gaps. It develops workforce plans to close gaps through recruitment, development, or restructuring. It validates plans against budget. It monitors progress and revises. It reports the workforce plan to governance. If a gap cannot be filled internally, external recruitment is authorised.

### Produces
Workforce Plan states the future headcount and skill requirements. Skills Gap Analysis records the difference between current and required capabilities. Recruitment Authorisation states the approved new roles.

### Outcome
The institution has a workforce aligned with its strategy and a clear path to close skill gaps.

### Fails when
Workforce planning is disconnected from budget, causing either overstaffing or critical skills shortages.

Name: Workforce Relations Mgt
Documentation:
### Identity
Management of employee relations, including union negotiations, disciplinary procedures, and grievance handling.

### Trigger
The arrival of a grievance, a disciplinary case, or a collective bargaining date.

### Consumes
Grievance Record supplies the employee's complaint. Disciplinary Case File supplies the alleged misconduct and evidence. Collective Agreement supplies the negotiated terms with recognised unions.

### Steps
The process assesses the case under policy. It follows the formal procedure: investigation, hearing, decision, and appeal. It applies the collective agreement where relevant. It consults with unions on collective matters. It records outcomes and implements sanctions or remedies. It reviews the case for learning. If an appeal is lodged, it is heard by a different manager. Cases are time-bound.

### Produces
Disciplinary Outcome Letter states the decision and sanction. Grievance Outcome Letter states the resolution. Collective Agreement Update records any new negotiated terms.

### Outcome
Employee relations are conducted fairly and legally, reducing disputes and protecting the institution.

### Fails when
A grievance or disciplinary case is mishandled, causing an employment tribunal claim and reputational damage.

Name: Workforce Reporting
Documentation:
### Identity
Workforce reporting and analytics, including headcount, diversity, absence, and turnover metrics.

### Trigger
The arrival of a reporting period close or a management information request.

### Consumes
Workforce Data Extract supplies the raw HR data for the period. Reporting Template supplies the required metrics and format. Prior Period Workforce Report supplies the comparison baseline.

### Steps
The process extracts and validates data. It calculates the metrics. It prepares reports for management and statutory bodies. It reviews for accuracy and consistency. It publishes to the appropriate recipients. It answers follow-up queries. It archives the report. If data quality issues are found, they are corrected at source.

### Produces
Workforce Report states the headcount, diversity, absence, and turnover metrics. Management Information Pack supplies the board-level summary. Data Quality Correction records any correction to source data.

### Outcome
The institution understands its workforce through accurate reports, informing decisions.

### Fails when
Workforce data is not validated, causing incorrect metrics to be reported to the regulator and misleading management.

Name: Academic Administration
Documentation:
### Identity
This is a management capability within the Teaching & Learning domain. It is accountable for the governing body of Programme Regulations and for ensuring those regulations are applied consistently to student progression and award decisions.

### Consumes
It consumes Student Appeals when a learner submits a formal challenge to a mark, progression decision or award. It consumes Regulatory Guidance when an external body issues a new condition that affects assessment or progression. It consumes Programme Approval Documents when a new course or modification is put forward for academic approval.

### Produces
It produces Programme Regulations as version-controlled rules that name modules, credits, progression thresholds and award requirements. It produces Assessment Board Decisions as a formal record of the board's resolution on each case. It produces Academic Policy Decisions as binding interpretations of regulations for future cases.

### Activities
Activities present in this capability are: apply Programme Regulations to a Student Appeal, record Assessment Board Decisions, issue Academic Policy Decisions, review Programme Approval Documents, reject a Student Appeal that lacks ground of challenge, and reassess a progression decision after an appeal is upheld.

### Fails when
It fails when Programme Regulations contain conflicting provisions or when Assessment Board Decisions are not recorded. Student Appeals then remain unresolved, progression decisions become inconsistent, and Student Records are not updated, delaying Student Completion.

### Constraint
This capability is constrained by the need to maintain a single authoritative interpretation of academic regulations across all academic years and programmes.

### Operating Conditions
A Student Appeal must include the learner identifier, module code, ground of challenge and supporting evidence; if these are missing it is returned as incomplete. Regulatory Guidance must carry a source, issue date and statutory reference; if the reference is absent it is escalated to legal review. Programme Approval Documents must name the responsible proposer, credit total and assessment load; if the credit total does not match the Programme Regulations, the document is rejected.

Name: Accommodation Management
Documentation:
### Identity
Layer: enabling; parent domain: Enabling Capabilities. This capability holds accountability for the allocation, tenancy, and condition of residential accommodation. It is answerable for matching enrolled students to available rooms, managing rent and deposits, and ensuring that accommodation meets statutory health and safety standards.

### Consumes
It takes in Accommodation Application, triggered when a student applies for a place in halls. It takes in Maintenance Request, triggered when an occupant reports a fault. It takes in Notice to Vacate, triggered when an occupant gives notice of departure. It takes in Rent Payment, triggered when a tenant pays scheduled rent.

### Produces
It issues Room Allocation when eligibility and preferences are matched against Room Inventory. It issues Tenancy Agreement when a room offer is accepted and deposit is received. It issues Room Condition Report when an occupant checks in or out. It issues Maintenance Work Order when a Maintenance Request is validated against urgency.

### Activities
Reviews Accommodation Application against eligibility and support needs. Verifies student enrolment status with the Student Record. Allocates Room against Room Inventory and waiting list. Generates Tenancy Agreement with rent and occupancy terms. Records Rent Payment against Tenant Account. Schedules Room Inspection for condition and compliance. Processes Early Termination Request and calculates fees due. Reassesses Allocation Appeal and issues revised Room Allocation. Manages Waiting List when demand exceeds room supply.

### Fails when
It stops delivering when Room Inventory is not updated with vacancies, maintenance status and reserved rooms, causing double allocation, unsuitable placements, or unoccupied beds during peak intake.

### Constraint
It operates on a fixed academic-year cycle with intense September intake and July turnaround, leaving little room to correct allocation errors before term starts.

### Operating Conditions
Accommodation Application must include Student ID, term dates, and support needs; if incomplete, it is returned to the applicant. Maintenance Request must include location, fault description and urgency; if urgency is absent, it is returned for clarification. Notice to Vacate must be signed and dated and match the Tenancy Agreement; if not, it is accepted with qualification and a rent adjustment is made. Rent Payment must include Student ID and amount; if mismatched, it is accepted and placed in suspense until reconciled.

Name: Alumni Engagement
Documentation:
### Identity
This is an operating capability within the Teaching & Learning domain. It is accountable for maintaining continuing contact with graduates and for converting that contact into measurable engagement and voluntary support.

### Consumes
It consumes Graduate Records when an award is conferred and the graduate becomes eligible for alumni contact. It consumes Alumni Contact Preferences when a graduate chooses channels or opts out. It consumes Donation Pledges when a graduate commits money or estate gifts.

### Produces
It produces Alumni Event Invitations when an event is scheduled and targeted to graduates by cohort or interest. It produces Alumni Newsletters when a publication cycle completes. It produces Donation Receipts when a Donation Pledge is paid.

### Activities
Activities present are: maintain Alumni Contact Preferences, validate Graduate Records for alumni eligibility, organise Alumni Event Invitations, publish Alumni Newsletters, record Donation Pledges, process Donation Receipts, and suppress contact when an opt-out is recorded.

### Fails when
It fails when Graduate Records are not matched to current contact details or when Alumni Contact Preferences are ignored. Engagement then drops, Donation Pledges are not recorded, and the institution has no reliable graduate contact base for statutory or fundraising purposes.

### Constraint
It is constrained by the UK GDPR requirement that every contact use a lawful basis and by the need to keep alumni data separate from current student records.

### Operating Conditions
A Graduate Record must be checked against the institution's graduation list and include the graduate identifier and programme title; if the title is missing it is accepted with a qualification for later correction. An Alumni Contact Preference must state the preferred channel and consent; if consent is absent the record is suppressed. A Donation Pledge must have a stated amount and payment instruction; if the instruction is incomplete the pledge is returned.

Name: Business Capability Management
Documentation:
### Identity
This is a layer two capability within Strategy & Governance. It is accountable for maintaining the inventory of business capabilities, assessing each against Strategic Objectives, and directing investment to close gaps or retire redundant capability.

### Consumes
It takes in the approved Strategic Plan when a new planning cycle starts; each Strategic Objective is extracted and mapped to the current capability inventory. It takes in Key Performance Indicators at the end of each academic term; each indicator is tied to a capability owner. It takes in Capability Assessment Requests from service owners when a service issue suggests a capability gap. It takes in Risk Register entries when a risk is linked to capability underperformance.

### Produces
It issues a Capability Roadmap when the governing body approves a set of investment priorities. It issues an Investment Decision when a business case has a named owner, cost estimate, and expected impact on a Strategic Objective. It issues a Capability Change Mandate when an investment is approved, which authorises the change. It issues a Capability Performance Report at the end of each academic year, stating maturity and utilisation for each capability.

### Activities
Activities include assessing a business capability against a Strategic Objective, prioritising a Capability Assessment Request, recording a capability owner, issuing an Investment Decision, escalating a Capability Performance Report that shows underperformance, rejecting an Investment Decision request that lacks a cost estimate, and reassessing a business capability after a Capability Change Mandate completes.

### Fails when
This capability fails when no current Capability Roadmap exists and the governing body refuses to approve one, because then Investment Decisions cannot be made and underperforming business capabilities continue without remediation.

### Constraint
Every business capability in the inventory must have a named accountable executive and a traceable link to at least one Strategic Objective; capabilities without both are excluded from investment decisions.

### Operating Conditions
Incoming Strategic Plan must be the governing-body-approved version for the current cycle and must contain measurable Strategic Objectives; if it is a draft or lacks measurable objectives, it is returned to the originator. Key Performance Indicators must be no older than the last completed academic term and must include the capability owner and baseline; if missing either, the indicator is rejected. Capability Assessment Requests must state the service issue and the suspected capability; without both, the request is accepted with a qualification and placed in a holding queue. Risk Register entries must carry a risk owner and a likelihood score; if not, they are returned. The produced Capability Roadmap is judged by whether each entry maps to a Strategic Objective and an Investment Decision; any entry without both is sent back for revision.

Name: Commercial Delivery
Documentation:
### Identity
An operating capability within the Commercial Activity domain. It ensures that contracted goods or services are delivered, accepted and recorded against the Commercial Contract.

### Consumes
Contract Agreement arrives when it is fully signed and binds delivery obligations; it triggers creation of a delivery plan. Service Request arrives from an internal or external party as a demand for contracted service; it triggers scheduling of resources. Supplier Invoice arrives when a supplier claims payment for delivered goods or services; it triggers verification against delivery acceptance.

### Produces
Delivery Acceptance Record is issued when the goods or services meet the Contract Agreement scope and quality requirements; it leaves an accepted state with date, recipient and contract reference. Payment Instruction is issued when a Supplier Invoice matches a Delivery Acceptance Record and contract pricing; it leaves an approved state for payment. Contract Variation is issued when scope, price or delivery date changes require formal amendment; it leaves a pending or approved state.

### Activities
Plan delivery milestones from Contract Agreement. Assign delivery resources to Service Requests. Verify delivered goods or services against Contract Agreement specifications. Record Delivery Acceptance Record. Reject non-conforming delivery and return to supplier or client. Verify Supplier Invoice against Delivery Acceptance Record and Contract Agreement pricing. Issue Payment Instruction for verified Supplier Invoice. Raise Contract Variation when scope or date changes exceed tolerance.

### Fails when
Deliveries cannot be accepted because they fail contract specifications, or Supplier Invoices cannot be matched to accepted deliveries; then payments are not authorised, suppliers or clients stop providing contracted goods or services, and Contract Agreements cannot close.

### Constraint
No payment is authorised for any Supplier Invoice until the corresponding Delivery Acceptance Record is recorded and linked to the Contract Agreement.

### Operating Conditions
Incoming Contract Agreement must be signed by an authorised signatory and contain complete specifications, pricing, delivery dates and acceptance criteria; unsigned or incomplete agreements are returned to origin. Service Request must reference a valid Contract Agreement or approved purchase; requests lacking that reference are rejected. Supplier Invoice must be accurate against contract pricing and receipt of goods; invoices with price or quantity mismatches are returned to supplier. Delivery Acceptance Record must be traceable to the named recipient and contract line; untraceable acceptance blocks payment. Contract Variation must carry revised approvals; an unapproved variation is rejected.

Name: Commercial Engagement
Documentation:
### Identity
An operating capability within the Commercial Activity domain. It establishes and develops commercial relationships with external clients and translates client needs into firm proposals and signed Contract Agreements.

### Consumes
Client Enquiry arrives when an external organisation requests commercial services or collaboration; it triggers qualification and scope discussions. Service Request arrives when an internal unit identifies a commercial opportunity requiring client engagement; it triggers proposal development. Contract Agreement arrives when legal and finance have approved the proposed terms; it triggers final client signature and record creation.

### Produces
Commercial Proposal is issued when scope, pricing and delivery terms are agreed with the client and the internal cost model is approved; it leaves a state ready for client acceptance. Contract Agreement is issued when both parties sign; it leaves a binding arrangements record and triggers delivery and invoicing. Client Record is issued when a prospective client is qualified and added to the pipeline; it leaves an active account state with contact, sector and creditworthiness.

### Activities
Qualify Client Enquiry against institutional commercial criteria. Develop Commercial Proposal with pricing model and delivery terms. Negotiate Contract Agreement terms with client. Escalate legal deviation to institutional legal review. Decline Client Enquiry where commercial viability or compliance risk is unacceptable. Maintain Client Record with engagement history and approvals.

### Fails when
A Client Enquiry cannot be converted to a signed Contract Agreement because pricing cannot cover costs or legal terms are not approved; then no external commercial income is generated for that opportunity and downstream delivery cannot start.

### Constraint
No commercial engagement proceeds beyond proposal stage without an institutional cost model and legal sign-off, regardless of client urgency.

### Operating Conditions
Incoming Client Enquiry must carry named client legal entity, contact authority and required services; enquiries without a legal entity are rejected. Service Request must include an approved internal sponsor and budget code; unauthorised requests are returned. Contract Agreement arriving from legal review must be complete with all schedules and signatories; incomplete agreements are returned for correction. Commercial Proposal must be traceable to the Client Enquiry and approved cost model; where the cost model is missing the proposal is not issued. Client Record must maintain current beneficial ownership and sanctions screening; failure to complete screening rejects the client.

Name: Commercial Monitoring
Documentation:
### Identity
An operating capability within the Commercial Activity domain. It monitors performance, financial delivery, risks and compliance of Commercial Contracts and produces reports for management and external obligations.

### Consumes
Contract Agreement arrives when executed and triggers registration in the monitoring system. Delivery Acceptance Record arrives when delivery is accepted; it triggers update of contract performance metrics. Supplier Invoice arrives when processed and triggers financial tracking and spend analysis. Government Policy document arrives when regulatory reporting duties change; it triggers update of monitoring indicators.

### Produces
Contract Performance Report is issued at each reporting period, recording key performance indicators, spend and delivery status. Risk Register is issued when risks are identified and assessed, with risk owner and mitigation. Financial Statement is issued when all transactions for the period are reconciled and audited. Regulatory Return is issued when statutory thresholds are met and obligations require submission.

### Activities
Track contract milestones against Contract Agreement. Reconcile Supplier Invoice and Delivery Acceptance Record against contract values. Identify contract performance exceptions. Escalate underperformance to contract owner and supplier. Maintain Risk Register with likelihood, impact and owner. Prepare Contract Performance Report with variance analysis. Submit Regulatory Return to regulator. Reassess contract compliance when Government Policy document changes.

### Fails when
Contract performance data is incomplete or Supplier Invoices cannot be reconciled to contract lines, preventing Financial Statements from being signed off and Regulatory Returns from being submitted; then management cannot evidence commercial performance and statutory deadlines are missed.

### Constraint
All contract performance and financial reporting must be traceable to the underlying Contract Agreement and its accepted delivery records, not to manual aggregates.

### Operating Conditions
Incoming Contract Agreement must be complete, dated and signed; unsigned contracts are rejected for monitoring until resolved. Delivery Acceptance Record must be recorded within the same reporting period as delivery; late records are accepted but flagged as non-current and excluded from performance metrics until corrected. Supplier Invoice must be matched to contract line and delivery; unmatched invoices are returned to processing. Government Policy document must be current and confirmed as applicable; superseded documents are archived and not applied. Contract Performance Report must reconcile to the Risk Register and financial ledger; unreconciled reports are not issued.

Name: Commercial Sourcing
Documentation:
### Identity
An operating capability within the Commercial Activity domain. It identifies, evaluates and selects external suppliers and assembles the terms that become Commercial Contracts for purchased goods and services.

### Consumes
Request for Purchase arrives when an institutional unit submits a requirement for goods, works or services not available internally; it triggers sourcing. Supplier Proposal arrives when a supplier responds to a call for competition or direct invitation; it triggers evaluation. Government Policy document arrives when procurement thresholds or sustainability duties are updated; it triggers alignment of sourcing criteria.

### Produces
Approved Supplier List is issued when supplier due diligence, financial checks and insurance evidence are complete and recorded; it leaves a list of suppliers eligible for future contracts. Commercial Contract is issued when chosen supplier and the institution agree price, scope, duration and terms; it remains unsigned pending approvals. Supplier Evaluation Record is issued after each proposal is scored against advertised criteria; it records scores, clarifications and non-compliance findings.

### Activities
Issue Request for Purchase to market. Evaluate Supplier Proposal against published selection criteria. Conduct supplier due diligence on financial standing and insurance. Negotiate Commercial Contract terms with selected supplier. Reject non-compliant Supplier Proposal when mandatory requirements are not met. Escalate affordability rejection to budget holder when price exceeds approved threshold. Record conflict of interest declaration and exclude conflicted supplier from evaluation.

### Fails when
No Supplier Proposal meets the evaluation criteria or affordability limits; then no Commercial Contract is issued and the requested goods or services cannot be procured, leaving the originating Service Request unresolved.

### Constraint
Every sourcing decision must be documented against pre-published evaluation criteria; no Commercial Contract may be awarded to an off-contract supplier.

### Operating Conditions
Incoming Request for Purchase must be complete with specification, budget code and authorised sign-off; incomplete or unauthorised requests are returned to requester. Supplier Proposal must be received by the published closing date; late proposals are rejected. Government Policy document must be current and authoritative; outdated policy is accepted only if archived with superseded status. Supplier due diligence outputs must be verified and traceable to the named supplier; missing financial statements cause rejection. Approved Supplier List and Commercial Contract must be traceable to the Supplier Evaluation Record; where traceability is broken, the decision is re-opened.

Name: Corporate Governance
Documentation:
### Identity
This is a layer two capability within Strategy & Governance. It is accountable for the lawful and proper conduct of the institution's governing body, its committees, and its statutory officers. It ensures decisions are made with a recorded quorum, conflicts of interest are declared, and obligations to the Office for Students, Companies House, and the Information Commissioner are met.

### Consumes
It takes in Government Policy Documents as they are published by regulators or Parliament; each is assessed for applicability and converted into a Compliance Obligation with a due date. It takes in Audit Findings from internal and external assurance providers; each is logged against a committee with a required response. It takes in Board Agenda Requests from officers and committees; each is scheduled against the annual governance calendar. It takes in Whistleblowing Reports through the confidential channel; each is forwarded to the nominated senior independent director.

### Produces
It issues Governance Decisions when a meeting has a recorded quorum and a majority vote; each decision is numbered and dated. It issues Board Minutes after they have been approved at the following meeting. It issues Statutory Filings to the relevant regulator on or before the statutory deadline. It issues Annual Reports when the external auditor has signed and the governing body has approved the accounts. It issues Policy Statements when a policy has passed equality impact assessment and governing body approval.

### Activities
Activities include scheduling a Board Agenda Request, preparing a Board Pack, reviewing a Compliance Obligation against the statutory calendar, recording a Governance Decision in the minute book, investigating a Whistleblowing Report, rejecting a Board Agenda Request that lacks an executive sponsor, escalating a Compliance Obligation that is past due, and approving a Board Minutes draft after amendment.

### Fails when
This capability fails when the governing body cannot achieve a quorum for two consecutive scheduled meetings, because no Governance Decision, Board Minutes, or Statutory Filing can be issued. As a result, the Office for Students is not notified of reportable events and the institution loses its registration conditions.

### Constraint
Every Governance Decision must be attributable to a named individual and recorded in Board Minutes within five working days; a decision without both is void.

### Operating Conditions
Incoming Government Policy Documents must state the issuing body, effective date, and affected legislation; if any is missing, the document is returned to the source with a request for the full text. Audit Findings must include evidence, impact, and a recommendation; if not, the finding is rejected and the auditor is asked to resubmit. Board Agenda Requests must include a decision required and an executive sponsor; without both, the request is returned. Whistleblowing Reports must be dated and identify the alleged breach; if anonymous and undated, the report is accepted with a qualification that limits investigation. Produced Governance Decisions are judged by whether they include the motion, vote count, and date; a decision missing any of these is not issued. Board Minutes are judged by whether they record all Governance Decisions and declarations of interest; if a decision is omitted, the minutes are returned for correction.

Name: Curriculum Management
Documentation:
### Identity
This is a management capability within the Teaching & Learning domain. It is accountable for the approval, maintenance and retirement of the institutional curriculum, including module content, credits, learning outcomes and assessment strategies.

### Consumes
It consumes Programme Specifications when a new programme is proposed or an existing one is revised. It consumes Module Proposals when a module is added, changed or withdrawn. It consumes External Examiner Feedback when a programme review identifies a quality issue. It consumes Professional Body Requirements when an accrediting body issues new standards.

### Produces
It produces an Approved Curriculum as the authoritative list of programmes, modules and credit values. It produces a Module Catalogue as a published, searchable record for students and staff. It produces Curriculum Change Notices when an approval or withdrawal is confirmed.

### Activities
Activities present are: draft Programme Specifications, review Module Proposals, validate Learning Outcomes against credit value, apply Professional Body Requirements, approve a Curriculum Change, reject a Module Proposal that lacks assessment strategy, and retire a Course when no longer viable.

### Fails when
It fails when Module Proposals are not approved before the academic year starts or when the Module Catalogue does not match the Approved Curriculum. Students cannot then select valid modules, assessment schedules become unusable, and Student Completion is delayed.

### Constraint
It is constrained by the requirement that every module and programme satisfy both institutional regulations and any relevant professional accreditation standard before it is listed in the Module Catalogue.

### Operating Conditions
A Module Proposal must state module code, credit total, learning outcomes and assessment strategy; if the assessment strategy is absent the proposal is returned. A Programme Specification must include progression rules and exit awards; if progression rules are missing it is rejected. External Examiner Feedback must reference the relevant programme and identify the issue; if the reference is absent it is escalated to the responsible committee.

Name: Facilities & Property Management
Documentation:
### Identity
Layer: enabling; parent domain: Enabling Capabilities. This capability holds accountability for the condition, safety, and utilisation of the institution's estate. It is answerable for planned and reactive maintenance, building compliance, energy performance, and space allocation.

### Consumes
It takes in Building Condition Survey, triggered by scheduled inspection or regulatory requirement. It takes in Facilities Work Order, triggered by fault report or planned maintenance due. It takes in Planned Maintenance Schedule, triggered by asset lifecycle or manufacturer interval. It takes in Utility Invoice, triggered by billing cycle. It takes in Space Request, triggered by department or service change.

### Produces
It issues Facilities Work Order closure when work is verified complete against specification. It issues Maintenance Schedule when asset condition and statutory intervals are assessed. It issues Building Compliance Certificate when statutory inspections pass. It issues Energy Performance Report when meter data is collected and analysed. It issues Space Allocation when a Space Request is approved against utilisation criteria.

### Activities
Inspects building fabric and plant to produce Building Condition Survey. Prioritises Facilities Work Order by safety impact and statutory risk. Schedules Planned Maintenance Schedule from asset register and condition data. Dispatches internal staff or external contractor for work. Verifies completion against work specification and test results. Maintains Asbestos Register for each building. Processes Space Request against room utilisation data and academic need. Handles Emergency Repair Request to restore safe operation. Manages contractor performance against safety and time standards. Responds to utility failure and restores supply.

### Fails when
It stops delivering when Building Condition Survey is missing or older than the statutory interval, causing unplanned failures, unsafe conditions, and maintenance backlog that cannot be prioritised.

### Constraint
It operates a 24-hour physical campus under statutory building safety, fire and environmental regulations, where a single failed asset can close a building.

### Operating Conditions
Facilities Work Order must include location, fault type, priority and requester contact; if incomplete, it is returned to the requester. Building Condition Survey must be current within the statutory interval and produced by an accredited surveyor; if not, it is escalated and not used for maintenance planning. Utility Invoice must reconcile to meter readings and contract tariffs; if mismatched, it is returned to the utility provider. Planned Maintenance Schedule must include asset ID, statutory interval and last completed date; if missing, it is returned to the asset owner. Space Request must include required space type, occupancy, and purpose; if incomplete, it is returned.

Name: Finance Management
Documentation:
### Identity
Layer: enabling; parent domain: Enabling Capabilities. This capability holds accountability for the institution's financial control, accounting, payroll, procurement, treasury, and statutory reporting. It is answerable for financial accuracy, liquidity, and compliance with funding and tax obligations.

### Consumes
It takes in Supplier Invoice, triggered by receipt of goods or services. It takes in Purchase Order, triggered by an approved procurement decision. It takes in Expense Claim, triggered by a staff member's business expense. It takes in Student Fee payment, triggered by invoice or payment plan. It takes in Budget Proposal, triggered by annual planning or reforecast. It takes in Payroll Change Request, triggered by a change in employment terms.

### Produces
It issues Payment Run when Supplier Invoices are approved and due. It issues Financial Statement when the general ledger is closed for a period. It issues Budget Report when actuals are compared to budget. It issues Payroll Record when payroll is calculated and paid. It issues Invoice Query Resolution when a supplier or student disputes a charge.

### Activities
Validates Supplier Invoice against Purchase Order and goods receipt. Processes Expense Claim against expense policy and budget code. Allocates Student Fee payment to Student Account. Prepares Payment Run with segregation of duties. Reconciles Bank Statement to Financial Transactions. Produces Financial Statement under statutory accounting standards. Reviews Budget Proposal against resource constraints and strategic priorities. Processes Payroll Change Request with effective date and authorisation. Investigates Invoice Query and corrects transaction or requests credit note. Manages credit control and debt recovery for unpaid invoices.

### Fails when
It stops delivering when Supplier Invoice cannot be matched to a valid Purchase Order or budget code, causing payment delays, supplier holds, and breach of statutory payment terms; or when Payroll Record cannot be calculated because Payroll Change Request data is missing.

### Constraint
It operates under HMRC tax rules, OfS financial reporting conditions, and external audit requirements, with hard month-end and year-end close deadlines.

### Operating Conditions
Supplier Invoice must include valid Purchase Order number, VAT registration, and amount; if missing, it is returned to the supplier. Expense Claim must include receipts and budget code; if incomplete, it is returned to the claimant. Student Fee payment must include Student ID and amount; if mismatched, it is accepted with qualification and allocated to a suspense account until reconciled. Payroll Change Request must include signed authorisation and effective date; if not, it is returned. Budget Proposal must include cost centre and full-year impact; if incomplete, it is returned. Purchase Order must include approved supplier, amount, and budget code; if missing, it is returned to the requester.

Name: Government, Public & Stakeholder Relationships
Documentation:
### Identity
Layer: enabling; parent domain: Enabling Capabilities. This capability holds accountability for the institution's external standing with government, regulators, local communities, media, and partners. It is answerable for monitoring policy, responding to consultations and requests, and protecting institutional reputation.

### Consumes
It takes in Government Policy document, triggered by publication from a government body. It takes in Consultation Request, triggered by a regulator or government department seeking institutional input. It takes in Stakeholder Enquiry, triggered by a partner, community group or public body. It takes in Freedom of Information Request, triggered by a written request from the public. It takes in Parliamentary Question, triggered by a parliament member's query.

### Produces
It issues Consultation Response when institutional position is approved. It issues Stakeholder Briefing when an issue requires internal awareness or external communication. It issues Public Statement when the institution responds to media or public concern. It issues Regulatory Submission when a statutory return is due. It issues Memorandum of Understanding when a partnership framework is agreed.

### Activities
Monitors Government Policy document for relevance to institutional obligations. Prepares Consultation Response with institutional position and evidence. Coordinates Stakeholder Enquiry handling and response. Prepares Public Statement under press office and executive approval. Maintains Stakeholder Register with contact and interest. Responds to Freedom of Information Request within statutory deadline. Manages Parliamentary Question response from internal briefings. Arranges stakeholder meeting and records Meeting Note. Handles complaint from external stakeholder and escalates where unresolved.

### Fails when
It stops delivering when a Government Policy document is received but not assessed for impact, causing the institution to miss a consultation deadline or fail a statutory return, with regulatory sanction.

### Constraint
It operates to external deadlines set by government and regulators, many of which are statutory and cannot be extended, while institutional reputation depends on accurate public communication.

### Operating Conditions
Government Policy document must be current and official; if draft or unauthorised, it is accepted with qualification and flagged for confirmation. Consultation Request must include closing date, scope and contact; if missing, it is escalated for clarification. Freedom of Information Request must be in writing and include requester details; if not, it is accepted and the requester is asked for clarification under the duty to advise. Stakeholder Enquiry must include subject and expected response date; if incomplete, it is accepted and logged with a default response target. Parliamentary Question must include identifying number and deadline; if missing, it is escalated.

Name: Human Resource Management
Documentation:
### Identity
Layer: enabling; parent domain: Enabling Capabilities. This capability holds accountability for the employment lifecycle, recruitment, pay, development, and employee relations across the institution. It is answerable for workforce capacity, legal compliance, and fair treatment of staff.

### Consumes
It takes in Position Request, triggered by a vacancy or organisational change. It takes in Employment Application, triggered by a candidate response to a vacancy. It takes in Payroll Change Request, triggered by a change in employment terms or personal details. It takes in Training Request, triggered by a development need or appraisal. It takes in Grievance Record, triggered by an employee complaint. It takes in Sickness Absence Record, triggered by employee illness.

### Produces
It issues Offer Letter when a candidate is selected. It issues Employment Contract when the offer is accepted and right-to-work checks pass. It issues Payroll Change Instruction when an approved change is sent for payroll processing. It issues Training Record when training is completed and recorded. It issues Disciplinary Outcome when a disciplinary hearing concludes. It issues Exit Interview Record when an employee leaves.

### Activities
Reviews Position Request against workforce plan and budget. Advertises vacancy and shortlists Employment Application. Interviews and selects candidate. Issues Offer Letter and Employment Contract. Onboards new employee and creates employee record. Processes Payroll Change Request against policy and authorisation. Maintains Training Record for each employee. Conducts appraisal and records Appraisal Outcome. Manages Grievance Record through investigation and hearing. Handles Sickness Absence Record and return-to-work meeting. Processes termination and issues exit documentation. Manages appeal against disciplinary or grievance outcome.

### Fails when
It stops delivering when Payroll Change Request is not processed before the payroll cut-off, causing incorrect pay, tax errors, and employee relations risk; or when Employment Contract is issued without right-to-work check, causing illegal working.

### Constraint
It operates under employment law, collective bargaining agreements, equality duties, and UK GDPR for employee personal data, with strict deadlines for pay and dispute resolution.

### Operating Conditions
Employment Application must include right-to-work evidence, qualifications, and application form; if incomplete, it is returned to the candidate. Payroll Change Request must be authorised by the budget holder and include effective date; if not, it is returned. Grievance Record must be submitted within policy timeframe and include a factual account; if late, it is accepted with qualification and investigated where reasonable. Sickness Absence Record must include fit note and dates; if missing, it is accepted and manager follows absence policy. Position Request must include job description and grade; if incomplete, it is returned. Training Request must include learner, course, and budget code; if incomplete, it is returned.

Name: Information & Communication Technology Mgt
Documentation:
### Identity
Layer: enabling; parent domain: Enabling Capabilities. This capability holds accountability for the institution's ICT infrastructure, applications, user support, security, and technology change. It is answerable for service availability, data integrity, and cyber resilience.

### Consumes
It takes in ICT Service Request, triggered by a user requesting access, equipment, or service change. It takes in Incident Record, triggered by a reported failure or disruption. It takes in Change Request, triggered by a need to alter an ICT service. It takes in Security Alert, triggered by a threat notification or detection. It takes in Asset Purchase Request, triggered by a hardware or software need.

### Produces
It issues Service Desk Ticket when an ICT Service Request is logged. It issues Configuration Item when an asset or software is recorded in the configuration management database. It issues Change Approval Record when a Change Request is assessed and authorised. It issues Security Patch Record when a vulnerability is remediated. It issues ICT Service Catalogue when a service is defined and published.

### Activities
Logs ICT Service Request and assigns Service Desk Ticket. Diagnoses Incident Record and applies known error. Resolves Incident Record or escalates to specialist group. Assesses Change Request for risk and impact. Tests change and implements with backout plan. Maintains Configuration Item for each asset and software version. Applies Security Patch Record to vulnerable systems. Handles Asset Purchase Request within procurement limits. Provisions user access and removes access on role change. Manages service continuity and disaster recovery.

### Fails when
It stops delivering when a Security Alert is not acted on, causing unauthorised access, data loss, or system compromise; or when Change Request cannot be assessed because Configuration Item data is inaccurate.

### Constraint
It operates under UK GDPR security obligations and a requirement for continuous service availability, where unplanned downtime disrupts teaching, research, and administration.

### Operating Conditions
Incident Record must include time, impact, affected service, and user contact; if missing, it is returned for clarification. Change Request must include risk assessment, backout plan, and approver; if not, it is rejected by the change advisory board. Security Alert must be verified from a trusted source; if unverified, it is accepted with qualification and quarantined. ICT Service Request must include requester and requested service; if incomplete, it is returned. Asset Purchase Request must include business need and budget code; if missing, it is returned.

Name: Information Management
Documentation:
### Identity
Layer: enabling; parent domain: Enabling Capabilities. This capability holds accountability for the institution's records, information assets, data protection, privacy, and retention. It is answerable for lawful processing, discoverability, and secure disposal of information.

### Consumes
It takes in Data Protection Impact Assessment, triggered by a new or changed processing activity. It takes in Record Retention Request, triggered by a department needing a retention schedule. It takes in Information Asset Register, triggered by an asset owner update or new asset. It takes in Data Subject Access Request, triggered by an individual's request. It takes in Information Classification Request, triggered by a new information asset or review.

### Produces
It issues Data Protection Impact Assessment approval when risks are mitigated. It issues Record Retention Schedule when retention periods are set. It issues Information Asset Register entry when asset details are recorded. It issues Data Subject Access Response when requested information is compiled. It issues Information Classification Decision when an asset is classified.

### Activities
Maintains Information Asset Register with owner, location, and classification. Conducts Data Protection Impact Assessment and reviews risk. Applies Record Retention Schedule to record series. Processes Data Subject Access Request within statutory deadline. Classifies information asset according to confidentiality and integrity. Handles data breach report and notifies regulator where required. Manages records disposal and destruction order. Responds to audit finding on information handling. Reviews third-party data sharing agreement.

### Fails when
It stops delivering when a Data Subject Access Request is not answered within one month, causing a regulatory breach and potential fine; or when Record Retention Schedule is missing, causing unlawful disposal or retention.

### Constraint
It operates under UK GDPR, Freedom of Information Act, and public records legislation, with statutory deadlines and evidence requirements that cannot be relaxed.

### Operating Conditions
Data Subject Access Request must include identity verification and scope; if missing, the requester is asked for proof before processing. Data Protection Impact Assessment must be completed before processing begins and include residual risks; if incomplete, it is returned to the data owner. Record Retention Request must specify record series, format, and proposed retention period; if not, it is returned. Information Asset Register entry must include owner, location, and classification; if missing, it is accepted with qualification and assigned an owner. Information Classification Request must include asset type and sensitivity; if incomplete, it is returned.

Name: Legal Services
Documentation:
### Identity
Layer: enabling; parent domain: Enabling Capabilities. This capability holds accountability for the institution's legal advice, contract drafting, litigation, regulatory compliance, and intellectual property. It is answerable for legal risk and for lawful execution of institutional obligations.

### Consumes
It takes in Legal Query, triggered by a request for advice from an internal department. It takes in Contract Draft, triggered by a proposed agreement with a third party. It takes in Litigation Notice, triggered by a claim or court document. It takes in Regulatory Notice, triggered by a regulator's communication. It takes in Intellectual Property Disclosure, triggered by an inventor or author.

### Produces
It issues Legal Opinion when advice is delivered. It issues Contract Agreement when terms are signed and approved. It issues Litigation Response when a defence or settlement is filed. It issues Regulatory Filing when a required submission is made. It issues Intellectual Property Assignment when ownership is transferred.

### Activities
Reviews Legal Query and assigns responsible lawyer. Drafts Legal Opinion with applicable law and risk. Negotiates Contract Draft against institutional terms. Executes Contract Agreement after approval. Responds to Litigation Notice within court deadline. Manages Regulatory Notice and coordinates regulatory filing. Assesses Intellectual Property Disclosure for ownership and commercial potential. Handles settlement negotiation and records settlement terms. Maintains legal precedent register. Supports internal investigation and disciplinary proceedings.

### Fails when
It stops delivering when Contract Draft is not reviewed before sign-off, causing the institution to accept unfavourable terms; or when Litigation Notice is overlooked, causing default judgment.

### Constraint
It operates under professional legal privilege, court deadlines, and statutory limitation periods, where delay can extinguish rights or create liability.

### Operating Conditions
Legal Query must include full facts, relevant documents, and desired outcome; if incomplete, it is returned to the requester. Contract Draft must be accompanied by procurement or partnership approval; if not, it is rejected. Litigation Notice must be date-stamped and served; if unclear, it is accepted with qualification and diarised. Regulatory Notice must be official and specify deadline; if missing, it is escalated. Intellectual Property Disclosure must include inventors, dates, and funding source; if incomplete, it is returned.

Name: Library Management
Documentation:
### Identity
Layer: enabling; parent domain: Enabling Capabilities. This capability holds accountability for the institution's library collections, access to information resources, borrowing, and research support. It is answerable for matching users to the materials they need within copyright and licensing terms.

### Consumes
It takes in Library Acquisition Request, triggered by a reading list, research need, or collection gap. It takes in Library Loan Request, triggered by a user wanting to borrow an item. It takes in Interlibrary Loan Request, triggered by a user requesting an item not held. It takes in Copyright Query, triggered by a use of third-party material. It takes in Resource Access Request, triggered by a user needing access to a digital resource.

### Produces
It issues Library Loan when a borrower's entitlement is confirmed and item is available. It issues Interlibrary Loan when a supplying library confirms availability. It issues Catalogue Record when an item is acquired and catalogued. It issues Copyright Clearance when a proposed use is assessed as lawful. It issues Resource Access Grant when a user is authorised for a platform.

### Activities
Reviews Library Acquisition Request against collection policy and budget. Selects and acquires item and creates Catalogue Record. Circulates Library Loan and records due date. Manages Overdue Loan and applies recall. Processes Interlibrary Loan Request and tracks return. Answers Copyright Query and advises on fair dealing. Grants Resource Access Request against licence terms. Maintains reading list support and scans chapter requests. Handles lost item and replacement fee.

### Fails when
It stops delivering when Library Loan Request cannot be fulfilled because Catalogue Record is missing or inaccurate, causing users to be unable to locate or access material.

### Constraint
It operates under copyright law and digital licensing agreements that restrict what can be copied, shared, or accessed across the institution.

### Operating Conditions
Library Acquisition Request must include reading list or research need and source details; if missing, it is returned. Library Loan Request must be from a registered borrower with valid status; if not, it is rejected. Interlibrary Loan Request must include full citation and copyright declaration; if incomplete, it is returned. Copyright Query must include intended use and extract; if not, it is escalated to the copyright officer. Resource Access Request must include user role and resource; if incomplete, it is returned.

Name: Promotions Management
Documentation:
### Identity
Layer: enabling; parent domain: Enabling Capabilities. This capability holds accountability for the institution's marketing, brand, recruitment promotions, campaigns, and events. It is answerable for attracting students, protecting brand consistency, and measuring campaign effectiveness.

### Consumes
It takes in Promotional Campaign Brief, triggered by a recruitment or reputational need. It takes in Market Research Report, triggered by a commissioned study or internal analysis. It takes in Budget Allocation, triggered by annual planning or campaign approval. It takes in Brand Asset Request, triggered by a department needing logo or template. It takes in Event Request, triggered by a proposed open day or promotional event.

### Produces
It issues Promotional Material when a campaign asset is approved and produced. It issues Communication Plan when a campaign approach is agreed. It issues Campaign Report when campaign performance is measured. It issues Brand Asset when a logo or template is supplied under licence. It issues Event Plan when an event is approved and scheduled.

### Activities
Reviews Promotional Campaign Brief against brand and objectives. Conducts market research or commissions Market Research Report. Creates Communication Plan with channels and timeline. Develops Promotional Material for print, web, and social. Approves brand use on Promotional Material. Runs campaign and monitors spend. Measures Campaign Report against key performance indicators. Handles Event Request and schedules event logistics. Manages promotional budget and reconciles spend.

### Fails when
It stops delivering when Promotional Campaign Brief lacks target audience or budget, causing a campaign to launch without measurable objective or sufficient resource.

### Constraint
It operates under brand guidelines and Advertising Standards Authority rules, within the seasonal recruitment cycle that concentrates activity in autumn and spring.

### Operating Conditions
Promotional Campaign Brief must include objective, target audience, budget, and deadline; if missing, it is returned to the requester. Market Research Report must include methodology and sample; if not, it is accepted with qualification and not used for major decisions. Brand Asset Request must comply with brand guidelines; if not, it is rejected. Event Request must include date, venue, audience, and purpose; if incomplete, it is returned. Budget Allocation must include cost centre and approved amount; if missing, it is returned.

Name: Research Administration
Documentation:
### Identity
This is an operational capability within the Research domain. It is responsible for setting up Research Contracts, Research Projects, Data Management Plans and Research Ethics Approvals after a Research Award Notice, and for producing Research Funder Reports from Research Progress Reports and Research Final Reports.

### Consumes
It consumes Research Award Notice, which arrives from funding and triggers the creation of a Research Contract and Research Project.
