It consumes Research Progress Report, which arrives at each reporting point and triggers administrative review against the Research Contract. It consumes Research Final Report, which arrives when research activities complete and triggers financial and technical closure checks.

### Produces
It produces Research Contract when a Research Award Notice is accepted and all funder terms are recorded. It produces Research Project when a Research Contract is signed and the project is assigned a start date. It produces Data Management Plan when research data requirements are agreed with the research lead. It produces Research Ethics Approval when an ethics review is complete and the approval is attached to the Research Project. It produces Research Funder Report when all Research Progress Reports and Research Final Reports have been accepted and contractual financial obligations are met.

### Activities
Accepting a Research Award Notice is present. Creating a Research Contract is present. Creating a Research Project is present. Producing a Data Management Plan is present. Producing a Research Ethics Approval is present. Reviewing Research Progress Report against the Research Contract is present. Reviewing Research Final Report against the Research Contract is present. Producing Research Funder Report is present. Rejecting incomplete Research Progress Report is present. Escalating late Research Final Report is present. Reassessing a Data Management Plan after an audit finding is present. Closing a Research Project after Research Funder Report acceptance is present.

### Fails when
This capability fails when Research Award Notices are received but Research Contracts cannot be signed because funder terms are unacceptable or Data Management Plans cannot be agreed, and no Research Projects are created. As a result, no Research Progress Reports or Research Final Reports can be reviewed, and no Research Funder Reports are issued.

### Constraint
The capability operates under the single legal institution constraint; it cannot administer Research Contracts or Research Ethics Approvals for multi-institution projects, and every Research Project and Data Management Plan is owned by the institution alone.

### Operating Conditions
Research Award Notice must include funder terms, award amount, duration and named research lead; notices missing any element are rejected. Research Progress Report must arrive before the contractual reporting deadline and include progress against milestones; late or incomplete reports are returned. Research Final Report must be submitted after all research activities cease and include final spend and deliverable completion; reports submitted before project end are rejected. Data Management Plan must specify storage, access, retention and open access arrangements; plans that do not meet funder conditions are returned for revision.

Name: Research Delivery
Documentation:
### Identity
This is an operational capability within the Research domain. It is responsible for executing Research Projects according to the Research Contract, producing Research Data and Research Outputs, and maintaining milestones up to the Research Final Report.

### Consumes
It consumes Research Project, which triggers the allocation of staff and facilities. It consumes Data Management Plan, which arrives with the Research Project and defines how Research Data is captured and stored. It consumes Research Ethics Approval, which arrives when the project involves regulated participants or data and must be in place before research activity begins. It consumes Research Budget, which arrives at project start and releases funds for approved research activities.

### Produces
It produces Research Data when experiments, fieldwork or analysis generate raw results, and the data is deposited under the Data Management Plan. It produces Research Output when research findings are synthesised and validated against the Research Contract. It produces Research Progress Report at each contractual reporting point. It produces Research Final Report when all research activities are complete and the Research Project closes.

### Activities
Executing a Research Project is present. Capturing Research Data is present. Storing Research Data under a Data Management Plan is present. Analysing Research Data is present. Producing Research Output is present. Producing Research Progress Report is present. Producing Research Final Report is present. Reassessing research methods after a failed experiment is present. Escalating Research Data loss or corruption is present. Rejecting Research Output that does not meet the Research Contract is present. Replanning Research Milestones after a budget or ethics change is present.

### Fails when
This capability fails when Research Projects are started without a valid Data Management Plan or Research Ethics Approval, and Research Data cannot be captured or stored. As a result, no Research Outputs, Research Progress Reports or Research Final Reports are produced, and the Research Contract is breached.

### Constraint
The capability operates as if all research activity occurs inside the single legal institution; it cannot deliver research in shared facilities or manage multi-institution research teams, and Research Data cannot leave the institutional boundary.

### Operating Conditions
Research Project must carry an approved Research Budget and named research lead; projects missing either are returned for correction. Research Ethics Approval must be current and cover the planned research methods; expired approvals block start. Data Management Plan must specify storage and access before Research Data capture; a plan without retention terms is rejected. Research Budget must be authorised and match the Research Award Notice; unauthorised budgets stop research activity. Research Output is judged downstream for completeness, reproducibility and open access eligibility; outputs without sufficient Research Data are returned for additional evidence.

Name: Research Funding
Documentation:
### Identity
This is a management capability within the Research domain. It is responsible for converting Research Funding Applications and Opportunity Register entries into Research Proposals, Research Costings, and finally Research Award Notices and Research Budgets.

### Consumes
It consumes Research Funding Application, which arrives from funders and triggers assessment of scope, deadline and eligibility. It consumes Opportunity Register, which arrives from planning and triggers matching of academic staff and research strengths to opportunities. It consumes Research Strategy, which arrives from planning and sets priority areas for proposal selection.

### Produces
It produces Research Proposal when a Research Funding Application is matched to a named academic lead and a feasible research plan is written. It produces Research Costing when the resource and cost estimate is completed and approved. It produces Research Award Notice when the funder accepts the Research Proposal and issues terms. It produces Research Budget when a Research Award Notice is accepted and the budget is allocated.

### Activities
Assessing Research Funding Application is present. Matching Opportunity Register entries to research strengths is present. Preparing Research Proposal is present. Preparing Research Costing is present. Reviewing Research Proposal against funder criteria is present. Submitting Research Proposal is present. Negotiating Research Award Notice is present. Rejecting Research Funding Application that is out of scope is present. Reassessing a Research Proposal after reviewer feedback is present. Producing Research Budget from Research Award Notice is present.

### Fails when
This capability fails when Research Funding Applications and Opportunity Register entries are available but no Research Proposal is submitted because the Research Costing cannot be approved, and no Research Award Notice arrives. As a result, Research Budgets are not produced and no new Research Projects can start.

### Constraint
The capability operates under the single legal institution constraint; it cannot submit joint Research Proposals with another institution or accept Research Award Notices that require shared Research Contracts, so every proposal and award is attributed to the institution alone.

### Operating Conditions
Research Funding Application must arrive before the funder deadline and with complete eligibility criteria; late or incomplete calls are rejected. Opportunity Register entry must carry a named academic lead and an identified funder; entries without both are returned. Research Strategy must be current and approved; an outdated Research Strategy blocks proposal initiation. Research Proposal must meet funder eligibility and include a Research Costing; proposals without an approved Research Costing are not submitted. Research Award Notice is accepted only when the funder terms match the submitted Research Proposal; a mismatch triggers escalation and renegotiation.

Name: Research Impact
Documentation:
### Identity
This is a management capability within the Research domain. It is responsible for collecting, validating and packaging Impact Evidence from Research Outputs and Research Publications into Impact Case Studies that meet external assessment requirements.

### Consumes
It consumes Research Output, which triggers the extraction of claims about economic, social or policy change. It consumes Research Publication, which arrives when a Publication Record is created and triggers citation and uptake tracking. It consumes Stakeholder Testimony, which arrives from external stakeholders and is logged for verification.

### Produces
It produces Impact Evidence when a claim is verified against a Research Output or Research Publication and assigned a source record. It produces Impact Case Study when Impact Evidence for a Research Project reaches the threshold and is packaged in the required template.

### Activities
Collecting Stakeholder Testimony is present. Extracting impact claims from Research Output is present. Extracting impact claims from Research Publication is present. Verifying Stakeholder Testimony against Research Output and Research Publication is present. Producing Impact Evidence is present. Producing Impact Case Study is present. Rejecting unverifiable Stakeholder Testimony is present. Reassessing Impact Evidence after external assessment feedback is present. Escalating Impact Case Study that misses the submission deadline is present.

### Fails when
This capability fails when Research Outputs and Research Publications exist but no Stakeholder Testimony can be verified into Impact Evidence, and Impact Case Studies cannot be produced. As a result, the institution has zero Impact Case Studies for the external assessment exercise and fails to demonstrate research impact.

### Constraint
The capability operates under the single legal institution constraint; it cannot attribute impact arising from collaborative research to another institution, and every Impact Case Study must be linked to the institution's own Research Outputs and Research Publications.

### Operating Conditions
Research Output must be deposited in the institutional repository with a persistent identifier and be publicly accessible where mandated; outputs without a repository record are returned. Research Publication must have a Publication Record and Open Access Compliance Record; publications without open access compliance are excluded from Impact Evidence. Stakeholder Testimony must name the Research Output or Research Publication and be attributable to a named individual; anonymous or unverifiable testimony is rejected. Impact Evidence must be accurate and current before inclusion in an Impact Case Study; evidence older than the assessment window is rejected.

Name: Research Improvement
Documentation:
### Identity
This is a management capability within the Research domain. It is responsible for analysing Research Funder Reports, Research Final Reports and Impact Case Studies to identify underperformance, and for producing Research Improvement Plans that change research practice and policy.

### Consumes
It consumes Research Funder Report, which arrives when Research Projects close and triggers analysis of spend, outputs and compliance. It consumes Research Final Report, which arrives from completed Research Projects and is reviewed for technical findings and deviations. It consumes Impact Case Study, which arrives after external assessment and is used to judge impact strength.

### Produces
It produces Research Improvement Plan when an analysis shows a deviation from Research Strategy or a funder requirement, and the plan specifies remedial actions and owners.

### Activities
Analysing Research Funder Report is present. Analysing Research Final Report is present. Comparing Impact Case Study against Research Strategy is present. Identifying deviations from funder requirements is present. Producing Research Improvement Plan is present. Rejecting Research Final Report that lacks complete data is present. Escalating recurring funder audit findings is present. Reassessing a Research Improvement Plan after implementation feedback is present.

### Fails when
This capability fails when Research Funder Reports, Research Final Reports and Impact Case Studies are all produced but no Research Improvement Plan is issued because analysis does not lead to corrective actions. As a result, repeated funder audit findings, compliance breaches and weak Impact Case Studies persist into the next academic year.

### Constraint
The capability operates under the single legal institution constraint; it cannot benchmark performance against other institutions or shared services, so every Research Improvement Plan must be scoped to the institution's own projects and outputs.

### Operating Conditions
Research Funder Report must include final spend, deliverable completion and compliance status; reports missing any of these are returned. Research Final Report must match the Research Contract milestones; mismatched reports are rejected. Impact Case Study must have passed external assessment review and include an Impact Evidence source; those without a source are not analysed. Research Improvement Plan must name a responsible owner and a review date; plans without either are not issued.

Name: Research Opportunity & Planning
Documentation:
### Identity
This is a management capability within the Research domain. It is responsible for scanning Government Policy and research performance to set the Research Strategy and maintain an Opportunity Register of funding and collaboration opportunities.

### Consumes
It consumes Government Policy, which arrives from external bodies and triggers review of research priorities, open access mandates and impact requirements. It consumes Research Improvement Plan, which arrives as a corrective output and triggers adjustment of the Research Strategy.

### Produces
It produces Research Strategy when Government Policy and Research Improvement Plans have been analysed and approved strategic priorities are set for the academic year. It produces Opportunity Register entry when a funding call or research theme aligns with the Research Strategy and a named academic lead is identified.

### Activities
Analysing Government Policy is present. Reviewing Research Improvement Plan is present. Setting Research Strategy is present. Identifying Opportunity Register entry is present. Prioritising Opportunity Register entry is present. Rejecting Government Policy that is out of scope is present. Reassessing Research Strategy after a funding council mandate is present. Escalating conflicts between Research Strategy and funder requirements is present.

### Fails when
This capability fails when Government Policy arrives but no Research Strategy is produced or updated, and no Opportunity Register entries are identified. As a result, Research Funding Applications are not assessed against current priorities, and the institution misses funding opportunities.

### Constraint
The capability operates under the single legal institution constraint; it cannot plan shared research opportunities or collaborative bids, and every Opportunity Register entry is assessed for institutional delivery alone.

### Operating Conditions
Government Policy must be the current official version and carry an effective date; superseded policy is rejected. Research Improvement Plan must have an approved owner and review date; plans without these are returned. Research Strategy must be approved before Opportunity Register entries are created; unapproved strategy blocks planning. Opportunity Register entry must include funder, deadline, scope and named academic lead; entries missing any field are not published.

Name: Research Publications
Documentation:
### Identity
This is an operational capability within the Research domain. It is responsible for depositing Research Outputs into the institutional repository, creating Publication Records, and ensuring every Research Publication meets open access mandates before release.

### Consumes
It consumes Research Output, which arrives when a Research Project produces a validated output and triggers deposit preparation. It consumes Data Management Plan, which arrives with the Research Output and specifies which data must accompany a publication. It consumes Government Policy, which arrives from opportunity and planning and defines open access requirements.

### Produces
It produces Open Access Deposit when a Research Output is deposited in the institutional repository with the required metadata. It produces Publication Record when an Open Access Deposit is validated and assigned a persistent identifier. It produces Research Publication when the Publication Record is complete and the version of record or accepted manuscript is made publicly accessible under the mandated licence. It produces Open Access Compliance Record when a Research Publication meets the funder and institutional mandates.

### Activities
Depositing Research Output is present. Validating Research Output metadata is present. Creating Open Access Deposit is present. Assigning Publication Record is present. Producing Research Publication is present. Producing Open Access Compliance Record is present. Escalating Research Output that is not deposited within the mandate period is present. Rejecting Research Output with missing Data Management Plan is present. Reassessing a Publication Record after a funder audit is present.

### Fails when
This capability fails when Research Outputs are produced but not deposited into the repository, and no Publication Records or Research Publications are issued. As a result, open access mandates are breached, Research Publications are not discoverable, and the institution's Research Output count for the academic year is zero.

### Constraint
The capability operates under the single legal institution constraint; it cannot deposit or publish Research Outputs held jointly with another institution, and every Research Publication must be attributed solely to the institution's repository.

### Operating Conditions
Research Output must arrive with a signed Data Management Plan and complete metadata including title, author list and funder identifiers; outputs missing these are returned. Data Management Plan must specify the open access version and embargo period; plans that conflict with funder mandates are returned for revision. Government Policy must be the current open access mandate; outdated mandates are not applied. Open Access Deposit must be made before the funder or institutional deadline; late deposits are accepted but flagged as non-compliant in the Open Access Compliance Record.

Name: Research Training
Documentation:
### Identity
This is an operational capability within the Research domain. It is responsible for developing research skills, supervising Research Degree Milestones, and maintaining Research Training Records for research students and research staff.

### Consumes
It consumes Research Student Application, which arrives from admissions and triggers enrolment into research degree programmes. It consumes Research Training Need, which arrives from supervisors and identifies required skills.

### Produces
It produces Research Training Record when a training activity is completed and assessed. It produces Supervisor Report when a research student reaches a progress review point. It produces Research Degree Milestone when a student passes a milestone such as confirmation or defence.

### Activities
Processing Research Student Application is present. Assessing Research Training Need is present. Delivering Research Training is present. Recording Research Training Record is present. Producing Supervisor Report is present. Producing Research Degree Milestone is present. Escalating Research Student Application that lacks supervisor capacity is present. Rejecting Research Training Need that is not linked to a research degree or project is present. Reassessing Research Degree Milestone after an examiner decision is present.

### Fails when
This capability fails when Research Student Applications are accepted but Research Training Needs cannot be met, and no Research Training Records or Supervisor Reports are produced. As a result, research students cannot progress through Research Degree Milestones, and the institution cannot award research degrees.

### Constraint
The capability operates under the single legal institution constraint; it cannot deliver joint research degrees or share Research Training Records with another institution, and every Supervisor Report and Research Degree Milestone is owned by the institution.

### Operating Conditions
Research Student Application must carry academic qualifications, supervisor agreement and funding source; applications missing any are returned. Research Training Need must be specific to a named research student and approved by a supervisor; unapproved or generic needs are rejected. Supervisor Report must be submitted before the progress review deadline; late reports are accepted but flagged as non-compliant. Research Training Record must be updated within five working days of a completed training activity; missing records block progression to the next Research Degree Milestone.

Name: Strategy Management
Documentation:
### Identity
This is a layer two capability within Strategy & Governance. It is accountable for setting the institution's long-term direction, translating external policy and funding changes into Strategic Objectives, and monitoring performance against those objectives each academic year.

### Consumes
It takes in Government Policy Documents when a regulator or funding body publishes a new requirement; each is assessed for impact on current Strategic Objectives. It takes in Key Performance Indicators covering Student Completion rates, Research Income per FTE, cost per Student Credit, and time from Research Grant application to award; these arrive at the end of each academic term. It takes in the previous Strategic Plan as a baseline when a refresh is mandated. It takes in Risk Register entries when a strategic risk is updated.

### Produces
It issues a Strategic Plan when the governing body approves it and it contains measurable Strategic Objectives for at least five academic years. It issues an Annual Budget when revenue and expenditure are reconciled to the Strategic Plan. It issues a Strategic Objective when a new external obligation requires a change in direction. It issues a Risk Appetite Statement when the governing body approves the level of risk the institution will accept. It issues an Environmental Sustainability Report when the Climate Change Act reporting period ends.

### Activities
Activities include formulating a Strategic Objective from a Government Policy Document, assessing a Key Performance Indicator against a target, allocating a Strategic Resource to a Strategic Objective, revising a Strategic Plan after a material change in funding, rejecting a Strategic Objective that lacks a measurable outcome, escalating a Key Performance Indicator that breaches an Office for Students condition, and reassessing a Strategic Objective after a Risk Register shows a new risk.

### Fails when
This capability fails when no current Strategic Plan has been approved for the upcoming academic year, because then the Annual Budget cannot be issued, Key Performance Indicators have no targets, and the institution cannot demonstrate compliance with Office for Students condition B3.

### Constraint
Strategic Objectives must be refreshed at least annually to incorporate changes in Office for Students conditions, open access mandates, and Climate Change Act reporting duties; a Strategic Plan older than one academic year is not valid.

### Operating Conditions
Incoming Government Policy Documents must include the issuing body, effective date, and the specific condition or mandate; if any is missing, the document is returned. Key Performance Indicators must cover the full academic year and be verified by the relevant data owner; unverified or partial-year indicators are rejected. The previous Strategic Plan must carry the governing body approval date; if not, it is accepted with a qualification and used only as an informal baseline. Produced Strategic Plan is judged by whether each Strategic Objective has a measurable target, a named owner, and a review date; any objective without all three is returned for revision. Annual Budget is judged by whether every line item traces to a Strategic Objective; unaligned items are returned. Strategic Objective is judged by whether it states the external obligation it addresses; if it does not, it is not issued.

Name: Student Administration
Documentation:
### Identity
This is an operating capability within the Teaching & Learning domain. It is accountable for maintaining the Student Record as the live, authoritative account of a learner's personal, enrolment and module status from first registration to award.

### Consumes
It consumes Student Data Changes when a learner updates personal details, such as name or address. It consumes Module Selection Forms when a learner chooses modules for a term. It consumes Interruption Requests when a learner asks to suspend study. It consumes Withdrawal Requests when a learner asks to leave the institution.

### Produces
It produces an Updated Student Record whenever a change is verified and applied. It produces Enrolment Confirmations to attest to current status for external bodies. It produces Module Selection Confirmations when a module selection is accepted.

### Activities
Activities present are: validate Student Data Changes, update Student Records, process Module Selection Forms, confirm enrolments, handle Interruption Requests, handle Withdrawal Requests, and recover a Student Record when a duplicate identifier is found.

### Fails when
It fails when the Student Record becomes outdated or duplicated, causing module selection to be assigned to the wrong learner or fee liabilities to be posted incorrectly. Enrolment Confirmations then stop, external bodies receive incorrect status, and graduation is blocked.

### Constraint
It is constrained by the need for one version-controlled Student Record per learner; all updates require evidence and a clear audit trail.

### Operating Conditions
A Student Data Change must carry the learner identifier and evidence of the change; if evidence is missing it is returned. A Module Selection Form must meet prerequisites and credit limits; if prerequisites are not met the selection is escalated for academic approval. An Interruption Request must state the suspension start date and reason; if the date is absent the request is returned.

Name: Student Admission Management
Documentation:
### Identity
This is an operating capability within the Teaching & Learning domain. It is accountable for deciding which applicants receive an offer and for ensuring every decision is derived from verified evidence and published entry criteria.

### Consumes
It consumes Student Applications when an applicant submits a completed application. It consumes Academic Transcripts when an applicant provides prior study outcomes. It consumes Fee Status Questionnaires when an applicant declares residence and funding basis. It consumes Reference Letters when a referee supports an application.

### Produces
It produces Admission Offers when an applicant meets the entry requirements and a place is available. It produces Rejection Notices when an applicant does not meet requirements or the course is full. It produces Conditional Offers when a place is offered subject to results.

### Activities
Activities present are: evaluate Student Applications against entry criteria, verify Academic Transcripts, calculate Fee Status from a Fee Status Questionnaire, issue Admission Offers, issue Rejection Notices, issue Conditional Offers, and reconsider a decision after an applicant appeals.

### Fails when
It fails when Student Applications are not assigned to decision-makers or when entry criteria are not applied consistently. Admission Offers then stop, applicants have no route to enrolment, and Student Enrolment numbers fall.

### Constraint
It is constrained by published entry criteria and by the equal treatment duties under the Office for Students; every decision must be explainable from the evidence.

### Operating Conditions
A Student Application must contain the applicant's identifier, course code and qualification history; if the course code is missing the application is returned. An Academic Transcript must be issued by the awarding body; if the body is unaccredited the transcript is rejected. A Fee Status Questionnaire must be signed and dated; if the date is absent it is returned.

Name: Student Assessment
Documentation:
### Identity
This is an operating capability within the Teaching & Learning domain. It is accountable for collecting, marking, moderating and recording the results that prove a learner has met the learning outcomes of a module.

### Consumes
It consumes Assessment Submissions when a learner submits coursework or sits an examination. It consumes Marking Rubrics when an assessor applies a standard to a submission. It consumes Extension Requests when a learner claims circumstances preventing timely submission. It consumes Mitigating Circumstances Claims when a learner asks for a result to be set aside.

### Produces
It produces Assessment Results as recorded marks for each module or component. It produces Assessment Board Papers as the set of provisional results needing board approval. It produces Resit Notices when a learner fails a component and is eligible to retake it.

### Activities
Activities present are: collect Assessment Submissions, apply Marking Rubrics, moderate a sample of marks, record Assessment Results, handle Extension Requests, investigate Mitigating Circumstances Claims, and issue Resit Notices.

### Fails when
It fails when Assessment Submissions are lost or when marks are not recorded in the Student Record by the board deadline. Assessment Board Papers are then incomplete, resits cannot be issued, and Student Completion stalls.

### Constraint
It is constrained by the academic integrity rules requiring anonymous marking where prescribed and by the external examiner role in confirming standards.

### Operating Conditions
An Assessment Submission must carry the module code and an anonymous candidate number; if the module code is missing it is returned. An Extension Request must state the affected assessment and evidence of the ground; if evidence is absent it is rejected. A Mitigating Circumstances Claim must be submitted within the published deadline; if late it is accepted only with a validated reason.

Name: Student Attraction & Recruitment
Documentation:
### Identity
This is an operating capability within the Teaching & Learning domain. It is accountable for generating prospective learner interest and converting that interest into eligible Student Applications.

### Consumes
It consumes Prospect Records when a prospective learner enquires or attends an event. It consumes Campaign Briefs when a marketing campaign is commissioned. It consumes Open Day Bookings when a prospect registers to visit. It consumes Market Research Reports when sector data is purchased or assembled.

### Produces
It produces Prospectuses as published course and fee information for prospective learners. It produces Student Applications when a prospect completes the application process. It produces Open Day Registers as proof of attendance and follow-up lists.

### Activities
Activities present are: maintain Prospect Records, run Campaigns from Campaign Briefs, host Open Day Bookings, convert enquiries into Student Applications, record Open Day Registers, and withdraw a Prospect Record when consent expires.

### Fails when
It fails when Prospect Records have no valid consent or when campaigns reach no eligible prospects. Student Applications then stop arriving, and the institution cannot fill its Student Enrolment places.

### Constraint
It is constrained by the need to balance promotional activity with fair access and by the UK GDPR requirement for consent before direct marketing.

### Operating Conditions
A Prospect Record must carry a source and a lawful basis for contact; if the lawful basis is absent the record is deleted. A Campaign Brief must state target audience, message and budget; if the budget is absent the campaign is halted for approval. An Open Day Booking must include an attendee identifier and contact detail; if the identifier is missing the booking is returned.

Name: Student Completion & Graduation
Documentation:
### Identity
This is an operating capability within the Teaching & Learning domain. It is accountable for confirming that each learner has completed all requirements and for producing the formal award and graduate evidence.

### Consumes
It consumes Completion Checks when programme requirements are compared against the Student Record. It consumes Award Classification Decisions when an Assessment Board confirms or recomputes the final class or merit. It consumes Fee Clearance Statements when all tuition and other charges are settled.

### Produces
It produces Awarded Degree Certificates when the learner is confirmed as complete and the award is conferred. It produces Graduate Records when the graduate's final details are validated for external transmission. It produces Transcripts of Results when a graduate requests a full academic statement.

### Activities
Activities present are: run Completion Checks, apply Award Classification Decisions, verify Fee Clearance Statements, print Awarded Degree Certificates, produce Graduate Records, produce Transcripts of Results, and suspend award when a Completion Check fails.

### Fails when
It fails when Completion Checks cannot reconcile the Student Record with the programme requirements or when Fee Clearance Statements are outstanding. Awarded Degree Certificates and Graduate Records then stop, so former learners cannot prove their award.

### Constraint
It is constrained by the requirement that awards are conferred only by the Assessment Board and only after fee clearance is confirmed, under the institution's formal award regulations.

### Operating Conditions
A Completion Check must list every module and credit against the Student Record; if a module is missing the check is returned. An Award Classification Decision must be signed by the Assessment Board Chair; if unsigned it is rejected. A Fee Clearance Statement must match the student's fee ledger; if the ledger shows a balance the award is suspended.

Name: Student Enrolment
Documentation:
### Identity
This is an operating capability within the Teaching & Learning domain. It is accountable for converting a valid Admission Offer into a live Student Enrolment, complete with identity, programme and fee status.

### Consumes
It consumes Admission Offers when an applicant has accepted an unconditional or conditional place. It consumes Identity Documents when a learner proves their legal identity. It consumes Student Fee payments when the first fee installment or deposit is paid. It consumes Visa Evidence when an international learner must prove study permission.

### Produces
It produces Student Enrolments as the event that activates the learner's Student Record for the academic year. It produces Student ID Cards as proof of enrolment. It produces Enrolment Declarations as a signed statement of enrolment terms.

### Activities
Activities present are: verify Admission Offers, check Identity Documents, record Student Fee payments, check Visa Evidence, create Student Enrolments, issue Student ID Cards, and refuse enrolment when a conditional offer has unmet conditions.

### Fails when
It fails when an Admission Offer cannot be verified against the Student Application or when fee payment is missing. Student Enrolments then do not activate, Student ID Cards are not issued, and the learner cannot access teaching or assessment.

### Constraint
It is constrained by the legal requirement to verify identity and study permission before enrolment and by the financial rule that no learner becomes enrolled without an accepted offer.

### Operating Conditions
An Admission Offer must be unconditional or have all conditions cleared; if conditions remain the offer is not processed for enrolment. An Identity Document must carry a photograph and official identifier; if it is not a recognised identity document it is rejected. A Student Fee payment must be matched to the learner's fee account; if the amount differs the payment is held for reconciliation.

Name: Student Support & Wellbeing Management
Documentation:
### Identity
This is an operating capability within the Teaching & Learning domain. It is accountable for receiving concerns about learner wellbeing and for organising the support, adjustments and referrals that keep a learner able to continue study.

### Consumes
It consumes Support Referrals when a tutor, medical service or self-referral identifies a learner in need. It consumes Wellbeing Concerns when a learner reports mental health or personal crisis. It consumes Reasonable Adjustment Requests when a disability or condition requires a study adjustment. It consumes Mitigating Circumstances Claims when a learner asks for assessment allowance.

### Produces
It produces Support Plans when a learner's ongoing needs are assessed and agreed. It produces Counselling Appointments when a learner is assigned to a practitioner. It produces Reasonable Adjustment Agreements when an adjustment is approved and communicated to teaching and assessment staff.

### Activities
Activities present are: triage Support Referrals, assess Wellbeing Concerns, create Support Plans, schedule Counselling Appointments, review Reasonable Adjustment Requests, record Mitigating Circumstances Claims, escalate a safeguarding case, and close a Support Plan when no longer needed.

### Fails when
It fails when Support Referrals are not triaged within the required response time or when safeguarding cases are not escalated. Learner needs then go untreated, Reasonable Adjustment Agreements are delayed, and Student Completion falls because learners stop engaging.

### Constraint
It is constrained by confidentiality and safeguarding duties, which require separating wellbeing records from the academic Student Record while still making approved adjustments actionable.

### Operating Conditions
A Support Referral must state the learner identifier, the concern and the urgency; if the urgency is absent it is returned to the referrer. A Wellbeing Concern judged as high risk must be escalated immediately; if not escalated the case is absorbed as a defect the service must correct. A Reasonable Adjustment Request must include evidence of the condition; if evidence is missing the request is returned.

Name: Supporting Services
Documentation:
### Identity
Layer: enabling; parent domain: Enabling Capabilities. This capability holds accountability for non-academic student support, including wellbeing, disability, counselling, careers, and financial advice. It is answerable for early intervention, reasonable adjustments, and safeguarding.

### Consumes
It takes in Student Support Request, triggered by a student seeking help. It takes in Disability Disclosure, triggered by a student declaring a disability. It takes in Counselling Referral, triggered by a student or staff member concerned about a student. It takes in Careers Enquiry, triggered by a student requesting careers guidance. It takes in Bursary Application, triggered by a student applying for financial support. It takes in Incident Referral, triggered by a safeguarding or conduct concern.

### Produces
It issues Support Plan when a student's needs are assessed. It issues Reasonable Adjustment when a disability is evidenced and agreed. It issues Counselling Appointment when a referral is triaged and matched. It issues Careers Advice Record when guidance is delivered. It issues Bursary Decision when an application is assessed against criteria. It issues Incident Report when a safeguarding concern is investigated.

### Activities
Triages Student Support Request by urgency and risk. Assesses Disability Disclosure and arranges Reasonable Adjustment. Arranges Counselling Appointment and manages waiting list. Provides Careers Advice and records Careers Advice Record. Assesses Bursary Application against funding criteria and budget. Manages Incident Referral and escalates to safeguarding lead. Creates Support Plan and reviews progress. Monitors student wellbeing through attendance and engagement. Refers to external agencies where specialist help is needed. Handles crisis and emergency intervention.

### Fails when
It stops delivering when Student Support Request is not triaged promptly, causing student harm, withdrawal, or a missed opportunity for intervention; or when Incident Referral is not acted on, causing safeguarding failure.

### Constraint
It operates under a duty of care, confidentiality, and multi-agency safeguarding requirements, where information sharing must balance privacy against risk of harm.

### Operating Conditions
Student Support Request must include student identifier and nature of issue; if missing, it is returned or immediate outreach is attempted. Disability Disclosure must be voluntary and include consent; if unclear, it is accepted and followed up. Counselling Referral must be from a registered source and include risk level; if missing, it is escalated as urgent. Bursary Application must include financial evidence and course details; if incomplete, it is returned. Incident Referral must include date, persons involved, and factual account; if missing, it is returned for immediate clarification. Careers Enquiry must include student identifier and query; if incomplete, it is returned.

Name: Teaching & Learning Delivery
Documentation:
### Identity
This is an operating capability within the Teaching & Learning domain. It is accountable for the scheduled delivery of teaching sessions and for producing the attendance and delivery records that confirm a learner has engaged with the curriculum.

### Consumes
It consumes Course Timetables when the academic timetable is finalised each term. It consumes Module Materials when a teaching session requires prepared content. It consumes Room Bookings when a session is allocated a physical or virtual space. It consumes Student Enrolments to know which learners are expected.

### Produces
It produces Learning Session Records when a session is delivered, listing the topic, time, staff and room. It produces Attendance Records when learner presence is captured. It produces Timetable Clash Notices when a scheduled session cannot run in the allocated room or time.

### Activities
Activities present are: schedule teaching sessions from Course Timetables, deliver teaching sessions using Module Materials, record Attendance Records, resolve Timetable Clash Notices, reschedule a session when a room is unavailable, and cancel a session when no staff member is available.

### Fails when
It fails when Course Timetables contain unresolved clashes or when Room Bookings are not confirmed. Learning Session Records then stop being produced, Attendance Records are missing, and learners cannot satisfy engagement requirements.

### Constraint
It is constrained by the academic calendar and staff contracts, which fix the number of teaching weeks and the timing within which all sessions must be delivered.

### Operating Conditions
A Course Timetable must include session date, module code, room and assigned staff; if the module code is absent the timetable is returned. A Room Booking must be confirmed by the room owner; if unconfirmed the session is treated as provisional and may be cancelled. Module Materials must match the module code and session topic; if they do not match they are returned to the originator before delivery.

Name: Commercial Activity
Documentation:
### Identity
The Commercial Activity domain is accountable for the institution's commercial arrangements with suppliers and external clients. It is responsible for ensuring every Commercial Contract is lawfully sourced, executed, delivered and monitored, and that the institution receives the goods, services and income it has contracted for. A person running this domain is answerable for the financial outcome of each Commercial Contract, for authorising payment against each Supplier Invoice only after verification, and for issuing Contract Agreements and Financial Statements that evidence the institution's commercial position. No financial commitment is made without an approved Commercial Contract, and every commercial transaction is captured in the institution's financial records.

### Consumes
When a Supplier Invoice arrives, the domain records it, matches it to the governing Commercial Contract and delivery acceptance, and schedules payment only after verification. When a Service Request arrives from an internal unit or external client, the domain qualifies it against existing Commercial Contracts and either converts it into a proposal or assigns it for fulfilment. When a Government Policy document arrives, the domain extracts procurement, data protection and sustainability obligations and updates contract terms and monitoring criteria. When a Contract Agreement arrives, the domain registers it for delivery and monitoring and stores the signed counterpart.

### Produces
The domain issues a Contract Agreement when both the institution and the counterparty have signed and all institutional approvals are recorded. It issues a Financial Statement after every commercial transaction in the period has been reconciled to its Contract Agreement and bank records. It issues a Regulatory Return when aggregated commercial activity reaches a statutory reporting threshold. It issues a Contract Performance Report at the close of each reporting period, recording key performance indicators, spend, and delivery status.

### Fails when
The domain stops delivering when no Commercial Contract can progress to signed status because supplier due diligence, affordability approval or legal review remains incomplete. Downstream, no Contract Agreement is issued, no Supplier Invoice is authorised for payment, fulfilment cannot legally begin, and the Financial Statements for the period cannot be closed without unresolved contract commitments. This failure also prevents the production of statutory returns and final accounts.

### Constraint
Every financial commitment and payment in this domain must be traceable to an approved Commercial Contract and its documented delivery acceptance; this single traceability condition separates commercial activity from activity funded by other means.

Name: Enabling Capabilities
Documentation:
### Identity
This domain holds accountability for the institution's internal operating integrity. It is answerable for the condition of the built estate, the accuracy of financial control, the legality of contracts, the availability of information systems, the management of people, and the provision of student support services. The person running this domain is accountable for ensuring that Supplier Invoices are paid correctly, Facilities Work Orders are completed on time, Employment Contracts meet legal terms, and Service Requests reach closure.

### Consumes
It takes in Supplier Invoices and validates them against procurement commitments before payment. It takes in Government Policy documents and assesses impact on statutory obligations. It takes in Student Fee payments and reconciles each against the Student Account. It takes in Service Requests from staff, students and external parties and assigns resolution ownership. It takes in Facilities Work Orders and schedules maintenance against building risk. It takes in Employment Applications and runs selection under recruitment policy. It takes in Procurement Requests and sources suppliers under financial limits.

### Produces
It issues Financial Statements when statutory reporting deadlines arrive and the general ledger is closed. It issues Employment Contracts when a candidate is selected and right-to-work checks pass. It issues Maintenance Schedules when a Building Condition Survey identifies required work. It issues Service Reports when a Service Request reaches closure. It issues Contract Agreements when procurement or partnership terms receive legal approval. It issues Library Loans when borrower entitlement is confirmed.

### Fails when
It fails when Financial Transactions cannot be processed because Supplier Invoice or Student Fee payment data lacks a valid account code, causing payments to stall and suppliers to withdraw service. It fails when Facilities Work Orders cannot be scheduled because building condition data is not current, causing estates to deteriorate and compliance notices to be issued. It fails when Legal Queries cannot be resolved because regulatory interpretation is unresolved, causing institutional decisions to halt.

### Constraint
The single condition that most distinguishes this domain is that it operates under simultaneous statutory reporting cycles, collective bargaining agreements, and physical infrastructure dependencies, so no internal service may optimise independently without degrading another internal service or an external compliance obligation.

Name: Research
Documentation:
### Identity
The Research domain is answerable for the institution's creation and dissemination of Research Outputs and Research Publications, the acquisition and administration of research funding, and the evidence of research impact. It is accountable for increasing Research Income per full-time equivalent academic staff member, reducing the time from Research Grant application to award, and ensuring that every Research Publication meets open access mandates. The domain must ensure Research Contracts are executed and delivered, Research Data is managed under a Data Management Plan, and Impact Case Studies are produced for external assessment.

### Consumes
The domain receives Research Funding Application from funders; on arrival, each is logged and assessed for eligibility, funding conditions, and alignment with the Research Strategy. It receives Government Policy documents; on arrival, these are interpreted into research compliance requirements, open access mandates, and impact evidence thresholds. It receives Research Data from research activities; on arrival, the data is checked for completeness and stored under an active Data Management Plan.

### Produces
The domain issues Research Publication when the corresponding Research Output has been deposited in the institutional repository and an Open Access Compliance Record has been created. It issues Research Output when a Research Project has produced a Research Final Report and the output has passed validation. It issues Impact Case Study when Impact Evidence reaches the threshold required by the external assessment framework. It issues Research Funder Report when a Research Contract completes and all financial and technical reporting requirements have been met.

### Fails when
The domain fails when no Research Funding Application results in a Research Award Notice before current Research Projects end, and no new Research Outputs are deposited. As a result, Financial Statements cannot report Research Income, the institution breaches open access mandates for Research Publications, and Impact Case Studies cannot be compiled for the external assessment exercise. Downstream, the institutional research performance measures collapse to zero Research Income per academic staff member and zero Research Outputs for the academic year.

### Constraint
The domain operates as if all research activity is contained within a single legal institution; it does not capture Research Contracts or Research Outputs arising from multi-institution collaborations, shared facilities, or jointly owned research assets. Every Research Funding Application, Research Contract and Research Publication is attributed to the one institution and cannot be split across partners.

Name: Strategy & Governance
Documentation:
### Identity
The Strategy & Governance domain is answerable for the institution's lawful operation, strategic direction, and public accountability. Its accountable executive must ensure that the institution meets the Office for Students condition B3 on student outcomes, discharges UK GDPR data protection duties, complies with open access mandates for research publications, and reports sustainability under the Climate Change Act. Failure in this domain means the institution loses the right to award degrees, receive public funding, or enter into legally binding contracts.

### Consumes
It takes in Government Policy Documents as they are published by regulators or Parliament and records each as a Compliance Obligation with an owner and due date. It takes in Key Performance Indicators covering Student Enrolments, Research Outputs, Commercial Contracts executed, and Service Requests resolved; each is compared against targets for the academic year. It takes in Audit Findings from internal and external assurance work and logs each as a corrective action. It takes in Risk Register updates from operations and maps each risk to a Strategic Objective.

### Produces
It issues a Strategic Plan when it has been approved by the governing body and includes measurable objectives for the next five academic years. It issues an Annual Budget when revenue and expenditure have been reconciled to the Strategic Plan. It issues Governance Decisions when a committee has a recorded quorum and a majority vote. It issues Statutory Filings when the relevant regulator's deadline falls due. It issues Policy Statements when a policy has been through equality impact assessment and governing body approval.

### Fails when
The domain fails when the governing body cannot form a quorum for two consecutive meetings, because no Governance Decision, Strategic Plan, or Annual Budget can be issued. As a result, statutory returns are not filed, the Office for Students can impose sanctions, and downstream operational planning has no approved budget or objectives.

### Constraint
The domain operates only for a single legal institution; it does not extend authority over shared services, franchise partners, or collaborative course delivery arrangements, so any governance object for those activities falls outside its remit.

Name: Teaching & Learning
Documentation:
### Identity
This domain is accountable for the student lifecycle from first contact through graduation and alumni engagement. It holds responsibility for enrolling students, delivering courses, assessing learning, conferring awards, and keeping the Student Record current as the authoritative record of academic progress. The accountable outcome is successful student completion evidenced by Awarded Degree Certificates and accurate Graduate Records.

### Consumes
It consumes Student Applications and assesses each against entry requirements, fee status and available places before an enrolment decision is made. It consumes Student Fee payments and posts each to a student account linked to the corresponding enrolment. It consumes Government Policy documents and translates each into institutional admission, teaching, assessment and award rules.

### Produces
It issues Awarded Degree Certificates when a student meets all programme requirements and the Assessment Board confirms the final award. It issues Graduate Records when an award is conferred, carrying final classification, credits and personal identifiers to confirm the graduate to external parties.

### Fails when
It fails when Student Applications cannot be converted into Student Enrolments because entry requirements or fee status remain unresolved, or when assessment results cannot be verified against the Student Record. Awarded Degree Certificates and Graduate Records then stop, and Student Completion rates fall against the academic year.

### Constraint
The single condition that most distinguishes this domain is its obligation to maintain one authoritative Student Record for each learner, updated only through formally approved academic decisions and subject to UK GDPR and OfS condition B3.

Name: Locations
Documentation: **The places where the institution operates.** This grouping brings together Campus, Off-Campus, and Online to describe where activities and services take place. It is used to record the physical or virtual settings for teaching, research, and support. Planners and administrators rely on this classification to allocate resources, manage access, and understand the distribution of operations across different environments. The grouping ensures consistent terminology for location-based reporting.

Name: Market Segments
Documentation: **Student populations split by origin.** This grouping brings together the distinct student populations the institution targets for recruitment and planning: Domestic & EU Students and International Students. The model uses these segments to separate demand, fees, funding, and support requirements because each group has different expectations, regulations, and revenue implications. Admissions, marketing, and academic planning teams rely on this distinction to forecast numbers, allocate resources, and design appropriate services. Both segments are business actors whose choices and needs drive institutional strategy. The grouping ensures that strategic planning accounts for the distinct characteristics of each student cohort.

Name: Products
Documentation: **The institution's educational and research offerings.** This group gathers the qualifications, programmes, publications, custom training, and intellectual property that the institution provides to learners, researchers, and external partners. It supports decisions about portfolio balance, resource allocation, and strategic direction. Members include Short Courses, HNC & HND, Batchelor Degree, Graduate Certificate, Masters Diploma, Graduate Diploma, Doctor of Philosophy, Research Publications, Tailored Learning & Teaching Products, and Intellectual Property Rights. The model uses this grouping to view the full range of what the institution offers and to manage them consistently.

Name: Consumers
Documentation: **The set of external parties who engage with the institution.** The model gathers Prospective Students, UG Students, PG Students, Public Community, Funding Bodies, Commercial Partners, and External Researchers because each consumes services, resources, or relationships offered by the organisation. Grouping these members supports planning for engagement, satisfaction, external impact, and the alignment of institutional activity with stakeholder expectations.

Name: Stakeholders
Documentation: **A group of parties with an interest.** This grouping gathers the individuals, organisations and public bodies that have a stake in the institution's activities and outcomes. Members include National Goverment, Local Goverment, Staff, Students, Sponsors, Governors, Professional Bodies & Reg Authorities, Suppliers, Accreditation Bodies and Local Community. The model uses this group to identify whose needs, expectations and obligations shape decisions about services, priorities and resources. Each member brings a distinct perspective: students seek education, staff seek employment and development, government bodies set policy and funding conditions, suppliers deliver goods, and accreditation bodies confirm standards.

Name: Campus
Documentation: **A physical site of the institution.** Campus is the main ground or set of buildings where the institution delivers its core activities. It houses teaching rooms, libraries, laboratories, offices, and student facilities. Staff and students use the campus for face-to-face learning, research, and administration. The model records campus locations to support timetabling, maintenance, security, and space planning. Decisions about building access, room allocation, and service placement depend on knowing which activities occur on campus.

Name: Off-Campus
Documentation: **A location away from the main campus.** Off-campus refers to any physical site that is not the institution's central campus but is used for its activities. This includes partner premises, fieldwork sites, placement locations, and outreach centres. The institution uses off-campus locations to deliver work-based learning, community engagement, and collaborative research. Recording these locations supports travel planning, risk assessment, and partnership management. It also helps the institution meet its obligations for students and staff who operate outside the main site.

Name: Online
Documentation: **A virtual space for learning and work.** Online is the digital setting where the institution delivers teaching, support, and administrative services over the internet. It includes learning platforms, video conferencing, and digital resources. Students and staff access online services from any location with an internet connection. The model records online as a location to distinguish remote delivery from physical presence. This distinction supports decisions about digital infrastructure, accessibility, and the balance between on-campus and remote operations.

Name: Short Courses
Documentation: **A short, focused learning programme.** The institution offers Short Courses to individuals seeking targeted knowledge or skills without enrolling in a full degree. These courses are delivered through condensed teaching and assessment for professional development, upskilling, or personal interest. In the model, they are used to plan flexible offerings, manage enrolments, and track completion. The institution designs and runs them to respond quickly to demand from learners and employers.

Name: HNC & HND
Documentation: **Vocational higher education qualifications.** The institution offers HNC & HND to students who want practical, work-related learning in a specific field. The institution delivers them through taught modules, projects, and assessments that align with industry needs. These qualifications prepare students for employment or progression to further study. In the model, they support the management of vocational pathways, employer engagement, and progression routes. The institution uses them to broaden access to higher education.

Name: Batchelor Degree
Documentation: **An undergraduate academic award.** The institution offers the Batchelor Degree to students who have completed secondary education and wish to gain in-depth knowledge in a chosen subject. Delivery involves structured teaching, assessment, and student support over an extended period. Graduates receive a recognised qualification for employment or further study. In the model, this product is used to plan curriculum, allocate academic staff, and monitor student progression and outcomes.

Name: Graduate Certificate
Documentation: **A postgraduate short qualification.** Offered to graduates who want to specialise or update their skills in a specific area. The institution delivers it through a focused set of advanced-level modules. It requires less study than a full master's degree but carries academic credit. In the model, it is used to manage postgraduate short offerings, track enrolments, and support continuing professional development. The institution issues the certificate upon successful completion.

Name: Masters Diploma
Documentation: **A postgraduate taught qualification.** Offered to graduates seeking advanced knowledge and professional skills in a specific field. The institution delivers it through a structured programme of taught modules and assessment. It requires less study than a full master's degree but more than a graduate diploma. In the model, it is used to manage postgraduate taught provision, allocate teaching resources, and track student progression and completion.

Name: Graduate Diploma
Documentation: **A postgraduate conversion or specialisation qualification.** Offered to graduates who need to develop knowledge in a new field or deepen existing expertise. The institution delivers it through a structured set of advanced modules that include applied work. It carries more credit than a graduate certificate and provides a pathway to further study. In the model, it is used to manage postgraduate pathways, track student load, and plan teaching resources. The institution awards it upon completion.

Name: Doctor of Philosophy
Documentation: **A research-based doctoral degree.** Offered to students who undertake original research under academic supervision. Delivery involves independent study, supervisory guidance, and examination of a thesis or equivalent output. It represents the highest level of academic achievement. The institution uses this product to manage doctoral candidates, allocate research supervision, and track completions and research outputs. It supports the institution's research mission and academic reputation.

Name: Research Publications
Documentation: **Scholarly works produced by the institution.** These are outputs of research activity, such as articles, books, conference papers, and other scholarly contributions. The institution's researchers create them, and the wider academic community and public use them to share knowledge. In the model, Research Publications are tracked to assess research performance, support reporting, and inform future research strategy. They also contribute to the institution's impact and standing.

Name: Tailored Learning & Teaching Products
Documentation: **Customised educational offerings.** These are programmes or learning materials developed to meet the specific needs of a client group, such as employers, industry bodies, or partner organisations. The institution uses its academic expertise and teaching resources to design and deliver them. In the model, they are used to manage bespoke contracts, commercial education, and workforce development. The institution relies on them to generate income and strengthen external partnerships.

Name: Intellectual Property Rights
Documentation: **Legal rights over creations of the mind.** These include patents, copyrights, trademarks, and other protections arising from research, teaching materials, and institutional branding. The institution owns or licenses these rights to control use and derive value. In the model, Intellectual Property Rights are managed as assets, supporting commercialisation, technology transfer, and protection of academic work. They help the institution capture the benefits of its innovation and scholarship.

Name: National Goverment
Documentation: **The central government that sets policy.** National Goverment is the central public authority that shapes higher education policy, funding and regulation for the institution. It expects the institution to deliver accessible, high-quality education, manage public money properly and contribute to national skills and research goals. Its view matters because the institution must respond to national policy changes, funding conditions and reporting requirements. In this model, decisions about strategic direction, curriculum offer and resource use take account of National Goverment expectations, as they affect funding, reputation and compliance.

Name: Local Goverment
Documentation: **A municipal authority with local oversight.** Local Goverment is the elected body responsible for services and regulation in the area where the institution sits. It expects the institution to follow local planning, licensing and environmental rules and to work with it on regional skills, transport and economic development. Its view matters because the institution needs approvals for building projects, events and other activities that affect the locality. In this model, input from Local Goverment shapes decisions about estate development, community engagement and collaborative initiatives that align with local priorities.

Name: Staff
Documentation: **Employees who deliver the institution's work.** Staff are the people employed by the institution to teach, research, support students and run its services. They expect fair pay and conditions, opportunities for development, a safe working environment and a voice in decisions that affect their work. Their view matters because they deliver the institution's core activities and understand operational realities. In this model, decisions about service design, technology, workload and organisational change take account of staff perspectives to maintain capability, engagement and quality of delivery.

Name: Students
Documentation: **Learners enrolled on the institution's courses.** Students are the individuals enrolled to study at the institution. They expect high-quality teaching, access to learning resources, support services and clear information about their programmes and progress. Their view matters because they are the primary beneficiaries of the institution's educational offer and their success defines institutional performance. In this model, decisions about curriculum design, timetabling, student support and the digital environment are informed by student needs, feedback and outcomes, ensuring that services remain focused on learning and student experience.

Name: Sponsors
Documentation: **Funders who support specific work.** Sponsors are individuals, companies, trusts or public funders that provide money or resources for specific institutional activities such as research, scholarships or events. They expect the institution to deliver agreed outcomes, use funds as intended and acknowledge their support. Their view matters because sponsored work depends on their continued backing and must meet their conditions. In this model, decisions about which projects to pursue, how to resource them and how to report progress take account of sponsor expectations, safeguarding funding and reputation.

Name: Governors
Documentation: **The governing body overseeing the institution.** Governors are the senior volunteers or appointed members who hold ultimate responsibility for the institution's strategic direction, financial health and legal compliance. They expect management to deliver the institution's mission while managing risk and using resources properly. Their view matters because they approve major plans, budgets and policies, and hold senior leaders to account. In this model, decisions about significant change, investment or partnership require consideration of governors' expectations and their duty to protect the institution's long-term interests.

Name: Professional Bodies & Reg Authorities
Documentation: **Bodies that set professional standards.** Professional Bodies & Reg Authorities are organisations that define standards for particular occupations or regulate entry to a profession. They expect the institution's courses to equip students with the knowledge, skills and ethical understanding required for professional practice. Their view matters because recognition by these bodies enables graduates to enter certain careers and confirms the quality of professional programmes. In this model, decisions about curriculum content, work placements and assessment are shaped by the expectations of these bodies, ensuring the institution's offer remains relevant and credible.

Name: Suppliers
Documentation: **External providers of goods and services.** Suppliers are external companies and organisations that provide goods and services to the institution, such as equipment, software, estate services or consultancy. They expect fair procurement processes, clear contracts and prompt payment. Their view matters because the institution depends on them for important operations and projects, and their performance affects cost, quality and risk. In this model, decisions about outsourcing, procurement and supplier management take account of supplier capabilities and relationships, ensuring the institution secures value and maintains continuity.

Name: Accreditation Bodies
Documentation: **Independent bodies that assess quality.** Accreditation Bodies are external organisations that evaluate the institution's courses, services or operations against recognised standards. They expect the institution to demonstrate compliance, maintain quality and provide evidence of continuous improvement. Their approval or accreditation affects the institution's ability to offer certain qualifications, receive funding or maintain reputation. In this model, their view matters because decisions about curriculum, quality assurance and resource allocation must satisfy the requirements these bodies set. Institutional leaders rely on accreditation outcomes to validate programmes and to identify areas needing attention.

Name: Local Community
Documentation: **People and organisations near the campus.** Local Community includes residents, community groups and local businesses in the areas where the institution operates. They expect the institution to contribute positively to the local economy, offer cultural or educational opportunities and manage its physical footprint responsibly. Their view matters because the institution's plans for buildings, transport, events and partnerships affect the community. In this model, understanding local community interests supports decisions about campus development, public engagement and community relations, helping the institution maintain its social licence to operate.
